title: The Path of the First Breath
summary: Path 11 joins Chokmah, Wisdom, to Kether, the Crown. It belongs to Aleph, the Ox, to elemental Air and to Atu 0, The Fool, and the Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Scintillating Intelligence. Working it builds openness, the willingness to begin without guarantees, and a lightness of spirit that is free rather than careless.

prepare.incense: Galbanum (777 col. XLII perfume of path 11). Add a touch of musk, Chokmah's perfume, for the lower temple if you have it.
prepare.candle: Bright pale yellow candle (King scale of Aleph) on a grey cloth (Queen scale of Chokmah). A sky-blue cloth (Queen scale of the path) is an alternative.
prepare.stone: Topaz (777 col. XL)
prepare.facing: East, the quarter of Air
prepare.notes: Banish first, with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or Liber XXV (the Star Ruby). A dagger or a fan, the weapons of Air, can lie on the altar. A window opened a little lets real moving air into the room. The working relies on the breath, so keep the fourfold holds gentle and shorten them if you feel light-headed. Keep your diary and a pen within reach and set aside about 25 undisturbed minutes. This is a supernal path, above the Abyss. Many teachers advise knowing the lower paths well before working it, and treating what you see as symbolic contemplation rather than attainment.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright with your hands resting open on your thighs, and let your eyes close. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. On this path the breath is part of the teaching, so give it particular care. Feel the cool air coming in through the nostrils and the warmth of it leaving. Let the ribs widen and settle. If a hold becomes uncomfortable, shorten the count; nothing here should strain. With each outbreath, let go a little more: the face, the throat, the shoulders, the hands, the chest and belly, the legs and feet. When the body is loose and quiet and the breath flows easily, let your attention rest lightly at the centre of your chest, ready to build the first image.

steps.title: The Temple of Chokmah
steps.text: A temple forms around you. Its walls and floor are a soft, glowing grey, the Queen-scale colour of Chokmah, like pearl or high cloud lit from within. There is no roof. Above you a dark sky is crowded with the fixed stars, and the twelve signs of the zodiac wheel slowly across it. At the centre rises a single tall pillar of grey stone, with a small altar before it, and the air is warm with musk. Wheels of light turn at the edges of your vision: the Auphanim, the choir of this sphere. Stand before the pillar, breathe in, and vibrate the name Yah, letting the short syllable carry up to the stars. Then call Ratziel, archangel of Chokmah, herald of hidden wisdom. Sense a presence of great force and clarity, and ask for guidance and protection on the path.

steps.title: The Veil of the Fool
steps.text: In the east of the temple hangs a veil painted with Atu 0, The Fool: a horned, green-clad figure poised as if in the moment of a leap. Grapes lie at his feet, a tiger is at his leg and a crocodile waits in the water below, and around him are spirals of colour, a dove, a vulture and a butterfly. Stand before it. With your right forefinger, trace the letter Aleph, א, in bright pale yellow light, the King-scale colour of this path: first the long diagonal from upper left to lower right, then the arm at the upper right and the leg at the lower left. Let it hang shining in the air. Vibrate its name, Aleph. The veil stirs as though a wind has risen behind it. Step through the letter and the image, and let them close behind you.

steps.title: The Open Sky
steps.text: There is no road. You are in open sky, clear and bright, washed in pale yellow light that shades into sky blue in every direction. Yet you do not fall. The air holds you as water holds a floating leaf. A steady wind moves around you, and you notice that it moves through you as well, entering with each breath and leaving with the next, until the boundary between you and the sky feels thin. Here and there the blue deepens into streaks of blue-emerald green, and green flecked with gold glitters at the edges of sight like sunlight on moving leaves. This is the Scintillating Intelligence: everything flickers and nothing settles. Let the wind carry you forward and upward without trying too hard to steer.

steps.title: The Ox, the Eagle and the Sylphs
steps.text: An eagle rises beside you on the same current, wings still, eye fixed ahead. Below you a great ox walks calmly across the sky as though it were a field, patient and enormous. Aleph means ox: the strength that pulls the plough is here too, quiet and unhurried. Now you glimpse slender, quick shapes in the wind itself. They flicker at the edges of your vision and vanish when you look straight at them: the sylphs, the beings of Air. A small island of earth drifts past carrying a stand of aspens, every leaf trembling and flashing silver. Somewhere a honey-coloured topaz glints in the light. The sharp, green scent of galbanum passes on the breeze and is gone.

steps.title: Within the Trump
steps.text: The wind carries you into the heart of the trump. Colours spiral outward from a centre you cannot quite find, pale yellow and blue and green, turning like breath made visible. A dove passes, then a vulture circling high above, then a butterfly that looks too fragile for such a wind and yet is untroubled by it. Heavy clusters of grapes hang in the air, sweet-smelling. Far below, water glints, and a crocodile lies in it, still and patient. A tiger paces nearby, its stripes like flame. None of these creatures threatens you; each one is simply present and complete. Notice how it feels to be here with no plan, no task and nowhere to go but this moment, and let any habit of bracing yourself loosen.

steps.title: The Guide
steps.text: A figure comes toward you from the centre of the spiral. It may appear as the Fool himself, green-clad and horned, light on his feet. It may appear as Hoor-pa-kraat, Harpocrates, a child seated on a lotus with a finger to his lips. Greet it with courtesy. If you want to test it, trace Aleph in pale yellow light between you and notice how the figure meets the sign. Then ask what this path has to teach you, and wait. The answer may come as a word, a gesture, a sound, a silence, or an object placed in your open hands. Receive whatever comes without judging it, improving it or deciding in advance what it ought to be. Take the time you need, and when the exchange is complete, give thanks.

steps.title: The Threshold of Kether
steps.text: The wind grows quiet, and the light ahead becomes so bright that the yellow and blue dissolve into pure white brilliance. This is the threshold of Kether, the Crown. You do not cross it. Stand, or float, at the edge and look. You may see a single point of light, or a vast swirling motion like the first stirring of the heavens, or the profile of an ancient bearded king with his other side turned away. You may see only brightness. Notice that the breath you have followed all along seems to begin here, before it becomes wind. Do not reach for it or try to keep it. Let a little of its stillness enter you, then bow and turn back.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Let the wind carry you back the way you came. The guide may go with you or stay; either is right. You pass the spirals, the tiger and the crocodile, the dove and the vulture, the aspens, the eagle and the patient ox, while the white light behind you softens to pale yellow and then to sky blue. Ahead you see the back of the veil with its green figure. Step through into the grey temple of Chokmah and feel your feet firmly on its floor. Turn to the veil and trace Aleph in reverse, last stroke first, watching the light dissolve until the cloth is plain. Face the pillar and thank Ratziel for guidance and protection. Let the temple fade gently into darkness.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Take a slow, full breath and let it go with a sigh. After so much air, let yourself grow heavy, like the ox. Feel the weight of your body on the seat and your feet flat on the floor. Notice the temperature of the room and the sounds around you. Wriggle your fingers and toes, stretch your arms and shoulders, and open your eyes. Look at a few ordinary objects and name them silently. Press your palms against the floor or stamp your feet. Before you do anything else, write down what you experienced, above all whatever the guide gave you, while the details are still clear.

closing: Declare the working closed, then perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Stamp your foot firmly and put out the candle. Airy paths can leave you light-headed or scattered, so ground with care: eat something substantial (bread or something salty), drink water, and walk on the ground or hold something heavy for a minute. In your magical diary, record the date, time, moon phase, your physical and mental state, and everything you saw and received. Then check your record against the symbols list: note what matches and what does not, and force neither. Leave interpretation for a day or two.

tunnel.reflection: In its averse aspect, the Fool's openness sinks into plain emptiness: freedom without direction, a leap that is only a fall, spirit scattering into vagueness, distraction or a refusal ever to commit. Consider the difference between an innocence that holds to nothing because it is whole and a drift that holds to nothing because it fears choosing. Treat Amprodias as a mirror for that difference, not as a force to call, and build up the day-side path of Aleph first.

notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth deck and Liber 777: Aleph, elemental Air, Atu 0 The Fool (777 title 'The Spirit of Aethyr'), joining Kether and Chokmah. The Golden Dawn also places the Fool on Aleph, so no swap applies here. The He/Tzaddi (Star/Emperor) exchange from Liber AL I:57 affects only paths 15 and 28. Data corrections: path 12's entries have run into the digest's plant, perfume and magical-power cells for this path. Standard 777 for path 11 is plants Aspen, perfume Galbanum, magical power Divination. 'Vervain, Herb Mercury, Major-lane [Marjolane], Palm [[Lime or', 'Mastic, White Sandal, [[Nutmeg]]' and 'Miracles of Healing, Gift of Tongues, Knowledge of [Sciences]' belong to path 12 and are not used here. The digest's tunnel 'power' field (Divination) is correct. The digest's 'correct design of the trump' entry ('a bearded Ancient seen in profile') echoes Kether's magical image. It may be Liber 777's own entry rather than a data error, but it does not describe the painted Thoth Atu 0. The veil and path therefore use the published Thoth imagery, and the Ancient appears only at the Kether threshold. The '[Swords] Emperors or Princes' note under the general Tarot attribution refers to the court cards of Air and is not an error. Optional: 777 col. V gives YHVH as the divine name of this path, which can be vibrated at the veil after Aleph. Chokmah's God-name Yah and archangel Ratziel follow the Golden Dawn and 777. The tunnel genius Amprodias comes from Liber 231 as used in Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden. The digest's Arabic-script spelling of the name is not traditional and was left out. This is a supernal path above the Abyss, so treat the journey as symbolic contemplation.

title: The Path of the Winged Word
summary: Path 12 joins Binah, Understanding, to Kether, the Crown. It belongs to Beth, the House, and to Mercury, shown in the Thoth deck as Atu I, The Magus, and the Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Intelligence of Transparency. Working it builds clear intent, care with speech and skill, and the ability to let the will pass through you without bending it.

prepare.incense: Mastic, white sandalwood, mace or storax (777 col. XLII perfumes of path 12). Optionally add a pinch of myrrh, Binah's perfume, while you build the lower temple.
prepare.candle: Yellow candle (King scale of path 12) on a black cloth (Queen scale of Binah). You can add a purple ribbon or cloth for the path's Queen-scale colour.
prepare.stone: Opal or agate (777 col. XL)
prepare.facing: East
prepare.notes: Banish first, with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or Liber XXV (the Star Ruby). Wednesday, or a planetary hour of Mercury, suits this path. A wand or caduceus can lie on the altar. Keep your magical diary and a pen within reach and set aside about 25 undisturbed minutes. This is a supernal path, above the Abyss. Many teachers advise knowing the lower paths well before working it. Treat what you see as symbolic contemplation, not as attainment of the grades these paths stand for.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in your chosen posture, spine straight, hands resting on your thighs, and let your eyes close. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the rhythm even, not forced; if the holds strain, shorten the count. With each outbreath, let one part of the body soften: brow and jaw, throat and shoulders, arms and hands, chest and belly, hips, legs and feet. Feel the weight of your body resting on the seat and the floor. Let the sounds of the room come and go without following them. When the breath runs by itself and the body is heavy and still, gather your attention just behind the eyes, as if you stood at the edge of a quiet space that is ready to be built.

steps.title: The Temple of Binah
steps.text: A temple forms around you. Its walls and floor are black, the Queen-scale colour of Binah. It is not a hard or empty black but the deep, living dark of still water at night, and it holds you the way the sea holds a swimmer. On a plain altar at the centre burns a single crimson flame, and the air is heavy and sweet with myrrh. Beside the altar stands the image of this sphere: a mature woman, robed and silent, her stillness older than the stones. At the edges of the dark sit great still forms, the Aralim, the choir of this sphere. A quiet sorrow may hang in the air; let it be. Face the altar, breathe in, and vibrate YHVH Elohim (Yod He Vau He Elohim) until the walls seem to hum. Then call Tzaphkiel, archangel of Binah, and ask for guardianship on the path.

steps.title: The Veil of the Magus
steps.text: In the east of the temple, where a wall should be, hangs a veil. As you come closer you see that it is painted with Atu I, The Magus: a young figure caught in swift motion, winged at the feet, with the tools of magic wheeling in the air around him, a caduceus rising behind him and the dog-headed ape of Thoth crouched below. Stand before it. With your right forefinger, trace the letter Beth, ב, in clear yellow light, the King-scale colour of this path: a roof, a wall and a floor, a house open on its left side. Let the letter hang shining in the air. Vibrate its name, Beth, and feel the sound pass into the cloth. The veil thins and brightens like light through glass. Step forward through the letter and the image, and let them close behind you.

steps.title: The Transparent Way
steps.text: You stand at the foot of a path that climbs steeply into clear, brilliant air. Everything is steeped in yellow light, the King-scale colour, shading at the edges into deep purple, the Queen scale, as though dawn and dusk were happening together. The path underfoot seems to be made of glass, or of air made firm, and through it you see yellow depths falling away below. This is the Intelligence of Transparency, which the old commentary links with the place that visions come from. Nothing here is hidden and nothing blocks the way. Notice how your own thoughts behave in this air: do they come sharp and quick, or do they cloud over? Threads of grey and violet light drift at the edges of sight, and the air carries the clean, resinous scent of mastic and storax. Walk slowly.

steps.title: The Creatures of Mercury
steps.text: As you climb, the path grows lively. Swallows cut past you, fast and exact, turning on currents you cannot see. On a ledge an ibis stands on one leg, its long curved bill tilted as though it were reading something written in the air. Further on sits a baboon, the cynocephalus sacred to Thoth, hands on its knees, watching you with bright, intelligent eyes. When you pause, it copies your posture. Low plants of vervain and marjoram edge the path, and a single palm leans out from the rock. In the cliff face a vein of opal catches the light and shifts through fiery colours as you pass. Above you the sign of Mercury turns slowly, crescent over circle over cross: the mark of the one who carries messages between the worlds.

steps.title: The House of the Word
steps.text: The path levels out onto an open height where the air almost rings, like the note of a struck glass. Here the picture on the veil comes to life around you. The tools of the art circle in a slow, wide orbit: a wand, a cup, a sword, a disc, a stylus, a scroll. Each one passes close to you and moves away again. Behind them stands a caduceus, a staff of light wound with two serpents whose heads meet beneath outspread wings. Remember that Beth means house, and that the Hebrew scriptures begin with this letter. Sense the whole path as that kind of house: a shelter where the first impulse of the Crown becomes a word that can be spoken and heard. Stay here a while and listen beneath the ringing.

steps.title: The Guide
steps.text: A figure steps out of the circling light: a youth, lithe and quick, winged at heel and helmet, carrying the caduceus. Some see him as Hermes, some as ibis-headed Thoth with the scribe's palette, some as both at once. Greet him courteously. If you want to test him, trace Beth in yellow light between you and watch how he meets the sign; a true guide of this path is at ease with it. Then ask him plainly what this path has to teach you, and listen. He may speak, show you a scene, or place a word, a symbol or an object in your hands. Receive whatever comes without judging it and without trying to shape it. Take all the time you need. When the exchange feels complete, thank him.

steps.title: The Threshold of Kether
steps.text: The guide turns and points upward. The path ends at a threshold where the yellow air becomes too bright to hold any colour at all. Beyond it is pure white brilliance, the light of Kether, the Crown. You do not cross. You stand at the edge and look. You may glimpse a single point of light, or a vast, slow swirling like the first motion of the heavens, or the profile of an ancient bearded king whose other side is never shown. You may see only the light itself. Do not strain toward it and do not try to keep it. Let a little of its stillness settle into you, the way sunlight warms a stone. When you have looked long enough, bow and turn away.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Walk back down the path the way you came. The guide may go with you or stay above; either is fine. You pass the circling tools, the ape, the ibis on its ledge, the vein of opal and the swallows, while the brilliance behind you softens to yellow and then to deepening purple. Ahead you see the back of the veil, bright with the Magus. Step through into the black temple of Binah and feel its floor beneath you. Turn to face the veil. Trace Beth in reverse, from the last stroke to the first, and watch the light withdraw until the cloth is plain and dark. Face the altar and its crimson flame, and thank Tzaphkiel for guarding your way. Let the temple fade gently into darkness.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Notice your breath, a little fuller now. Feel the weight of your body on the seat, your feet on the floor and the temperature of the air on your skin. Hear the ordinary sounds of the room. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, stretch if you need to, and open your eyes when you are ready. Look around and silently name a few plain objects you can see. Press your palms to the floor or stamp your feet lightly. Before you do anything else, write down what you saw, heard and received, above all whatever the guide gave you, while it is still fresh.

closing: Declare the working closed, then perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Stamp your foot firmly (three times, if that is your custom) and put out the candle. Eat something plain and substantial and drink some water. In your magical diary, record the date, time, moon phase, your physical and mental state, and everything you saw and received. Then check your record against the symbols list: note what matches and what does not, and force neither. Leave interpretation for a day or two.

tunnel.reflection: Consider the Magus's shadow. The same quickness that carries truth can carry a lie, and the ape at his feet repeats the word without understanding it. Ask where your own cleverness has been used to mislead others or yourself, and where your speech has run ahead of the truth. Treat Baratchial as a mirror for this self-examination, not as a power to call, and work the day-side path of Beth until its clarity is steady before you turn to the tunnel.

notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth deck and Liber 777: Beth, Mercury, Atu I The Magus (777 title 'The Magus of Power'), joining Kether and Binah. The Golden Dawn places the Magician (Juggler) on this path too, so no swap applies here. The He/Tzaddi (Star/Emperor) exchange from Liber AL I:57 affects only paths 15 and 28. Data corrections: the digest's plant, perfume and magical-power cells are shifted by one row. Path 12's own values begin in path 11's cells, and path 12's cells hold the last words of its own entries followed by path 13 (Gimel/Moon) values: 'Almond, Mugwort, Hazel, Moonwort', 'Menstrual Blood, Camphor, Aloes' and 'The White Tincture, Clairvoyance, Divination by [Dreams]'. The journey uses the standard 777 values for path 12 instead. Plants: Vervain, Herb Mercury, Marjolane (marjoram), Palm, with the bracketed addition [[Lime or Linden]], which the shift split across the path 11 and 12 cells. Perfumes: Mastic, White Sandal, [[Nutmeg]], Mace, Storax, all fugitive odours. Powers: Miracles of Healing, Gift of Tongues, Knowledge of Sciences; the digest's tunnel 'power' field already has these correctly. Stone: 777 col. XL gives Opal, Agate for this path. 'Especially Fire Opal' is 777's qualifier for Hod's opal, so it is not given here. 'Helment' in the trump-design entry is a typo for helmet. Optional: 777 col. V gives this path the divine name Azbogah (אזבוגה, the 'name of eight', matching Mercury's number), which can be vibrated at the veil after Beth. Binah's God-name YHVH Elohim and archangel Tzaphkiel follow the Golden Dawn and 777. The tunnel genius Baratchial comes from Liber 231 as used in Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden. The digest's Arabic-script spelling of the name is not traditional and was left out. This is a supernal path above the Abyss, so treat the journey as symbolic contemplation.

title: The Silver Road of the Priestess
summary: Path 13, Gimel, runs straight up the Middle Pillar from Tiphareth through the Abyss to Kether. It is the longest path on the Tree, the path of the Moon and Atu II The Priestess. Working it develops stillness, receptivity and deep intuitive memory: the ability to become a clear, reflecting surface for what lies beyond the self.

prepare.incense: Camphor (sparingly, as the smoke is sharp) or aloes wood (777 col. XLII: camphor, aloes, all sweet virginal odours). A grain of olibanum at the opening honours Tiphareth.
prepare.candle: Blue, the path's King-scale colour (777 col. XV), on a silver or pale grey cloth for its Queen-scale silver (col. XVI). A gold candle or cloth for the Tiphareth opening is optional.
prepare.stone: Moonstone, pearl or clear quartz crystal (777 col. XL)
prepare.facing: East; if you work at night with the Moon visible, you may face the Moon instead
prepare.notes: Work it on a Monday, in a planetary hour of the Moon, or near the full Moon. This is the highest path on the Middle Pillar and it crosses the Abyss, so tradition has it worked late, after the lower paths and the paths into Tiphareth. Dim light is enough. Keep your diary within reach, because lunar impressions fade like dreams. The holds add up to about 15 minutes; allow 20 to 25 minutes in all.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright with your spine straight, feet flat on the floor, palms resting on your thighs. Close your eyes. Take up the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, rest empty for four. Let the rhythm settle until it needs no effort. With each out-breath, release tension from the top down: forehead, eyes, jaw, throat, shoulders, arms, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. Notice the coolness or warmth of the air and the small sounds of the room, and let them recede. This path asks for stillness above all, so take your time here. When body and breath are quiet, let the count dissolve and rest in simple awareness.

steps.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
steps.text: Around you a temple takes shape. Its walls and floor are clear gold, as if sunlight had been made solid. It is six-sided, and the warm air carries the scent of frankincense. At the centre stands an altar with a single steady flame. On the wall beyond it you see the magical image of this sphere: a majestic king, a child, a crucified god. One of these faces may come forward more strongly than the others. Stand before the altar and vibrate the divine name of Tiphareth: YHVH Eloah va-Daath (Yod Heh Vav Heh Eh-loh-ah vah-Dah-ath). Let it fill the golden room. Then call on the archangel Raphael. Feel a bright, clear presence, like fresh air full of sunlight, take its place beside you as guardian of your journey.

steps.title: The Veil of Gimel
steps.text: Beyond the altar, in the eastern wall, hangs a tall curtain of deep blue shot with silver. Painted on it is Atu II, The Priestess. A woman sits with her arms lifted, and from them a veil of shimmering light falls around her like a net of dew; it is all she wears. A bow lies across her knees, a camel stands at her feet, and seeds and crystals are scattered below. Look at the painting until it feels present and alive. Then raise your hand and trace the letter Gimel ג large on the curtain, in pure bright blue: a tall upright stroke with a short foot stepping out at its base. Vibrate the letter's name, Gimel (Gim-mel, with a hard G). The blue letter flares, the curtain parts down its centre, and you step through.

steps.title: The Moonlit Desert
steps.text: You come out under a night sky of deep, clear blue. A full Moon hangs high ahead, and its silver light lies across a wide, pale desert. The sand is cool underfoot and faintly luminous: silver, shading to a cold pale blue where the dunes fold. There is almost no wind. The path is not a road. Instead, a single line of moonlight runs straight ahead across the sand, rising gently, and you know it leads up to the crown of the Tree. This is the longest of all the paths, climbing the Middle Pillar from the Sun to the Crown. The silence is complete. Stand here for a while and let the cold, clean air and the silver light wash through you.

steps.title: The Camel
steps.text: A camel kneels on the sand beside the line of light, pale in the moonlight, calm and patient, with a saddle-cloth of blue and silver on its back. Gimel means camel: the creature that crosses the desert carrying its own water. Approach it slowly, rest a hand on its warm neck, and mount. It rises with a rocking motion and walks, unhurried, along the silver line. Feel its steady gait beneath you. For a while a lean, pale dog, a hound of the huntress, keeps pace at your side, then drops back. At the edges of the dunes, faint shapes may drift like mist or half-remembered faces. Let them pass without giving them your attention. Keep your gaze on the Moon.

steps.title: The Uniting Intelligence
steps.text: The desert grows wider and emptier. The ground falls away on either side, and you realise the camel is walking a narrow ridge across a great gulf: the Abyss, where the middle of the Tree seems to open into darkness. Do not look down for long. The moonlight holds the path firm. Small things glint in the sand as you pass: a pearl, a moonstone, a clear crystal, the grey-green leaves of mugwort, an almond branch in flower, a small ranunculus. The air carries a faint, clean scent of camphor. This path is called the Uniting Intelligence, the essence of glory and the fulfilment of the truth of spiritual things. Feel how it binds the heart of the Tree to its source with a single cord of silver light.

steps.title: The Priestess
steps.text: Ahead, where the ridge meets the far side, a figure waits in the moonlight. The camel kneels and you dismount. She is the Priestess. She sits veiled in a web of shimmering light that falls from her raised arms like a curtain of dew and starlight. She wears a lunar crown, and a bow rests across her knees. At her feet lie seeds, fruits and crystals, the first beginnings of form. You may instead see Artemis with her bow and hounds, or Khonsu, the young Egyptian moon god crowned with disc and crescent. Let the form come as it will. Greet her quietly. Ask what this path teaches, and what you must become to walk it. Then be still, and let her answer come as words, an image, a gesture or silence.

steps.title: The Threshold of Kether
steps.text: Thank her. Behind her, the silver line runs a short way further to the very top of the Tree. Go to its edge and stop. Above and before you is a brilliance so pure it has no colour: white beyond white, a single point that is also everywhere. You sense the first stirrings of motion, the Primum Mobile, where all turning begins. Silently, the divine name Eheieh, 'I am', sounds within you. Do not try to enter the light or hold on to it. Look only for as long as is comfortable. Then lower your eyes, bow, and turn back.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: The Priestess, or whatever form met you, has withdrawn into the veil of light. The camel is waiting. Mount again and ride back down the silver line, over the ridge across the gulf and through the pale desert under the Moon. The way back is quicker. Dismount where you began, thank the camel, and walk to the painted curtain of the Priestess standing in the sand. Step through it into the golden temple of Tiphareth. Turn and trace the letter Gimel once more in blue, then watch it fade into the cloth as the curtain closes. Turn to the altar and thank the archangel Raphael for guarding your way. Let the golden temple dim and dissolve.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Feel your body again, heavier after the thin air of the path. Notice the chair beneath you, the floor under your feet, the temperature of the room. Breathe a little deeper and a little faster than before. Move your fingers and toes and stretch your arms. Rub your palms together until they are warm, and press them gently over your eyes. Open your eyes and look at something solid and ordinary, naming it to yourself. Stamp your feet or press them firmly into the floor. Before anything else, write down the guide's word or symbol and whatever you saw, heard or felt, however slight. Lunar impressions fade quickly, like dreams on waking.

symbols.symbol: Silver rayed with sky blue (Empress scale)

symbols.source: 777 col. XLI; bow on the Thoth trump

symbols.symbol: Scent of camphor or aloes; sweet, virginal odours
Khonsu (Chomse), young moon god with disc and crescent
A woman veiled in a net of light, arms raised
Seeds, fruits and crystals, the beginnings of form
Drifting shades or half-seen faces (lemures, ghosts)

closing: Banish with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Stamp your feet, then eat something substantial and drink water, because lunar work can leave you dreamy and ungrounded. Record the session in your diary: date, time, planetary hour, Moon phase, what you saw, and the guide's word or symbol. Then check it against the symbols list, noting what matched and what did not. For the next few nights, keep a dream log. 777 gives divination by dreams as this path's magical power, and material from the working often surfaces there.

tunnel.reflection: On the averse side, the Priestess's veil hardens into a wall: secrecy kept for its own sake, a Moon that reflects nothing, dream-fog and psychic glamour mistaken for depth, memory circling on itself among ghosts. In plain waking reflection, consider where you hoard the hidden to feel special, or prefer vague impressions to clear seeing. Work the day-side path of Gimel first, and more than once. Keep this as contemplation and journaling, not a journey into the tunnel.

notes:
Attributions follow Liber 777 and The Book of Thoth. Path 13 is not affected by Crowley's Tzaddi/He swap; the Moon and Atu II are the same in the Golden Dawn and Thoth systems. Crowley titles the card 'The Priestess', and its Book T title is 'The Priestess of the Silver Star'.

Where the digest was incomplete or differed:
- Plants: the digest listed only ranunculus. 777 col. XXXIX gives almond, mugwort, hazel (as Luna), moonwort and ranunculus, and these are used.
- Perfumes: the digest gave only 'sweet virginal odours'. 777 col. XLII also lists camphor and aloes.
- Magical powers: the digest's main field said only 'Dreams'. 777 col. XLV gives the White Tincture, clairvoyance and divination by dreams, as the digest's tunnel field correctly shows.
- Trump design: the digest's 'correct design' line (a crowned priestess before the veil of Isis, between the Pillars of Seth) is the older Golden Dawn description. The steps follow Crowley's painted Thoth design.
- Tiphareth's vision: the digest's field was truncated. It is 'the Vision of the Harmony of Things (also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion)'.

Other notes:
- Tiphareth's archangel follows the 777 / Golden Dawn order given for this project (Raphael); some systems give Michael.
- Path 13 crosses the Abyss and Daath. In Thelemic terms, visualising it rehearses the path's symbols; it is not the crossing the A∴A∴ treats as a grade attainment. Keep the approach to Kether a brief, modest glimpse.

title: The Door of the Empress
summary: Path 14, Daleth, runs level across the top of the Tree between Binah and Chokmah, joining Understanding and Wisdom above the Abyss. It is the path of Venus and Atu III The Empress, the 'door' where the Father's force and the Mother's form meet. Working it develops love as a creative principle: the fertile imagination that gives birth to form, and a felt sense that the supernal pair are one.

prepare.incense: Sandalwood, myrtle or rose (777 col. XLII: sandalwood, myrtle, all soft voluptuous odours). A pinch of myrrh at the opening honours the Binah temple.
prepare.candle: Emerald green, the path's King-scale colour (777 col. XV), on a sky-blue cloth, its Queen-scale colour (col. XVI). A black cloth under the candle for Binah's Queen-scale colour is optional.
prepare.stone: Emerald or turquoise (777 col. XL)
prepare.facing: East, the usual quarter for temple work
prepare.notes: Work it on a Friday or in a planetary hour of Venus. Path 14 is a supernal path, so tradition has it worked after the lower paths. Keep the light low and the room warm. Have your diary and the symbols checklist ready. The holds add up to about 15 minutes; with reading time, allow 20 to 25 minutes.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs. If you know the god-form posture, you can use that. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold full for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the count grow slow and even. With each out-breath, let one part of the body soften: the jaw, then the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs. Notice your weight settling into the chair and the floor. Let the day's thoughts pass without following them. When breath and body are quiet, let the count go and simply breathe, aware of the room around you and the stillness gathering inside.

steps.title: The Temple of Binah
steps.text: Before you a temple forms. Its walls, floor and vaulted roof are black. The black is not empty but full, a soft deep darkness like the sea at night. Low crimson lamps burn in niches, and the air is heavy with myrrh. Far off you hear the slow breathing of waves. At the centre stands a black altar with a cup on it. Behind the altar stands the magical image of this sphere: a mature woman, grave and calm, the Great Mother. Stand before the altar and vibrate the divine name of Binah: YHVH Elohim (Yod Heh Vav Heh Eh-loh-heem). Feel it roll out into the darkness. Then call on the archangel Tzaphkiel, the Beholder of God. Sense a vast, quiet presence, like a hooded shadow, take its place beside you as witness and guardian.

steps.title: The Veil of Daleth
steps.text: Behind the altar, in the far wall, is a doorway hung with a heavy curtain. Painted on it is Atu III, The Empress. A crowned woman sits enthroned among greens, blues and rose. Her arms and body form a circle crossed by a bar. A sparrow and a dove are beside her, a pelican at her feet, and an arched gateway behind her. Look at the painting until it seems to breathe. Then raise your hand and trace the letter Daleth ד large on the curtain, in brilliant emerald green: a level roof with a single leg dropping from its right-hand end. Vibrate the letter's name, Daleth (Dah-leth), and feel it resound. Daleth means door, and the curtain swings open like one. You step through.

steps.title: The Level Road
steps.text: You step out into morning light. A path leads through green country, the emerald of new leaves and the soft green of early spring, under an open sky of clear, soft blue. The air is mild and smells of damp earth and something sweet. The ground rolls in gentle folds, and small springs run through the grass. Now and then the light takes on a flush of rose, shot through with pale yellow rays, as if dawn and blossom were one colour. You notice that you are neither climbing nor descending. This road runs level across the very top of the Tree, from the Mother's darkness towards the Father's grey radiance. Walk slowly. Feel the ground under your feet and the warmth on your face, and notice how easily everything here grows.

steps.title: Myrtle, Rose and Dove
steps.text: The path runs between hedges of glossy, fragrant myrtle and wild roses that open as you watch. Clover covers the ground at your feet. Sparrows dart and chatter in the branches. A pair of white doves lands on the path ahead and walks in front of you for a while. Further on, a still pool lies among reeds, and a swan moves across it without leaving a ripple. The water is the blue-green of turquoise, and on its bed you glimpse a stone of deep emerald. A light wind carries the scent of sandalwood and rose. Let each thing be exactly itself, and notice its colour, texture and sound. Nothing here asks you to hurry. Everything is making something: leaf, flower, egg, seed.

steps.title: The Illuminating Intelligence
steps.text: The path opens onto a meadow. At its centre stands a throne whose pillars rise in twisting shapes, like flames of green and gold. Behind it an arched gateway frames the sky. The throne is empty for now, but the scene of the card is laid out around its foot. A pelican stands over her nest, piercing her own breast to feed her young. Beside her leans a shield bearing a white, double-headed eagle. A lotus lies on the seat. This is the fourteenth path, called the Illuminating Intelligence: the light in which the hidden foundations of holy things first take shape. Stand quietly before the throne. Feel the green light around you thicken and soften, the way light might just before it becomes a form.

steps.title: The Empress
steps.text: A presence gathers on the throne, and a woman is seated there: the Empress. Her robes shift between green and blue. Her arms and body together make the shape of a circle crossed by a bar, the alchemical sign of Salt. A sparrow and a dove rest near her, and she takes up the lotus. You may instead see Hathor, cow-horned with the sun's disc between her horns, or Aphrodite. Let whatever form comes, come. Greet her with respect. Ask her what this path teaches, and what you need to know about love and making. Then be silent and receptive. She may speak, show you something, or give you a symbol or a word. Receive it without judging it, and remember it.

steps.title: The Threshold of Chokmah
steps.text: When the exchange feels complete, thank her. Beyond the throne the gateway stands open, and the path runs a little further to a threshold. Walk to it and stop at the edge. Before you lies a vast, soft grey radiance, pearl and silver. Within it is a pale, pure blue, like the sky seen from a great height. Points of light turn slowly inside it: the wheeling of the fixed stars and the zodiac. You sense a force that is pure outgoing will, restless and bright, the Father's energy before it takes any form. Somewhere within you, the short divine name Yah sounds. Do not enter. Take in only what comes, bow to the threshold, and turn around.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Walk back along the level road the way you came. Pass the empty throne and the pelican's nest, the pool and the swan, the roses and the myrtle. The doves lift away as you pass. The green light feels gentle and familiar now. Ahead you see the painted curtain of the Empress standing in the meadow like a door without a wall. Step through it into the black temple of Binah. Turn to face the curtain and trace the letter Daleth over it once more. Watch the emerald letter sink into the fabric as the curtain falls closed. Turn to the altar and thank the archangel Tzaphkiel for guarding you, and feel the dark, still presence withdraw. Let the temple dim and fade.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Become aware of your body again: its weight in the chair, your feet on the floor, your hands where they rest. Feel the breath moving in and out on its own. Listen to the sounds of the room and the world outside. Take a few deeper breaths, and with each one become more fully present. Move your fingers and toes and roll your shoulders. When you are ready, open your eyes and look around, naming a few ordinary things you see. Stamp your feet lightly on the floor. Before you do anything else, write down what you saw, heard and felt, especially the guide's word or symbol, while it is still fresh.

symbols.symbol: Bright rose or cerise rayed with pale yellow (Empress scale)
Venus, the morning or evening star
Scent of sandalwood or myrtle; soft, voluptuous odours
Hathor, cow-horned with the solar disc
A pelican feeding her young with her own blood
A shield bearing a white double-headed eagle
An enthroned woman whose arms and torso form the alchemical sign of Salt, holding a lotus
The Illuminating Intelligence: light that founds hidden, holy ideas

closing: Banish with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or the Star Ruby if that is your practice. Stamp your feet or press them firmly into the floor, then eat something simple, such as bread or fruit, and drink water. Record the session in your magical diary: date, time, planetary hour, Moon phase, what you saw, and the guide's word or symbol. Then check it against the symbols list, noting what matched, what did not, and anything new. Leave interpretation for a day or two.

tunnel.reflection: On the averse side, the door of Daleth opens only inward. Love narrows into appetite, and the fertile mother becomes one who devours what she bears: the pelican reversed, feeding on her young instead of feeding them. In ordinary waking reflection, consider where your desire seeks to possess rather than to create, and where care has turned into control. Work the day-side path of the Empress several times first, and keep this as notebook contemplation, not a journey or an invocation.

notes:
Attributions follow Liber 777 and The Book of Thoth. Path 14 is not affected by Crowley's Tzaddi/He swap; Venus and Atu III are the same in the Golden Dawn and Thoth systems.

Corrections to the digest:
- The 'Title of the Tarot trump' field ran into the next row. The fragment 'The Son of the Morning, chief among the [Mighty]' (often printed 'Sun of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty') is the Book T title of Atu IV The Emperor. The Empress's title is 'The Daughter of the Mighty Ones'.
- The 'correct design' line in the digest (a winged, star-crowned goddess standing on the Moon) appears to be the older Golden Dawn-style description, not the painted Thoth card. The steps follow Crowley's Thoth design.

Other notes:
- Binah's magical image here is 'a mature woman, a matron', from Golden Dawn usage. 777 remarks that almost any female image shows some aspect of Binah.
- Path 14 is horizontal, so 'lower' and 'upper' are conventions. It is worked here from Binah (3) to Chokmah (2), but can equally be worked from Chokmah.
- The Sepher Yetzirah title is sometimes translated 'Luminous Intelligence'.
- The swan and the wider 'birds' entry appear in the digest as bracketed secondary animals.

title: The Window of the Star
summary: The fifteenth path, He (the window), rises from Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Adept, across the Abyss to Chokmah, the sphere of the fixed stars. In Crowley's arrangement it carries Atu XVII, The Star, and Aquarius: Nuit pouring the waters of life, and the recognition of oneself as a star in the body of infinite space. Working it develops clear aspiration, hope grounded in perception rather than fantasy, and a felt sense of one's own orbit.

prepare.incense: Galbanum (777 col. XLII, Aquarius row, which follows the Star under Crowley's swap). A little olibanum may be burned first for the temple of Tiphareth. (Golden Dawn attribution: dragon's blood, for Aries.)
prepare.candle: A violet candle (King scale of Aquarius, 777 col. XV) on a sky-blue cloth (Queen scale, col. XVI); a gold or yellow candle may stand for Tiphareth. (Golden Dawn / 777 as first printed for path 15: scarlet.)
prepare.stone: Chalcedony, or a clear glass sphere (777 col. XL: artificial glass).
prepare.facing: East, the quarter of Air for fixed-air Aquarius and the station of Raphael.
prepare.notes: Saturday (Saturn is the traditional ruler of Aquarius) or any clear night; if you can, spend a few minutes looking at the real night sky before you begin. Study the Thoth Atu XVII before closing your eyes. Banish beforehand; the Star Ruby is especially fitting. Have your record ready. This path crosses the Abyss, and the journey halts at its edge by design.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat, hands open on your thighs, head balanced lightly on the spine. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the count be slow and exact. This path belongs to air, so attend to the breath itself: its coolness as it enters, its warmth as it leaves. With each exhalation loosen one region of the body: the face and eyes, the throat, the shoulders, the chest, the belly, the hips and legs. Imagine the body as a clear vessel, emptying of tension the way a cup empties when it is tipped. Let outside sounds pass through you. When the breath is even and the body feels light and settled, release the count and rest.

steps.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
steps.text: Around you a temple forms, six-sided, its walls glowing a clear golden yellow, the Queen-scale colour of Tiphareth. Sunlight seems to come from everywhere at once, though no sun is visible. The floor is inlaid with a great hexagram. At its centre stands a cubic altar bearing a Rose Cross, a red rose blooming where its arms meet. The air is rich with olibanum. On the walls are three images: a majestic king, a child, and a god upon a cross, three faces of this sphere. Let the room grow steady and bright. Then draw a full breath and vibrate the God-name: YHVH Eloah va-Daath. Feel it fill all six walls. Call the archangel Raphael, and see a tall presence form beside you, robed in yellow shot with violet, bringing a cool, clean breeze like morning air.

steps.title: The Window of He
steps.text: Raphael leads you to one wall, where a tall curtain hangs. It is painted with Atu XVII of the Thoth deck, The Star: a woman beneath a night sky of blue and violet, pouring from two cups, a great seven-pointed star above her. Study it until it is vivid. Raise your hand and trace the letter He on the cloth in violet light, the King-scale colour of Aquarius, which travels to this path with the Star: a flat roof across the top, a long leg descending on the right, and a short separate leg on the left that does not quite reach the roof, a window with a gap for the light. Vibrate its name: He. The letter shines steadily. The curtain draws aside onto an open window full of night. Raphael remains, keeping the way. Climb through.

steps.title: Between Land and Water
steps.text: You stand at the edge of a vast, still night. The light here is violet, soft and cool, and the air has the pale clear blue of a sky just before dawn, though stars shine everywhere above you. Breathe it in: clean, fresh, perfectly still, air that holds its shape. Beneath your feet the ground is scattered with crystals, clear and faceted, catching the starlight. The path runs gently upward along a shoreline where calm water meets the land. Olive trees grow beside it, their silver-green leaves pale in the violet light. Among them a peacock steps slowly, then opens its tail: a hundred eyes of blue and green and bronze, each one a small watching star. Walk slowly. Notice the silence, and how far you can see.

steps.title: The Constituting Intelligence
steps.text: A green, resinous, faintly bitter scent reaches you: galbanum, rising from a censer that hangs from a low olive branch, its smoke curling upward in slow spirals. Beneath it, on a flat rock, lie a smooth stone of milky blue chalcedony and a sphere of clear glass. Pick up the glass and look through it. The stars seem nearer, and the darkness between them grows deeper and richer, not empty but full. The Sepher Yetzirah names this path the Constituting Intelligence, said to constitute the substance of creation in pure darkness. Let your attention rest not on the stars but on the dark between them, the ground from which every point of light stands out. Feel that darkness as something that holds rather than something that hides. Then set the glass down where you found it.

steps.title: The Star Pours
steps.text: Ahead, where the shore curves, a woman stands at the meeting of land and water. Her skin holds the faint blue of the night sky, and her hair falls long about her. In one hand she raises a cup of gold and pours; in the other she holds a cup of silver, pouring low, so that two shining streams fall, mingle, and run out over the land and into the still water. Behind her turns a great celestial globe, and above it blazes a seven-pointed star. All around her the light moves in slow spirals, as if space itself were curling. Watch the water fall. Notice where it lands and what it touches. Crowley names this figure Nuit, the star-goddess of infinite space, and the Book of the Law tells you that every man and every woman is a star.

steps.title: The Daughter of the Firmament
steps.text: She turns and sees you. Approach slowly and stop at a respectful distance; the water runs past your feet, cool and bright. This is the Daughter of the Firmament, the Dweller between the Waters. Greet her simply, then ask: what does this path teach? Be still and wait. The answer may come as words, a picture, a feeling, a colour, or a movement of the water. She may offer you something from one of her cups, or show you a single star and let you look at it. Take what is given without deciding yet what it means, and hold it clearly in memory. If anything in the figure seems wrong or strained, trace He in violet between you and watch how it responds: a true image grows steadier, a false one falters. If nothing comes, stay and listen. Take all the time you need.

steps.title: The Edge of the Abyss
steps.text: When the meeting feels complete, thank her. The path continues past her, rising into open night, until the land simply stops. Before you lies the Abyss, a gulf that is less dark than absent. Do not step off the edge. Stand, and look across. Far beyond, a great sphere of soft grey light glows, pearly and iridescent, touched with pure soft blue. Around it the whole wheel of the zodiac turns, and every star you have seen tonight seems to draw its light from there, as if from a fountain. This is Chokmah, Wisdom, the sphere of the fixed stars, where the name Yah resounds and the archangel Ratziel keeps the secrets of God. Let its radiance reach you across the gulf. Remain on this side. When you have seen enough, turn back.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Walk back down the path at the pace you came. Pass the woman, still pouring; the globe and the seven-pointed star; the censer of galbanum and the glass sphere on its rock; the olive trees and the peacock, its tail now folded. The crystals glint underfoot. Ahead you see the window you climbed through, framed in golden light. Climb back into the six-sided temple of Tiphareth. Turn to face the window and the painted Star. Trace He in violet once more, and this time watch it fade gently into the cloth as the curtain falls closed. Turn to Raphael and thank the archangel for keeping the way. Bow to the altar and the Rose Cross. Let the golden walls grow transparent, and let the temple dissolve into light, and then into quiet.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Come back into your body. Notice the chair beneath you, the floor under your feet, the temperature of the room on your skin. Take a few ordinary, deeper breaths, slightly quicker than before. Move your fingers and toes, stretch your neck and shoulders, and let the sounds of the room return fully. Open your eyes and look at something solid and familiar, naming it to yourself. Press your feet firmly into the floor and stamp them twice. Then, before anything else, write down what you experienced: the Star's answer, anything you were given, the colours, scents and sounds, and any surprises. Later, compare your record with the symbol list for this path.

symbols.source: King and Queen scales, 777 cols. XV-XVI, Aquarius row (path 28), moved with the Star
Emperor and Empress scales, 777 cols. XVII-XVIII, Aquarius row (path 28)

symbols.symbol: Aquarius: fixed air, water poured out
a star-woman pouring from a gold cup and a silver cup
a celestial globe; spirals of light
crystals at the meeting of land and water
Nuit, the star-goddess of infinite space
symbols.source: Crowley's identification of the Star figure; Liber AL

symbols.symbol: peacock; man or eagle (Cherub of Air)
a darkness that holds the stars rather than hides them

closing: Perform a banishing: the Star Ruby suits this path well, or use the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram. Stamp your feet, drink a glass of water, and eat something simple; if you feel light-headed or elated, a short walk outdoors helps. Record the session: date, time, sky conditions, what you saw, the Star's answer and anything received. Test the vision against the symbol list, noting matches, misses, and anything that belongs to the Golden Dawn Emperor/Aries set instead (ram, scarlet, ruby), which shows which attribution your imagination is drawing on. Revisit the notes after a day or two before interpreting them.

tunnel.reflection: The averse face of the Window is a pane that, turned toward the dark, shows only your own reflection: hope become fantasy, a star followed because it flatters, visions consecrated that lead nowhere. Consider, as reflection and not invocation, where your aspiration has become a picture you gaze at instead of a direction you travel, and where borrowed light has been mistaken for your own. Work the day-side path of the Star until it is familiar before turning to this, and banish afterwards.

notes: Crowley's swap: following Liber AL I:57 ('but צ [Tzaddi] is not the Star'), Crowley exchanged Atu IV and Atu XVII. In the Thoth system path 15 (He, Tiphareth to Chokmah) carries Atu XVII The Star with Aquarius, and path 28 (Tzaddi, Netzach to Yesod) carries Atu IV The Emperor with Aries. The Golden Dawn attribution, and 777's row for path 15 as printed, is He = The Emperor = Aries. The digest supplied that Emperor/Aries set: the trump, scarlet/red/brilliant flame/glowing red, ram and owl, tiger lily and geranium, ruby, dragon's blood, Men Thu, Athena, Mars and Minerva, the power of consecrating things, the fragment 'Mighty' (from the Emperor's title 'Sun of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty'), and the Emperor's 'correct design' (a flame-clad god). This journey replaces it with the Aquarian correspondences that travel with the Star, taken from 777's Aquarius row (path 28): violet, sky blue, bluish mauve, white tinged purple; man or eagle (Cherub of Air) and peacock; olive and coconut; artificial glass and chalcedony; galbanum; censer or aspergillus; Ganymede and Juno; power: astrology. The trump title becomes 'The Daughter of the Firmament, the Dweller between the Waters'. Crowley did not reissue 777's colour and correspondence rows after the swap, so carrying the whole Aquarius set to path 15 is a common Thoth-based reading rather than a printed table; some practitioners keep 777's scarlet on path 15 regardless of the swap. If you work Golden Dawn style, use the Emperor, scarlet and Aries throughout. The letter meaning (window) and the Sepher Yetzirah Intelligence (Constituting) belong to the path and do not move. Also corrected: the digest's magical-weapon field ran on into path 16 ('The Labour of Preparation' belongs to Vau), so only 'the horns, energy, the burin' is the Aries entry. The tunnel entry's power ('consecrating things') is likewise the Aries value. This path crosses the Abyss, so the journey halts at its edge and looks across; Chokmah is shown in its 777 colours (grey, pure soft blue, pearl iridescence). Crowley's identification of the Star figure as Nuit is followed; the paraphrased phrase 'every man and every woman is a star' is Liber AL I:3. Card details are paraphrased, and the glass sphere, censer on the branch and window framing are visualisation devices, not traditional teaching.

title: The Path of the Nail
summary: The sixteenth path, Vau (the nail), rises from Chesed, Mercy, across the Abyss to Chokmah, Wisdom. Under Taurus and Atu V, The Hierophant, it is the path of revelation: the nail that joins the divine to the human, and the teaching heard as an inner voice rather than received as an outer rule. Working it develops steadiness, patient inner listening, and the discernment to tell living tradition from dead dogma.

prepare.incense: Storax (777 col. XLII, Taurus). A pinch of cedar may be burned first for the temple of Chesed.
prepare.candle: A red-orange candle (King scale of the path, 777 col. XV) on a deep indigo cloth (Queen scale, col. XVI). A blue candle may stand for the temple of Chesed (its Queen-scale colour).
prepare.stone: Topaz (777 col. XL), held in the hand or set before you.
prepare.facing: North, the quarter of Earth, for fixed-earth Taurus. East is fine if you face East for all path work.
prepare.notes: Friday or an hour of Venus suits Taurus, which Venus rules. Study the Thoth Atu V for a few minutes before closing your eyes. Banish beforehand (Star Ruby or LBRP). Have your record and a pen ready. This path crosses the Abyss: approach it as an act of listening, go no farther than the journey describes, and do not repeat it on the same day.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs, spine tall but not stiff. Let your eyes close. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count slow and even. With each out-breath, let one part of the body soften: the jaw, the brow, the shoulders and arms, the belly, the legs. Notice the weight of the body pressing into the chair and the feet pressing into the floor, the way a bull stands in its field: heavy, patient, unhurried. Let the sounds of the room come and go without following them. When the breath runs by itself and the body feels settled and warm, let the count fall away and rest in the stillness.

steps.title: The Temple of Chesed
steps.text: Around you a temple takes shape: square, four walls of deep clear blue, the Queen-scale colour of Chesed, rising to a vault flecked with violet. The floor is cool blue stone and the air smells of cedar. Against the far wall stands a throne, and on it sits a mighty king, crowned and enthroned, broad-shouldered and generous of face, a sceptre in his hand. Before him a low altar holds a wand and a shepherd's crook. Take in the room slowly until it is steady. Then draw the breath deep and vibrate the God-name of this sphere, sending the sound out to all four walls: El. Feel the stone hum with it. Call on the archangel Tzadkiel, the Righteousness of God, and see a tall figure robed in blue and violet gather at your side, the soft glitter of the Chashmalim about him.

steps.title: The Veil of the Hierophant
steps.text: Tzadkiel leads you to the right of the throne, where a heavy curtain hangs in the wall. Painted on it is Atu V of the Thoth deck, The Hierophant: a figure enthroned above a bull, a tall window behind him, a woman standing before him. Look until the image is clear. Raise your hand and, with a finger of light, trace the letter Vau on the curtain: a single upright stroke with a short head turning to the left, like a nail or a hook. Draw it in red-orange, the King-scale colour of this path, and see it burn steadily against the cloth. Vibrate the letter's name: Vau. The curtain stirs as if breathed upon and parts down the middle. Tzadkiel remains at the threshold, keeping the door. Step through.

steps.title: The Red-Orange Road
steps.text: Beyond the veil you stand on a broad road of packed earth. The soil is a rich brown and the fields on either side a deep warm olive. The light is red-orange, low and steady like an evening that does not end, and above it the sky deepens to indigo. The road rises gently. Mallow grows along the verges, soft-leaved, its pale flowers nodding at your ankles. Ahead, giant trees stand at intervals beside the way, trunks so broad that several people could not circle them, roots gripping deep. Walk slowly and feel the ground take your weight with each step. In a field to one side a great bull grazes. It lifts its head and regards you, calm and immovable, then returns to the grass. Notice how much quiet there is here.

steps.title: The Triumphal Intelligence
steps.text: The air grows sweet with storax, warm and balsamic, seeping as resin from the bark of the great trees. Where the road passes between two of them, a wooden gate stands open, hung on heavy iron nails driven cleanly into the posts. Pause and look at the nails. Each one joins two things that would otherwise fall apart; in Hebrew the letter Vau is also the word for 'and'. Set into one gatepost is a large topaz, golden-brown, taking in the red light and giving it back softer. Rest your hand on it. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this the Triumphal or Eternal Intelligence: a delight in glory with nothing beyond it, a garden made ready for the just. Let that settle without forcing a meaning. Feel a joy that does not flare and fade, but stays, the way the earth stays.

steps.title: The Temple of the Hierophant
steps.text: Beyond the gate the road climbs to a hall of dark indigo stone. Inside, red-orange light falls through a tall oriel window whose upper frame is fastened with nine great nails; above it you can make out a serpent and a dove. Beneath the window a throne rests upon a bull, and elephants stand patiently on either side. In the four corners of the hall the four living creatures, a man, a lion, an eagle and a bull, face the throne. On it sits the Hierophant. On his breast a six-rayed star holds a five-pointed one, and within it a small child dances. His hand holds a wand crowned with three interlocking rings. Before him stands a woman girt with a sword, upright and unafraid. Take in each detail slowly. Nothing here is hurried.

steps.title: The Ancient Speaks
steps.text: The Hierophant turns his face toward you. He is an Ancient, crowned and sceptred, his hand raised in blessing, and his expression is hard to read; there may be a smile at its edge. Approach with respect and stand before him, beside the woman with the sword. Greet him in whatever way feels right, then ask plainly: what does this path teach? Be still and listen. The answer may come as words, an image, a gesture, or a sensation in the body; it may come from him, from the woman, or from the child. He may place something in your hands. Receive whatever is given without judging it, and remember it exactly. Should anything feel wrong, trace Vau in red-orange before it and watch how it responds. If nothing seems to come, simply stay. Silence here is also an answer.

steps.title: The First Nail over the Abyss
steps.text: When the exchange feels complete, bow, and pass through a door beside the oriel window. The road continues upward and soon becomes a bridge, fastened plank by plank with iron nails, reaching out over a gulf whose bottom you cannot see. This is the Abyss. Go no farther than the first nail. Stand there and look across. Far beyond the gulf glows a soft grey light, iridescent like pearl and shot through with pure soft blue. Within it great wheels turn slowly, set with the stars of the zodiac, and you may sense a single outpouring force, immense and without shape. This is Chokmah, Wisdom, where the name Yah is spoken and the archangel Ratziel keeps the secrets of God. Let the sight touch you. Do not cross. When you have seen what you can, turn back.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Retrace your steps at the same unhurried pace: off the bridge, through the door, past the throne where the Hierophant sits as before, and out beneath the oriel window. Walk down the road, through the gate on its iron nails, past the topaz and the weeping storax. The giant trees go by one by one; the bull still grazes. Ahead the veil appears, painted with Atu V. Pass through it into the blue square temple of Chesed. Turn to face the veil and trace Vau upon it once more, this time watching the red-orange letter dim and sink back into the cloth until the curtain hangs closed and still. Turn to Tzadkiel and thank the archangel for keeping the way. Bow to the enthroned king. Let the blue walls grow faint and transparent, and dissolve.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Become aware of your body in the chair: the weight of your hands on your thighs, your feet on the floor, the air moving at your nostrils. Take three deeper breaths, a little quicker than before. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and let the sounds of the room return. When you are ready, open your eyes and look around, naming a few ordinary objects to yourself. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor, twice. Before you do anything else, write down what you saw, heard and received, especially the Hierophant's answer and anything placed in your hands, while the memory is fresh. Later, compare your notes with the symbol list for this path.

closing: Perform a banishing: the Star Ruby or the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram. Stamp your feet, drink water, and eat something plain and earthy such as bread or root vegetables. Write the session into your magical record: date, time, planetary day and hour, what you saw and heard, the Hierophant's answer, and anything you were given. Then check your notes against the symbol list, marking what matched, what did not, and what surprised you. Leave interpretation for a day or two, and do not repeat the working on the same day.

tunnel.reflection: The averse face of Vau is the nail that fixes instead of joins: teaching hardened into dogma, ritual performed with no one listening, authority that demands obedience instead of awakening understanding. Consider, as reflection and not invocation, where your own practice has set like a driven nail: beliefs you no longer test, voices you defer to in place of your own inner hearing. Work the day-side path of the Hierophant first, and more than once, before sitting with this; contemplate it from a steady footing and banish afterwards.

notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth tarot and Liber 777: Vau, Taurus, Atu V The Hierophant. Path 16 is not affected by the He/Tzaddi swap. This path crosses the Abyss (Chesed to Chokmah), so the journey stops at the first nail of the bridge and glimpses Chokmah across the gulf instead of approaching its temple; treat it as an act of listening, not a claim to any grade. Chokmah's glimpse uses its 777 colours: grey (Queen), pure soft blue (King), pearl-grey iridescence (Emperor). Digest corrections (the source table had rows bleeding in from path 17, Gemini): Greek gods: 777 gives only (Hera) for Taurus; 'Castor and Pollux, Apollo the Diviner' belong to path 17. Trump title: 'The Magus of the Eternal'; 'The Children of the Voice: the Oracle of the Mighty Gods' is the title of Atu VI, The Lovers (path 17). Magical power: 'The Secret of Physical Strength'; the power of being in two or more places at once, and of prophecy, belongs to path 17. Magical weapon: 'The Labour of Preparation (the Throne and Altar)'; its first half had slipped into path 15's row in the digest. The 'correct design' field is truncated: 777 describes an Ancient between the pillars, crowned, sceptred and blessing threefold, adored by four living creatures. Thoth-card details are paraphrased from the Harris painting. The gate, the topaz in the gatepost and the nailed bridge are visualisation devices, not traditional teaching.

title: The Path of the Oracle
summary: The seventeenth path runs from Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Tree, across the Abyss to Binah. It is attributed to Zain (the sword), to Gemini and to Atu VI The Lovers. Working it develops discrimination and union together: the ability to divide things clearly, to hold two opposites without collapsing either one, and to let a true answer emerge where they meet.

prepare.incense: Wormwood (777 col. XLII). Burn only a small pinch on charcoal, because the smoke is harsh, and ventilate the room afterwards. Olibanum (frankincense), the perfume of Tiphareth, is a gentler companion or substitute.
prepare.candle: An orange candle (the King scale of Zain) on a pale mauve cloth (the Queen scale of Zain). Two candles side by side suit Gemini if you like.
prepare.stone: Iceland spar (clear optical calcite, which doubles whatever you see through it), tourmaline or alexandrite (777 col. XL). Hold it in your left hand or set it on the altar in front of you.
prepare.facing: East. Golden Dawn practice gives East to Air, and Gemini is an Air sign. East is also the quarter of the rising sun of Tiphareth.
prepare.notes: Wednesday is a good day (Mercury rules Gemini), as is any time the Moon is in Gemini. A small tripod or three-legged stand holding the stone or the incense echoes the path's weapon. Work seated upright. This path crosses the Abyss to Binah, so the script stops at the threshold and does not enter. Keep your journal ready, and write before you check the correspondences.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright on a firm chair with your feet flat on the floor and your hands resting palm-down on your thighs. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. This is a path of Air, and the lungs belong to it, so let your attention rest on them. Feel them fill from the base upward and empty from the top down, the two sides of the chest moving together as a pair. Round by round, let the body soften: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, hands, belly, legs and feet. Let the faint bitterness of the incense mark the edge of the ordinary room. When the breathing has become steady and unforced, rest there for a while.

steps.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
steps.text: A six-sided hall of gold forms around you. Its walls glow with the clear yellow of the Queen scale. The light has no single source, as if the air itself were sunlit. The floor is warm underfoot. In the centre stands an altar shaped as a double cube and draped in white, with a small flame burning steadily on it. Above the altar the image of this sphere shifts gently as you watch: a majestic king, then a child, then a god with arms outstretched as on a cross. It settles into whichever form is clearest to you. Breathe in the sweet resin of olibanum. Vibrate the God-name so that it fills all six walls: Yod He Vau He Eloah va-Daath. Call the archangel: Raphael. A tall figure in yellow touched with violet stands beside you, and the air feels fresh and healing. Ask Raphael to guard the temple and your return.

steps.title: The Veil of the Lovers
steps.text: A curtain hangs in the eastern wall, painted with Atu VI, The Lovers. A hooded figure spreads his arms over a crowned king and queen. There are a lion and an eagle, two children, a winged egg with a serpent wound around it, and a winged archer overhead, all beneath an arch of swords. Stand in front of the curtain. With your right forefinger, trace the letter Zain in bright orange light: a single upright stroke topped by a short crossbar, like a sword standing on its point. Vibrate its name: Zain. As the sound fades, the painted figures seem to breathe. The curtain parts down its centre into two equal halves. Step between them and let them close behind you.

steps.title: The Twin Roads
steps.text: You are standing on a road washed in orange light, bright and restless as the air at noon. After a few paces the road divides into two lanes running side by side, separated only by a thin line of light. Then they join, then divide again, over and over. Walk in whichever lane you choose, and notice that you can see the other one clearly the whole time. A light wind moves constantly, carrying voices you cannot quite make out. A magpie watches you from a post, black and white at once. Further along, hybrid creatures wander calmly: a striped horse, a bird that cannot fly. Orchids grow along the verges. The old text calls this the Disposing Intelligence, which disposes the upright toward faith. Notice what in you is being sorted and set in order.

steps.title: The Royal Marriage
steps.text: The roads join for the last time in a hall under a high arch of swords, their blades pointing down, bright and quiet. The scene from the veil stands alive before you. A dark king crowned with gold holds a lance, and a red lion walks beside him. A pale queen crowned with silver holds a cup, and an eagle as white as frost stands beside her. A hooded figure between and above them extends his arms over both, and their hands are joined beneath his. Two children, one dark and one fair, stand at their feet holding flowers and a club. In the centre of the floor rests an egg with wings, a serpent wound around it. At the very top, a winged child draws a bow. Two women's shapes are half-seen at the edges, one pale and one dark. Take it all in slowly.

steps.title: The Tripod
steps.text: Beyond the pair, in a quieter recess, a bronze tripod stands over a shallow bowl. A thin thread of bitter smoke rises from it: wormwood. This is the seat of the oracle, the tripod of Apollo the Diviner. Breathe slowly. Feel your lungs take in the smoke-scented air and give it back, one movement in two halves. Look up through the arch and you see two bright stars close together. They are Castor and Pollux, the twins of Gemini, one mortal and one immortal in the old story, who chose to share their fate. A clear crystal lies on the rim of the bowl, and through it everything appears twice. Beside it, a darker stone changes colour as the light shifts, from green to red. Notice how everything here comes in pairs.

steps.title: The Officiant
steps.text: The hooded figure turns from the king and queen and comes toward you. His robe is covered in fine writing you cannot read, and his face stays in the shadow of the hood. He stands before you with his arms crossed on his breast in the Sign of Osiris Risen, then lowers them and waits. Greet him in whatever way feels right. Ask plainly: What does this path teach me? Then be still. The answer may come as words, as an image in the smoke of the tripod, as a feeling in the chest, or as a long silence. All of these are acceptable. You may be given a symbol or a word to carry back. Receive whatever comes without interpreting it yet. You may ask one more question. Then thank him and stay quietly in his presence until you are ready to go on.

steps.title: The Threshold of Binah
steps.text: Past the tripod the road climbs, and the orange light cools and thins. The air grows very still, and the wind of the lower path has dropped entirely. The road ends at an edge. Before you lies a great gulf that ordinary sight cannot cross. Stay on this side of it. On the far side, faint and immense, stands a temple of black stone rimmed with dark crimson. Behind it lies a sea without waves, as deep as night. You may sense a vast, patient understanding coming from there, in which the pairs you have just seen do not seem opposed at all. The name Tzaphkiel may come to mind. Do not step forward or try to cross. Look, receive whatever impression comes, and then bow.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Turn and walk back down the path. Pass the tripod and its thread of smoke. As you pass the royal pair beneath the arch of swords, bow to the hooded figure. The roads divide and rejoin under your feet, and the magpie, the orchids and the wind slip by. Ahead you see the two halves of the curtain. Step between them into the golden hall of Tiphareth. Turn to face the veil: the orange letter Zain still hangs before it. Trace it again in reverse and watch it fade until only the painted cloth remains. Turn to Raphael and give thanks for guarding the temple and your way. Let the archangel, the image above the altar and the golden hall fade quietly.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Come back to the body in the chair. Feel your weight, your feet on the floor and, if you are holding it, the stone in your hand. Let the breath become ordinary again, no longer counted, and notice how your two lungs have been working together all this time. Listen to the sounds of the room and beyond it, and notice the smell of the air. Move your fingers and toes and stretch your neck gently. When you are ready, open your eyes, look around and name a few ordinary things you see. Stamp your feet lightly on the floor three times. You are here, in your own time and place.
