closing: Perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or Liber XXV (the Star Ruby) if that is your practice. Stamp your feet firmly, drink water and eat something simple. Put out the candle and air the room of wormwood smoke. Write the record straight away: date, time, the Moon's sign, what you saw, heard and felt, and any word or symbol you received. Only then compare it with the symbol list, marking what matches the correspondences and what does not. Over the next few days, notice any choices or pairings that come up and add them to the record.

tunnel.reflection: In Grant's Nightside scheme, Zamradiel holds the seventeenth tunnel. Its averse face is division for its own sake: the sword that only cuts apart, the broken union, the mind that weighs every pair of options until it can choose neither, the twin who turns on the other. Consider where your own discrimination has become endless splitting or indecision, and what it would take for the sword to serve a union instead of preventing one. Treat this as reflection, not invocation, and work the day-side path until it is familiar before you turn toward its shadow.

notes: Attribution: Crowley and the Golden Dawn agree on this path: Zain, Gemini, Atu VI The Lovers, path 17 joining Tiphareth (6) and Binah (3). The He/Tzaddi swap does not affect it. Crowley heads the card 'The Lovers (or The Brothers)' and pairs it with Atu XIV Art, with the marriage here and its consummation there. Corrections to the digest, which had shifted rows: (1) The trump title field held a fragment of Atu VII's title. The title of Atu VI is 'The Children of the Voice: the Oracle of the Mighty Gods'. (2) The animals field mixed in Cheth's creatures (Crab, Turtle, Sphinx, Whale), which belong to path 18. The 777 animals for Zain are Magpie and hybrids [Parrot, Zebra, Penguin]. (3) The Greek gods field was truncated. The full entry is Castor and Pollux, Apollo the Diviner [Eros]. (4) Magical powers: 777 gives 'Being in two or more places at one time' as well as Prophecy. (5) Tiphareth's vision field was cut short. It is the Vision of the Harmony of Things (Mysteries of the Crucifixion) [Beatific Vision]. Other points: this path crosses the Abyss, so the journey only glimpses Binah from the threshold. Alternative guides are Apollo the Diviner or the twins Castor and Pollux. The tunnel genius name comes from the Qliphothic genii of Crowley's Liber 231, as Grant uses them.

title: The Path of the Grail-Bearer
summary: The eighteenth path joins Geburah, the sphere of Mars and Severity, to Binah, the Great Mother beyond the Abyss. It is attributed to Cheth (the fence), to Cancer and to Atu VII The Chariot. Working it builds the discipline of the vessel: a self that is armoured and ordered so that it can carry something holy without spilling it, not so that it can conquer.

prepare.incense: Onycha, the path perfume in 777 col. XLII. Benzoin or storax are the usual practical substitutes. If you want to mark the starting sphere, burn a pinch of tobacco (777's perfume for Geburah) before you begin.
prepare.candle: An amber candle (the King scale of Cheth) on a maroon cloth (the Queen scale of Cheth). You can add a scarlet candle (the Queen scale of Geburah) for the starting temple.
prepare.stone: A piece of amber (777 col. XL). Hold it in your left hand or set it on the altar in front of you.
prepare.facing: West. Golden Dawn practice gives West to Water, and Cancer is a Water sign.
prepare.notes: Monday is a good day (the Moon rules Cancer), as is any time the Moon is in Cancer. A cup of water on the altar echoes the Grail. Work seated upright, not lying down. This path crosses the Abyss to Binah, so the script stops at the threshold and does not enter. Keep your journal within reach, and write up the vision before you look at the symbol list.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair with your feet flat on the floor and your hands resting on your thighs. Keep your spine tall but not strained. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let each round be a little slower than the one before. As you breathe, let your attention travel down the body. The scalp softens, the jaw unclenches, the shoulders drop away from the ears, the belly loosens and the legs grow heavy. Notice the weight of the amber in your hand, or its place on the altar before you, and the faint scent of the incense. Let the sounds of the room recede without pushing them away. When the breath has found its own rhythm, rest in it for a while before going on.

steps.title: The Temple of Geburah
steps.text: A five-sided hall forms around you. Its walls are scarlet, the Queen-scale colour of Geburah. The light inside is hot and clear, as if it came from a forge you cannot see. The floor is dark iron and cool under your feet. In the centre stands a plain altar with a sword laid flat on it. Beyond the altar stands the magical image of this sphere, perfectly still: a mighty warrior in a chariot, armed and crowned. Breathe in the dry, sharp air. Now vibrate the God-name, letting it roll from your chest out to all five walls: Elohim Gibor. Feel the hall answer. Call the archangel: Kamael. A tall figure forms in scarlet flecked with green, a sword at rest in its hands. Ask Kamael to guard the temple and your way back.

steps.title: The Veil of the Chariot
steps.text: A heavy curtain hangs in the western wall of the hall. Atu VII, The Chariot, is painted on it: an armoured figure under a deep blue canopy holding a glowing cup, with four strange beasts resting in front of him and scarlet wheels at his sides. Stand in front of the curtain. With your right forefinger, trace the letter Cheth in the air before it in clear amber light. It is two upright strokes joined by a roof across the top, like a gateway or a fenced yard. Vibrate its name: Cheth. The letter hangs there, glowing. The painted cloth ripples as if a tide were moving it, and a gap opens in its centre. Step through and feel the curtain fall closed behind you.

steps.title: The Warded Road
steps.text: You are standing on a road bathed in amber light, warm and dense, like sunlight through resin. Low walls run along both sides, close enough to touch. This is the fence of Cheth, the enclosure that makes a path a path. Beyond the left-hand wall lies a shoreline under a large, pale moon, and the tide draws in and out. At the water's edge a crab moves sideways over the wet stones, carrying its house on its back. A little further on, a turtle rests with its head drawn in. The air smells faintly of the sea and of the incense in your room. Walk slowly. Notice that the walls hold you rather than confine you. Let yourself settle into the pace of the road.

steps.title: The Chariot at Rest
steps.text: The road widens into a courtyard, and the Chariot stands before you. It is not moving. Four sphinxes lie in front of it. Look at each one in turn: every sphinx is made from the same four creatures (bull, lion, eagle and man), combined differently each time. There are no reins. Above the car, four pillars hold up a canopy the deep blue of night, scattered with stars. The wheels are scarlet and still carry the heat of Geburah behind you. The Charioteer sits within, clad in amber armour marked with ten stars. A crab rises from his helm, and his visor is closed, so no face can be seen. In his hands he holds a wide cup of violet stone, and at its centre a light turns slowly, like blood lit from within.

steps.title: The House of Influence
steps.text: Stand quietly near the Chariot and notice what flows here. The old text calls this path the Intelligence of the House of Influence, a place through which abundance passes downward and is received. You may feel it as a gentle pressure from above, as if the night of the canopy were pouring slowly into the cup. At the edge of the courtyard a pool holds a single lotus, still closed at its tip. Beside the pool a black scarab, Khephra, rolls a dark red sun along the ground, pushing it through the night toward a morning you cannot yet see. Somewhere nearby, a furnace glows behind an iron door, and you may feel its warmth in your stomach, the body's own furnace. A piece of amber lies on the ground with something small held unchanged inside it. Look at each image and let it be what it is.

steps.title: The Charioteer Speaks
steps.text: Approach the Chariot and stand in front of the sphinxes. Give whatever sign of respect feels right to you, such as a bow or a hand over the heart. The visor does not open, but you sense attention turning toward you from behind it. Ask plainly: What does this path teach me? Then wait. The answer may come as words from inside the helm, as a picture in the cup, as a feeling in the body, or as nothing at all for a long while. Any of these is acceptable. You may be offered a symbol or a word to carry back. Receive whatever comes without arguing with it or adding to it. If you wish, ask one more question. Then thank the Charioteer and stay silent in his presence until you are ready to go on.

steps.title: The Threshold of Binah
steps.text: Beyond the Chariot the road climbs, and the amber light deepens toward crimson, then toward a darkness that is not empty. The walls of the road end at a ledge. In front of you is a gulf you cannot see across with ordinary sight. Stay on this side of it. Far across it, a temple of black stone rises out of stillness, faintly crimson at its edges. Behind it lies a vast dark sea, completely calm. The shape of the Grail you have just seen echoes that sea. You may sense a great, patient presence, feminine and very old, and the name Tzaphkiel may come to you. Do not step forward and do not try to enter. Simply look, and let whatever you glimpse of Understanding leave its mark on you. Then bow.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Turn and walk back down the road. As you pass the Chariot, bow to the Charioteer. Pass the pool with its lotus, the scarab with its sun and the warm iron door. The walls rise again on either side, and the moonlit shore, the turtle and the crab slide past. Ahead you see the back of the painted curtain. Step through it into the scarlet hall of Geburah. Turn to face the curtain: the amber letter Cheth still hangs there. Trace it again in reverse and watch it fade until only the painted cloth remains. Turn to Kamael and give thanks for guarding the temple and your way. Let the archangel, the image and the hall fade gently into darkness.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Become aware of your body in the chair: its weight, the pressure of your feet on the floor and, if you are holding it, the amber in your hand. Let the breath deepen, then let it become ordinary breathing again, no longer counted. Notice the smell of the room, the sounds outside and the temperature of the air on your skin. Move your fingers and toes and roll your shoulders. When you are ready, open your eyes, look around the room and name a few ordinary objects to yourself. Stamp your feet lightly on the floor three times. You are here, in your own time and place.

closing: Perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or Liber XXV (the Star Ruby) if that is your practice. Stamp your feet firmly, drink a glass of water and eat something plain. Snuff the candle and put the amber away somewhere apart from everyday things. Write the record straight away: date, time, the Moon's sign, what you saw, heard and felt, and any word or symbol you received. Only then compare it with the symbol list, marking what matches the correspondences, what does not, and what surprised you.

tunnel.reflection: In Kenneth Grant's Nightside scheme, Characith holds the eighteenth tunnel. Its averse face is the vehicle without a driver: momentum with no one at the centre, armour that has grown into a prison, and the power of casting enchantments turned inward as self-enchantment. Consider where your own discipline has become a shell that keeps life out instead of a vessel that carries it. Treat this as reflection, not invocation, and work the day-side path until it is familiar before you turn toward its shadow.

notes: Attribution: Crowley and the Golden Dawn agree on this path: Cheth, Cancer, Atu VII The Chariot, path 18 joining Geburah (5) and Binah (3). The He/Tzaddi swap does not affect it. Corrections to the digest, which had shifted rows: (1) The Sepher Yetzirah field ran path 19 into path 18. The eighteenth path is only the Intelligence of the House of Influence; the Intelligence of all the Activities of the Spiritual Beings belongs to Teth. (2) The animals field held Teth's creatures (lion, cat, tiger, serpent). The 777 animals for Cheth are Crab, Turtle, Sphinx [Whale, all Beasts of Transport], and they had drifted into path 17's row. (3) The magical weapons field included Teth's Discipline (Preliminary) and Phoenix. Cheth's weapons are the Furnace [Cup or Holy Graal]. (4) The trump title was truncated. The full title is 'The Child of the Powers of the Waters: the Lord of the Triumph of Light', and its first half had slipped into path 17's row. (5) Geburah's vision field ran into Tiphareth's. Geburah's is the Vision of Power. Other points: this path crosses the Abyss, so the journey only glimpses Binah from the threshold. Alternative guide god-forms from 777 are Khephra and Apollo the Charioteer. The tunnel genius name comes from the Qliphothic genii of Crowley's Liber 231, as Grant uses them. 418 as the full spelling of Cheth is Crowley's own gematria, not Golden Dawn doctrine.

title: The Path of the Lion and the Cup
summary: Path 19 runs level across the Tree from Geburah (Mars, Severity) to Chesed (Jupiter, Mercy), through Teth the serpent, Leo, and Crowley's Atu XI Lust. It reconciles force and grace. Working it develops courage felt as joy, and the skill of guiding vital, animal energy through love rather than suppression.

prepare.incense: Olibanum (frankincense), the 777 col. XLII perfume of path 19. A pinch of tobacco, 777's perfume for Geburah, is optional for the Geburah temple.
prepare.candle: A greenish-yellow candle (King scale of path 19) on a deep purple cloth (Queen scale of path 19). A scarlet candle for Geburah (its Queen scale) is optional.
prepare.stone: Cat's eye
prepare.facing: South, because Leo is fixed Fire. East, the usual temple orientation, also works.
prepare.notes: Work on a Sunday or in an hour of the Sun (Leo's ruler). Come to it rested and fed, not hungry or agitated, because this path stirs vitality and appetite. Banish first (LBRP or Star Ruby). Put a sunflower on the altar if one is in season, and keep a glass of water within reach. Keep the journal and the symbols checklist nearby, but don't read the checklist until afterwards. Allow 30-40 minutes, including reading time.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright, feet flat on the floor, hands resting open on your thighs. Close your eyes and begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count steady and easy. Let the breath settle into the centre of your chest, and feel your heart beating beneath it, patient and strong. With each exhalation release a little more tension — brow, jaw, throat, shoulders, hands, belly, hips, legs. If restlessness or heat rises in the body, do not suppress it; notice it and let it ride on the breath, the way a rider sits a willing horse. Let the sounds of the room fade into the distance. You are relaxed, awake, and ready.

steps.title: The Temple of Geburah
steps.text: Around you a temple rises: a five-sided hall whose walls burn a deep, clean scarlet, the Queen-scale colour of Geburah. At its heart stands a stone altar, and smoke rises from it with a dry, sharp scent. On the altar lie the implements of this sphere — a sword, a spear, a scourge, and a chain — set out with precision, nothing wasted. Behind the altar, in the red light, stands the image of the sphere: a mighty warrior in a chariot, armed and crowned. Take your place before the altar. Breathe in fully and vibrate the Name so that the walls ring with it: Elohim Gibor. Then call the archangel: Kamael. Sense a stern, upright presence taking its place beside you, clear-eyed and without malice. Ask Kamael to guard your crossing and your return.

steps.title: The Veil of Lust
steps.text: In the wall that faces toward the Pillar of Mercy hangs a curtain painted with Atu XI, Lust, as it appears in the Thoth deck: a woman astride a lion-beast of many heads, leaning back in rapture, lifting high a cup that burns with light. Stand before it and raise your hand. Trace the letter Teth in the air — a rounded form that curls back into itself, like a serpent coiled with its head turned inward. Draw it in clear greenish-yellow light, the King-scale colour of this path, and let it hang there glowing. Vibrate its name: Teth. The letter brightens and seems to breathe; the painted cup catches its light. The curtain draws aside. Step through, carrying Kamael's steadiness at your back.

steps.title: The Level Road
steps.text: You step out onto open land beneath a high, hot sky. This road does not climb; it runs level, straight across the Tree, from the fortress of Severity to the palace of Mercy. The air is full of a greenish-yellow radiance, like midsummer sunlight through young leaves. Golden earth and long grass stretch away on either side, and the ground is warm beneath your feet. Where shadows fall they are tinted deep purple, the Queen-scale colour of the path. Sunflowers stand in rows along the way, their heavy faces turned toward the sun. This is Leo, fixed Fire: heat that does not flicker but endures. Feel it settle into your chest. Your heart beats with it, strong and even, and you walk on at an easy pace.

steps.title: Serpent and Stone
steps.text: A low wall of sun-warmed stone runs beside the road, and set into it, like eyes, are smooth rounded gems across which a single line of light slides as you pass: cat's eye, the stone of this path. You feel watched, though not unkindly. A serpent crosses the road ahead, unhurried, its scales gleaming green-gold, and slips into the grass. Teth is the serpent — coiled, sinuous life that renews itself by shedding its skin. The Sepher Yetzirah names this the Intelligence of the Secret of all Spiritual Activities, the hidden current moving beneath every living impulse. Notice what stirs in your own body as you walk: warmth, desire, eagerness, unease. Treat each as a creature you are coming to know, not an enemy to drive out.

steps.title: The Lion
steps.text: Ahead, on a flat rock in full sun, lies a lion. It is enormous and completely at ease, its mane dark gold, its long tail moving like a serpent. It lifts its head and looks at you. Stay where you are and breathe. Notice what you feel — awe, fear, excitement, the wish to flee or the wish to master it. Do neither. Let your breath slow and your heart open toward the animal as toward a great force of nature that is also part of you. The old lists give this path the power of training wild beasts; it begins here, with unhurried recognition. Courage, on this path, is an open heart in the presence of power. When the lion rises and comes toward you, walk beside it and let it lead.

steps.title: The Woman and the Beast
steps.text: The lion brings you to a place where the road widens into a sun-bright court, and there she waits: a woman, naked and radiant, riding a great beast of many heads, the reins held lightly in one hand, the other lifting a cup that glows red-gold. Her face is full of joy, and nothing in her power is strained. This is the figure of the trump. She may instead appear as a lion-headed goddess, Sekhet or Pasht; accept the form that comes. If you wish to test the vision, trace the letter Teth between you in greenish-yellow light: a true image grows brighter and clearer; if it blurs or coarsens, withdraw with courtesy. If it holds, greet her, ask what this path has to teach you now, and ask for a word, image, or gift to carry back. Then wait in silence and receive whatever comes, without shaping it.

steps.title: The Threshold of Chesed
steps.text: When the exchange is complete, thank her, and thank the lion. The road runs on a little further and ends at a tall doorway in a wall of pale stone. Stand on the threshold and look within, but do not cross. You glimpse the temple of Chesed: a four-square hall of calm, deep blue, the Queen-scale colour, rising to violet in the vaults. After the heat of the plain the air is cool, and it carries the scent of cedar. Far off, a mighty king sits crowned and enthroned, and brilliant beings move about him — the Chashmalim. You may sense the archangel Tzadkiel and hear, faintly, the Name El. Here force is held in generous order; this is the sphere of the Vision of Love. Take in what you are shown, then bow and turn back.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Walk back along the level road, past the sun-bright court, the rock where the lion lay, the wall set with cat's-eye stones, the sunflowers and the warm grass. The greenish-yellow light deepens gradually toward red as the veil of Geburah comes into view. Step through into the five-sided temple. Turn and face the curtain, and see the letter Teth still glowing there. Retrace it in reverse, and watch it sink into the painted card until only the image of Lust remains. The curtain falls still. Turn to Kamael and thank the archangel for keeping watch; feel that stern, clear presence withdraw. Stand a moment in the scarlet hall, upright and whole.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Let the temple of Geburah fade, its red light drawing down into a steady warmth in your chest, and from there into your feet and the floor beneath you. Feel the weight of your body in the chair, your hands on your thighs, your feet on the ground. Take three slow, full breaths. Hear the room around you. Stretch your fingers and toes, roll your neck and shoulders, and open your eyes. Look deliberately at the altar — the candle, the stone, the curling smoke — and name each thing to yourself. If you feel overheated, restless, or elated, sit quietly until it settles. You are fully returned. Reach for your journal before you speak.

symbols.symbol: a woman riding a seven-headed lion-beast
a cup (the Graal) lifted high and glowing

symbols.source: 777 col. XXXVIII (Lion, Kerub of Fire); Leo

symbols.symbol: a lion-headed or cat goddess (Sekhet, Pasht, Mau)
heat or a strong beating in the heart
taming or training a wild animal

closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram (or the Star Ruby), then stamp firmly on the floor to mark the end. Drink water and eat something substantial. If you feel charged or restless, take a short walk before you sit down to write. Journal straight away: date, time, conditions, the full sequence of images, how the lion behaved, the guide's form, and the word or gift you received. Then compare your record with the symbols list (what agrees, what is missing, what surprised you) without bending the vision to fit. Over the next day, notice any heat, desire, anger or elation. Effects of this path often show up in mood and appetite, and observing them is part of the training.

tunnel.reflection: Reversed, this path is appetite with no rider: the lion let loose, an ecstasy that devours instead of illuminating, force that mistakes itself for freedom. As a reflection, not an invocation, consider where passion drives you rather than being ridden with love, and where suppressing it has only made the beast hungrier. Work the day-side path of Teth first, and approach the Tunnel of Temphioth only as a meditation on that shadow.

notes: Thoth numbering: in Crowley's deck this trump is Atu XI Lust. The Golden Dawn and Waite call it VIII Strength. The Golden Dawn had moved Strength to VIII and Justice to XI so that the trumps follow the order of the letters. Crowley went back to the older Marseille numbering (XI Lust, VIII Adjustment) and kept Teth/Leo on Lust and Lamed/Libra on Adjustment. Unlike the He/Tzaddi swap on paths 15 and 28, this exchange does not change the path attribution: Teth, Leo, Geburah to Chesed, exactly as in the Golden Dawn. The digest's 'atu: VIII' is corrected to XI for the Thoth deck; the digest's tunnel record already reads 'XI Lust'. Corrections to the digest: (1) The trump title is only 'The Daughter of the Flaming Sword'. The rest of that field ('The Prophet of the Eternal, the Magus of the...') belongs to Atu IX, path 20. (2) The 'Correct design' text (a smiling woman holding a lion's jaws) is 777's Golden Dawn image. The journey uses the Crowley-Harris Thoth design: the Woman riding the many-headed Beast and holding up the Graal. (3) The Sepher Yetzirah field was cut short to 'Being'; it is restored as the Intelligence of the Secret of all Spiritual Activities (Westcott: of all the activities of the spiritual beings). (4) The animals field ('Woman]]') and magical weapons field ('Wand]]') are truncated. 777 gives Lion (Kerub of Fire) for animals and 'The Discipline (Preliminary)' for weapons; the lion was used. (5) Geburah's vision field has text shifted in from Tiphareth. Geburah's vision is The Vision of Power; 'the Vision of the Harmony of Things' belongs to Tiphareth. The digest's 'Legendary orders of being' entry could not be verified and was not used. Everything else was used as given: colours, Ra-Hoor-Khuit/Pasht/Sekhet/Mau, Horus, Narasimha, Demeter, sunflower, cat's eye, olibanum, and the power of training wild beasts. Kamael is spelled כמאל as in the Golden Dawn. Tunnel genius Temphioth is from Grant's Nightside of Eden, after Liber 231.

title: The Path of the Hidden Lamp
summary: Path 20 joins Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree, to Chesed, the throne of Jupiter, through Yod, the hand and the seed-point of the Name, under Virgo and Atu IX The Hermit. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Intelligence of Will. Working it teaches the self-contained inner light, and develops solitude without isolation, discretion, and the patience of a seed carried through to its harvest.

prepare.incense: Narcissus (777 col. XLII, the perfume of path 20). Olibanum may also be lit for the Tiphareth temple.
prepare.candle: A yellowish-green candle (King scale of path 20) on a slate-grey cloth (Queen scale of path 20). A gold candle for Tiphareth (its Queen scale) is optional.
prepare.stone: Peridot
prepare.facing: East, the usual direction for temple work. Some prefer North because Virgo is an Earth sign.
prepare.notes: Work in the evening, ideally on a Wednesday or in an hour of Mercury (Virgo's ruler). Banish first (LBRP or Star Ruby). Keep the room silent, since this path belongs to Harpocrates, the god of silence. Put a small piece of bread on the altar to eat at the close (777 lists the Bread among the path's weapons). Keep the journal and the symbols checklist nearby, but don't read the checklist until afterwards. Allow 30-40 minutes, including reading time.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright on a firm chair or cushion, spine straight, hands resting on your thighs. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the count become slow and even. With each exhalation, loosen one region of the body in turn — the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs — until the chair is holding you rather than you holding yourself. Feel the length of your back, the column that keeps you upright without strain. Let the sounds of the room recede. Notice the faint scent of narcissus and the single flame before you, then let them sink into the background. You are quiet, alert, and unhurried.

steps.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
steps.text: Around you a temple takes shape: a six-sided hall whose walls glow a warm, clear gold, the Queen-scale colour of Tiphareth. The light seems to come from everywhere at once, as if you stood inside the sun. At the centre stands a cubical altar where olibanum smoulders, and above it hangs a rose-pink radiance, the King-scale colour, like dawn behind the gold. On the eastern wall you see the images of this sphere: a majestic king, a child, a god with arms outstretched upon a cross. Stand before the altar. Draw a full breath and vibrate the Name slowly, letting it resonate through the hall: YHVH Eloah va-Daath. Then call the archangel: Raphael. Feel a presence gather in the east, tall and luminous, carrying the sense of clean moving air and healing. Ask Raphael to watch over your passage and your return.

steps.title: The Veil of the Hermit
steps.text: In the wall that faces toward the Pillar of Mercy, at the top of a few low steps, hangs a heavy curtain painted with Atu IX, The Hermit, as it appears in the Thoth deck: a hooded, cloaked figure bending over a lamp in which a small sun burns, ripe wheat rising around him. Climb the steps and stand before it. Raise your hand and trace the letter Yod in the air — a single small stroke, like a seed or a tongue of flame. Draw it in yellowish-green light, the King-scale colour of the path, and see it hang there, bright and clear. Vibrate its name: Yod. The letter pulses once. The curtain stirs and parts at its centre. Step through, keeping the sense of Raphael's presence behind you.

steps.title: The Road Among the Grain
steps.text: You stand at the foot of a long road that climbs gently away from the sun behind you. The air is filled with a soft yellowish-green light, like new leaves at evening. The ground underfoot is slate-grey stone, cool and dry — the Queen-scale colour of the path — softened here and there by grey-green lichen. On either side lie fields of ripe wheat, heavy-eared and still, for this is Virgo, the harvest sign, earth that has carried its seed to fullness. No wind moves the grain. You are alone, and the solitude feels chosen rather than imposed. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this the Intelligence of Will; here you feel your will not as strain but as quiet direction, like a seed that knows which way is up. Walk slowly, and let your steps set the pace of your breath.

steps.title: Flower, Stone and Hand
steps.text: As the road rises, the fields give way to thin mountain grass. Small white flowers grow along the verge: snowdrops bowing their heads, tall lilies, narcissi whose sweetness is the perfume of this path. Pause and let it reach you. In the grey rock beside you a vein of olive-green crystal catches the light — peridot, the stone of this path. Lay your palm on it and feel its steady coolness. Then look at your own hand. Yod means hand, and this is the path of the hand that holds, withholds, and gives at the right time. Further up, the stone has been worn into shallow steps by those who walked here before you, each of them alone. Ahead, a small cave opens in the hillside, and a faint light glows within.

steps.title: The Terrace of the Egg
steps.text: Before the cave the ground levels into a small terrace, and the design of the trump comes alive around you. On a flat stone rests an egg, pale and smooth, with a serpent coiled about it: the Orphic egg, the world held in potential, life waiting inside its shell. At the edge of the terrace lies a great dog with three heads, calm and watchful, the guardian of the underworld who now follows the one who carries the light. Above, the sky deepens toward twilight and the first stars appear. Let each thing be exactly as it is, and do not force detail. If something appears that you did not expect, note it quietly for later. The silence here is thick and friendly, the silence of someone who has nothing to prove.

steps.title: The Hermit
steps.text: From the mouth of the cave a figure emerges: an ancient one wrapped in a cloak and deep hood, bent a little, carrying a lamp. Inside the lamp burns not a flame but a small, perfect sun — the light of Tiphareth carried inward. The guide may instead come as a silent child with a finger to the lips, Heru-pa-kraath; accept the form that appears. If you wish to test it, trace the Yod between you in yellowish-green light: a true image steadies or brightens; if it blurs or coarsens instead, withdraw with courtesy and return. If it holds, greet the guide and ask plainly what this path has to teach you now, and ask for a word, an image, or a gift to carry back. Then be silent. Whatever comes, or does not come, is yours. Stay with it.

steps.title: The Threshold of Chesed
steps.text: When the meeting is complete, thank your guide. The lamp is lifted toward the summit, and you walk on a little further, to where the road ends at a doorway cut into the rock. Stand on the threshold and look, but do not enter. Beyond lies the temple of Chesed: a four-square hall of deep, calm blue, the Queen-scale colour, shading upward into violet. The air carries the dry, resinous scent of cedar. Far within, a mighty king sits crowned and enthroned, and brilliant presences move around him — the Chashmalim. You may sense the archangel Tzadkiel, and hear the Name El sounding faintly, like a bell across water. This is the sphere of Jupiter, of generous and ordered grace. Take in what you are shown, then bow and turn back.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Walk back down the road the way you came: past the cave and its terrace, the dog and the egg, the vein of peridot, the white flowers, the silent fields of grain. The light warms toward gold as you descend, and ahead the radiance of Tiphareth glows through the curtain. Step through the veil into the six-sided temple. Turn and face the curtain, and see the letter Yod still hanging there. Retrace it in reverse and watch it fade into the cloth until only the painted trump remains. The curtain falls still. Turn to the east, thank Raphael for guarding your passage, and feel the archangel's presence withdraw. Stand a moment in the golden hall, whole and present.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Let the temple of Tiphareth soften and fade, its gold light folding down into a warm point at the centre of your chest. Become aware of your body sitting in the room: the weight of your hands, the contact of your feet with the floor, the length of your back. Take three deliberate, deeper breaths. Hear the ordinary sounds around you. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and when you are ready, open your eyes. Look at the flame, the peridot, the bread on the altar, and name each to yourself. You are fully returned. Before speaking or doing anything else, reach for your journal.
