closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram (or the Star Ruby), then stamp once, firmly, on the floor to mark the end. Eat the bread from the altar, or something plain, and drink water. Put out the candle deliberately. Journal straight away, before interpreting anything: date, time, conditions, the whole sequence of images, the guide's form, and the word or gift you received. Then check your record against the symbols list. Note what agrees, what is missing and what is unexpected, but do not change the vision to make it fit. Leave at least a day before working another path, and keep the guide's word in mind as you go about the next day.

tunnel.reflection: On its averse side, the Hermit's solitude hardens into isolation. The lamp is hoarded, the seed is held back until it withers, and discretion turns into secrecy for its own sake. As a reflection, and never as an evocation, consider where your own withdrawal has stopped nourishing anything and has become a wall. Work and journal the day-side path of Yod first, and then approach the Tunnel of Yamatu only as a meditation on that shadow, not as a journey into it.

notes: Thoth and Golden Dawn agree on this path: Yod, Virgo, Atu IX The Hermit, Tiphareth to Chesed. The He/Tzaddi swap (paths 15 and 28) does not affect it. Corrections to the digest: (1) The 'Correct design of the Tarot trump' field runs on into the Atu X description ('A wheel of six shafts...'). That text belongs to path 21 and was left out. (2) The trump title is cut short. 777 gives 'The Prophet of the Eternal, the Magus of the Voice of Power'; the first half of that title slipped into the path 19 record. (3) Tiphareth's vision field is scrambled by a shifted row. The standard entry is 'The Vision of the Harmony of Things (also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion)', with the Beatific Vision as Crowley's addition; the first half was found under Geburah in the path 19 digest. (4) The col. V divine-name entry ('(34) אל אב (4) אבא') is not garbled. It reads El Ab, 'God the Father' (gematria 34), and Abba, 'Father' (gematria 4), which fits Yod as the Father-letter of YHVH. It is a correspondence for contemplation, not a name for vibration, so the journey vibrates only the Tiphareth God-name and the letter name. Everything else in the digest agrees with 777 and was used: colours, Sepher Yetzirah 'Intelligence of Will', Isis as Virgin, Heru-pa-kraath, plants, peridot, narcissus, lamp/wand/bread, invisibility and parthenogenesis. Heru-pa-kraath (Harpocrates) is offered as an alternative form for the guide. The Tiphareth and Chesed temples use their Queen-scale colours. The Crowley-Harris Thoth design (lamp holding a sun, Orphic egg, Cerberus, wheat) replaces 777's older Golden Dawn description. Tunnel genius Yamatu is from Grant's Nightside of Eden, after Liber 231.

title: The Path of the Turning Wheel
summary: Path 21 runs from Netzach, the green sphere of Venus, to Chesed, the blue sphere of Jupiter. It falls under the letter Kaph (the palm), the planet Jupiter and Atu X Fortune. Working it builds the ability to meet change and expansion without clutching. You learn to see rising and falling circumstance as a rhythm, and to find the still hub within it where grace and opportunity can be received.

prepare.incense: Saffron (777 col. XLII: saffron and all generous odours). Cedar suits the Chesed threshold, and a little benzoin or rose may be burned at the Netzach opening.
prepare.candle: A violet candle (King scale of path 21) on a blue cloth (Queen scale of path 21). An emerald-green candle for the Netzach temple (its Queen scale) is optional.
prepare.stone: Amethyst or lapis lazuli (777 col. XL).
prepare.facing: East, the usual quarter for opening path work. If you know where Jupiter is in the sky, you may face it instead.
prepare.notes: Best on a Thursday or in an hour of Jupiter. Banish first (LBRP or Star Ruby) and do the Qabalistic Cross. The journey starts in Netzach, so prior work on the paths that reach it (29, 28, 27) helps make the temple vivid. Study the Thoth Atu X Fortune for a few minutes before closing your eyes. Keep your diary within reach.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright with your spine straight and your hands resting open on your thighs, palms up. Kaph is the palm, and you begin with it open. Close your eyes. Start the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Notice that the breath is a small wheel, turning through its four quarters without effort once it is set going. With each exhalation loosen something: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. If thoughts rise, let them ride round and drop away like objects carried on a rim. When the rhythm is steady and the body is heavy and at ease, let the outer room recede.

steps.title: The Temple of Netzach
steps.text: You stand in a seven-sided temple of emerald. The walls are green stone veined with paler green, and the light is soft and moving, like sun through leaves. Roses climb the seven pillars, and the air holds benzoin, rose and a trace of red sandalwood. At the centre, on a low altar, burns a single lamp. Beyond it stands the image of this sphere, a beautiful naked woman, calm and unashamed. Face the altar and vibrate the Name so that it rolls around the seven walls: YHVH Tzabaoth. The green deepens and brightens in reply. Then call the archangel: Haniel. A presence gathers in green and rose-coloured light, warm and clear-eyed. Ask Haniel to watch over your going and your return.

steps.title: The Veil of Fortune
steps.text: In the far wall, where a distant blue glimmers through, hangs a curtain. As you approach, its painting comes clear: Atu X, Fortune. A great wheel of ten spokes stands against a violet sky scattered with stars and split by lightning. A Sphinx holding a sword crouches on its rim. One figure climbs up one side while another tumbles down the other. Raise your hand and trace the letter Kaph before the curtain: a stroke across the top that curves round and returns along the base, like a cupped palm: כ. See it shine in clear violet. Vibrate its name: Kaph. The painted wheel gives one slow turn, and the curtain parts at its hub. Step through. The emerald warmth falls behind you, and the air becomes wide and cool.

steps.title: The Open Country
steps.text: You are on a broad road climbing through open country beneath an enormous sky. Overhead the light is violet deepening to royal blue, with bands of gold streaming up from the horizon, so the whole sky seems blue rayed with yellow. The land rolls in long slopes, and there is more room here than you are used to. Great oaks stand alone in the fields, each with space around it. A line of tall poplars marks a far stream, their leaves flickering silver and green. The air smells warm and rich, of saffron and resin. Walk slowly. Notice that the road, though it climbs, bends gently all the while, so that over a long distance you travel around as well as up.

steps.title: Eagle, Fig and Stone
steps.text: An eagle circles high above, riding the warm air in wide rings, rising without a single wingbeat simply by turning. By the roadside grows a fig tree heavy with fruit, and at its roots a low bush of hyssop, blue-flowered and sharply fragrant. Among the roots lie stones: purple amethyst and deep blue lapis flecked with gold. Stoop and rest one in your open palm. Feel its cool weight. Kaph is the palm, the hand that receives and the hand that grasps. Notice which your hand wants to do, then set the stone back. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this road the Intelligence of Conciliation and Reward, the channel that receives the divine influence and passes it on as blessing to all that exists. Let the phrase settle as you walk.

steps.title: The Wheel
steps.text: The road brings you to the foot of a vast wheel standing upright against the sky, its rim taller than any tower, its ten spokes glinting. It turns slowly, and the heavens seem to turn with it: stars wheel past behind it and thin lightning flickers down from above. On one side a jackal-headed figure, Hermanubis, clambers upward on the rim, quick and eager. On the other a dark, heavy figure, Typhon, slides downward, slow and inevitable. At the summit sits the Sphinx, sword in hand, and though the rim moves beneath it, it keeps its place at the top. Stand close and feel the rhythm of the turning in your chest. Then let your attention travel inward along a spoke to the hub, which scarcely moves at all.

steps.title: The Guide: Amoun
steps.text: Beside the axle, where the ground does not move, a tall figure waits. His skin is the blue of lapis and his crown is a pair of tall straight plumes. He holds a long sceptre forked at the foot and topped with an animal's head. This is Amoun-Ra, the Hidden One, whom the Greeks called Zeus Ammon. Approach with open palms. If anything about him feels false, trace Kaph in violet between you. A true figure grows clearer and a false one fades. Greet him and ask what this path has to teach you. Then be quiet and wait. He may speak, point to the wheel, or place something in your hand. Receive whatever comes without shaping it, and remember it.

steps.title: The Threshold of Chesed
steps.text: When the exchange feels complete, thank him in your own way. He lifts the sceptre toward the road that continues beyond the wheel. Follow it a short way uphill until the violet clears into a deep, luminous blue. Ahead stands a four-square temple of blue stone with its doors open, the scent of cedar flowing out. Through the doorway you glimpse a mighty king, crowned and enthroned, in a light that feels generous, orderly and immense. The Name El seems to sound from the stone itself, and Tzadkiel's presence fills the hall. This is Chesed, Mercy, the sphere of Jupiter. Do not enter. Stand on the threshold, let its breadth wash over you like open sky, and take only the impression.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Turn back. Walk down the road, past Amoun beside the axle, past the great wheel still turning with its climber and its faller, past the fig, the hyssop and the stones among the roots. The eagle circles overhead as you descend, and the road curves gently beneath your feet. The violet sky softens, and the curtain appears ahead, its painted wheel on this side too. Pass through, then turn to face it. Trace the Kaph once more in violet, and watch the letter sink into the fabric as the curtain seals and stills. You stand again in the seven-sided emerald temple of Netzach, rose scent around you, the lamp burning on the altar. Turn to Haniel, thank the archangel for watching over your journey, and see the presence withdraw into the green light.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Let the green temple dissolve into the darkness behind your eyelids. Feel your body again: the chair beneath you, your feet on the floor, your hands resting palm-up on your thighs. Close your hands gently, so the palm that opened at the start now closes. Take three slower, deeper breaths without counting. Move your fingers and toes, stretch, and open your eyes. Look around the room and name a few plain objects. Press your feet firmly into the floor or stamp them. Then, before anything else, write down what the guide gave you and everything you met on the road: colours, creatures, plants, stones, figures, words. Only afterwards compare them with the symbol list for this path.

symbols.symbol: violet light; the letter Kaph traced in violet
bright blue sky rayed with yellow
a ten-spoked wheel turning against a starry sky with lightning
a Sphinx with a sword at the summit (Sulphur)
breadth, abundance, the glyph of Jupiter

closing: Once you are back in the room, perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram (or the Star Ruby) and seal with the Qabalistic Cross. Stamp your feet, drink water and eat something simple and grounding. In your magical diary, record the date, time, planetary hour and the Moon's sign, the guide's word or symbol, and everything you met on the path. Then check it against the symbol list. Mark what matched, what did not, and anything that felt invented rather than received. Come back to the entry after a day or two before drawing conclusions.

tunnel.reflection: In its averse aspect the wheel becomes a cage. Fortune is felt as something that merely happens to you, rising and falling with no lesson, and Jupiter's expansion swells into a hunger for ascendancy for its own sake. Consider where you have handed your will over to luck, or clung to a rise as though it could never turn. Treat this as reflection, not invocation. Work the day-side path of Fortune first, so the still hub is familiar before you look at the rim from below.

notes: Thoth attribution: Kaph, Jupiter, Atu X Fortune ('Wheel of Fortune' in the Golden Dawn). No swap or renumbering affects this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) Trump title: 777 gives 'The Lord of the Forces of Life'. The trailing 'The Daughter of the Lords of Truth...' belongs to Atu VIII (path 22) and shifted in from the next row. (2) Greek gods: 777 gives Zeus for Kaph. 'Themis, Minos, Aeacus and [Rhadamanthus]' belongs to Lamed (path 22). (3) Archangel: the digest spells Haniel האניאל, with an extra Aleph. The usual Golden Dawn spelling, הניאל, is used here. (4) The digest's 'Legendary orders of being' entry (Incubi, Nightmares) could not be confirmed against 777, so it is left out of the symbol list. Kaph's value is 20, and its final form ך is 500. The Sepher Yetzirah title is usually rendered 'Intelligence of Conciliation and Reward', and its text is paraphrased here. Netzach's God-name is YHVH Tzabaoth; Elohim Tzabaoth belongs to Hod. Assigning Sulphur, Mercury and Salt to the Sphinx, Hermanubis and Typhon follows Crowley's account of the card. Amoun-Ra is 777's Egyptian attribution. The description of him (lapis-blue skin, double plumes, was-sceptre) follows standard Egyptian iconography. The tunnel genius Kurgasiax is the Liber 231 genius of Kaph, which Kenneth Grant used as the name for the Tunnel of Set in Nightside of Eden.

title: The Path of the Balance
summary: Path 22 joins Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree, to Geburah, the fiery sphere of Mars. It runs under the letter Lamed (the ox-goad), the sign Libra and Atu VIII Adjustment. Working it builds a felt sense of equilibrium: every act is met by its exact consequence, and Geburah's sword and the scales of Maat belong together. It trains clear judgement without cruelty, and honesty without self-punishment.

prepare.incense: Galbanum, the 777 perfume for Lamed (col. XLII). A little olibanum may be burned at the opening for the Tiphareth temple.
prepare.candle: An emerald-green candle (King scale of path 22) on a blue altar cloth (Queen scale of path 22). A gold or yellow candle for Tiphareth (its Queen scale) is optional.
prepare.stone: Emerald (777 col. XL). Any clear green stone can stand in if you have no emerald.
prepare.facing: East. Libra is a cardinal Air sign, and Golden Dawn practice gives Air to the East. East is also the usual quarter for opening from Tiphareth.
prepare.notes: Best on a Friday or in an hour of Venus (Libra's ruler), or while the Sun or Moon is in Libra. Banish first (LBRP or Star Ruby) and do the Qabalistic Cross. The journey starts in Tiphareth, so it helps to have worked the lower paths into Tiphareth (25, 26, 24) first. Study the Thoth Atu VIII for a few minutes before closing your eyes. Keep your diary and pen within reach, and use a soft timer if you are not being read to.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the count become even and unforced. With each exhalation release one region of the body: the brow, the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the thighs, the feet. Now notice where you lean. Perhaps more weight sits on one hip, or one side of the neck is tighter than the other. Adjust gently until you feel centred. This path is about balance, and it begins with the body's own. When the breath runs by itself, let the room fade to a quiet background.

steps.title: The Temple of Tiphareth
steps.text: You stand in a six-sided temple of gold. Light comes from everywhere at once, warm and even, like late-morning sun through amber glass. The floor is polished yellow stone, and a banner of deeper gold hangs on each of the six walls. At the centre stands a double-cube altar with a single lamp. Behind it, carved in relief, three images seem to melt into one another as you look: a majestic king, a child, a god with arms stretched upon a cross. A thread of olibanum smoke rises straight up. Face the altar, draw a full breath, and vibrate the Name so it fills the space: YHVH Eloah va-Daath. Feel the gold brighten in answer. Then call the archangel: Raphael. A tall presence gathers beside the altar, robed in gold edged with violet, bringing the smell of clean air. Ask Raphael to guard your going and your return.

steps.title: The Veil of Adjustment
steps.text: In the wall ahead, where a faint red glow shows through from beyond, hangs a heavy curtain. As you approach, its painting sharpens: Atu VIII, Adjustment. A slender masked woman stands poised on the tips of her toes, both hands on the hilt of a long sword pointed down before her, two scale pans hanging from the plumes of her crown. The whole picture is washed in blue and green. Raise your hand and trace the letter Lamed in the air before the curtain, the tall upper stroke first, then the body bending and sweeping down: ל. See it burn in clear emerald green. Vibrate its name: Lamed. The letter flares, and the curtain parts along the line of the painted sword. Step through. The gold falls away behind you, and cool green air touches your face.

steps.title: The Level Road
steps.text: You stand on a straight road of pale stone running gently uphill, perfectly level from side to side. On either hand stretches a plain of emerald grass, so even it might have been cut with one stroke. The sky is a deep blue-green, like sea over white sand, and the light is cool and steady, casting short, clean shadows. Nothing leans here. The few trees stand plumb, and the grass tilts neither way. A sharp, green, resinous scent hangs in the air: galbanum. As you walk, notice your own gait. Where you favour one leg, the road seems to rise a little on that side. When you correct yourself, it lies flat again. Walk on until your steps fall evenly, left and right, each the same length and the same weight.

steps.title: Goad, Elephant and Aloe
steps.text: Ahead, an elephant stands across the road, grey and patient, its trunk swinging slowly. It is so heavy the ground ought to tilt beneath it, yet everything stays level. As you come near it steps aside. Where it stood grows a clump of aloe, thick-leaved, a broken tip beading with bitter, healing sap. Beside the aloe lies a long staff with an iron point: an ox-goad. Pick it up and feel its weight. It is not a weapon but a prompt, the small sharp touch that keeps a strong beast moving along its furrow. Lamed is this goad, and Aleph, the ox, is what it drives. Together they spell AL. Lay the goad back where you found it. Recall that the Sepher Yetzirah names this the Faithful Intelligence, by which spiritual virtues are increased.

steps.title: The Balance
steps.text: The road opens into a round court paved in squares of pale green and deep blue. In its centre hangs a great balance, its beam as long as a ship, its chains rising out of sight into the blue-green sky. In one pan rests an Alpha, in the other an Omega, both cut from emerald, and the beam is perfectly still. Set into the paving beneath it is an equal-armed cross. At the edges of the court rest four spheres, two bright and two dark, holding one another in equilibrium. This is Libra, cardinal Air, the equinox where day and night are equal. Stand beneath the beam and recall one recent action of your own. Let it be weighed: what led to it, and what followed. Do not judge it. Simply watch the pans register it and come to rest.

steps.title: The Guide: Maat
steps.text: Beyond the balance, on a low dais, you see her: the woman of the trump, tall and slender, masked, balanced on the very tips of her toes. The ostrich plumes of Maat rise from her head, and from them hang the scales. Both her hands rest on the hilt of the great sword, its point touching the ground between her feet. She seems utterly still, yet you sense constant, minute motion, as if she corrects for every tremor in the world. If anything about her feels false, trace Lamed in emerald between you. A true figure grows clearer and a false one fades. Greet her as Maat and ask what this path has to teach you. Then wait. She may speak, show you something, or place something in your hands. Receive it without shaping it, and remember it.

steps.title: The Threshold of Geburah
steps.text: When the exchange feels complete, thank her. She turns her masked face slightly toward the road beyond. Follow it a short way to where the green light warms through orange into scarlet. Ahead rises a five-sided temple of red stone with its doors open. Through them you glimpse a mighty warrior in his chariot, armed and crowned, and feel a dry heat like a forge. A strong scent of tobacco leaf drifts out. The Name Elohim Gibor hangs in the air, and within is the presence of Kamael. This is Geburah, Severity, the sphere of Mars, home of the sword you have just seen held so carefully. Do not enter. Stand on the threshold, let the force touch your face like warmth from a fire, and take only the impression.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Now turn around. Walk back down the road, past the woman with the sword, across the chequered court beneath the still balance, past the aloe and the place where the elephant stood. Keep your steps even. The emerald plain and the blue-green sky carry you gently downward. Soon the curtain appears, painted on this side with the same trump. Pass through it, then turn and face it. Trace the Lamed once more in emerald green, and watch the letter sink into the fabric as the curtain falls closed and still. You stand again in the gold temple of Tiphareth, olibanum in the air, the lamp burning on the altar. Turn to Raphael and thank the archangel for guarding the way. See the presence withdraw into the light.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Let the golden temple fade, like sunlight seen through closed eyelids. Become aware of your body in the chair: its weight, the floor under your feet, the air on your hands and face. Take three slow, deeper breaths and let the fourfold count go. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and when you are ready, open your eyes. Look around the room and name a few ordinary things you can see. Stamp your feet lightly or press your palms flat against the floor. Before doing anything else, write down what the guide said or showed you, and every colour, animal, object and word you met. Only then compare your notes with the symbol list for this path.

symbols.symbol: emerald-green light; the letter Lamed traced in emerald
a slender masked woman poised on tiptoe
scales hanging from a plumed crown, Alpha and Omega in the pans
a balance, equinox, day equal to night
judges of the dead: Themis, Minos, Aeacus, Rhadamanthus; Yama

closing: Once you are back in the room, perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram (or the Star Ruby, if that is your practice) and seal with the Qabalistic Cross. Stamp your feet, drink water and eat something plain. In your magical diary, record the date, time, planetary hour and the Moon's sign, the guide's word or symbol, and everything you saw. Then check it against the symbol list. Note what matched, what did not, and anything that felt imposed rather than received. Leave interpretation for a day or two.

tunnel.reflection: The averse face of Lamed is the tampered scale. It is judgement that has lost its measure, karma imagined as revenge, and the sword used to settle scores rather than to adjust. Consider where your own sense of balance hardens into punishment, of others or of yourself, and where 'justice' has become a mask for resentment. Hold this as a question to look at in daylight, not a current to call up. Work the day-side path of Adjustment first, until true equilibrium is familiar enough that you can recognise its distortion.

notes: Thoth attribution: Lamed, Libra, Atu VIII Adjustment. The digest's 'atu XI' is the Golden Dawn numbering. The Golden Dawn put Justice at XI and Strength at VIII so the numbers followed the letter order. Crowley kept the letter and sign attributions but went back to the older numbering: Adjustment VIII, Lust XI. This is only a renumbering. It is not the He/Tzaddi swap, which affects paths 15 and 28. Corrections to the digest: (1) Greek gods: 777 gives Themis, Minos, Aeacus and Rhadamanthus for Lamed. The digest split this list across paths 21 and 22 because of a row shift. (2) Trump title: 777's full title for this trump is 'The Daughter of the Lords of Truth; the Ruler of the Balance'. Its first half had shifted into path 21's row. (3) Magical weapon: only the Cross of Equilibrium belongs to Lamed. 'The Cup and Cross of Suffering' is Mem's (path 23) and spilled into this row, as did 'The Hanged Man—[Cups]' in the general tarot attribution. (4) The digest's 'Divine name of the path: אל' is not used. It is probably another row shift: El is the divine name of Jupiter and Chesed, so it would belong to Kaph (path 21), while 777 usually gives the zodiacal paths permutations of YHVH. This could not be confirmed against the table. Geburah's God-name, seen at the threshold, is אלהים גבור, Elohim Gibor. Reading AL as the ox (Aleph) plus the goad (Lamed), with Adjustment as the Fool's complement, is Crowley's own Thelemic interpretation, not an older tradition. The Sepher Yetzirah text is paraphrased. The tunnel genius Lafcursiax is the Liber 231 genius of Lamed, which Kenneth Grant used as the name for the Tunnel of Set in Nightside of Eden.

title: The Path of the Still Deep
summary: The 23rd path runs straight up the Pillar of Severity from Hod, the sphere of Mercury and the analytical mind, to Geburah, the sphere of Mars and just force, through Mem, the Mother letter of Water, and Atu XII, the Hanged Man. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Stable Intelligence, and it teaches the intellect to suspend itself: to be turned upside down and held steady by something deeper than its own cleverness. Working it builds surrender without collapse, and a calm that can meet severity without being swept away.

prepare.incense: Onycha and myrrh (777 col. XLII). Onycha is hard to find; myrrh alone, or myrrh with a little storax (Hod's perfume), will do.
prepare.candle: A deep blue candle (the path's King scale, 777 col. XV) on a sea-green cloth (the path's Queen scale, col. XVI). An orange light for the Hod temple (Hod's Queen scale) is optional.
prepare.stone: Beryl or aquamarine (777 col. XL)
prepare.facing: West, the quarter of Water in the Golden Dawn and Pentagram-ritual arrangement
prepare.notes: Set a cup of clean water or wine on the altar; 777 gives the path's weapon as the Cup and Cross of Suffering, and Wine. Banish before you begin (Star Ruby or LBRP). Any time is suitable, and some prefer the Moon in a water sign. Keep a journal and pen within reach. If water or inversion imagery distresses you, keep the causeway firm under your feet and skip the optional sharing of the Hanged Man's view in step 7.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright with your spine straight, feet flat on the floor and hands resting palms-down on your thighs. Close your eyes and begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold full for four, out for four, hold empty for four. After several rounds let the count grow soft and automatic. Now relax the body in stages, following the breath downward: forehead and eyes, jaw and tongue, throat, shoulders, arms, chest, belly, hips, legs and feet. Imagine the body slowly filling with still, cool water, rising from the soles to the crown until nothing in you moves except the breath. Let thoughts pass like reflections on the surface. When you feel quiet and heavy, notice a warm orange glow beginning in the darkness in front of you.

steps.title: The Temple of Hod
steps.text: The orange glow resolves into walls. You stand in an eight-sided temple of clear, bright orange. The floor is laid in black and white squares, and the air is sweet with the balsam of storax. On the central altar lie a caduceus and a shallow dish of quicksilver that trembles and shines at the smallest movement. Shelves of books and scrolls line the walls. At the far side stands the magical image of this sphere: a hermaphrodite, poised and composed, holding both natures without strain. Stand before the altar and vibrate the God-name of Hod, Elohim Tzabaoth, and feel the sound fill all eight walls. Then call the archangel: Mikael. Wait until you sense a tall, alert presence beside you, bright as polished metal, and ask Mikael to guard the way you are about to take.

steps.title: The Veil of Mem
steps.text: Turn to the wall through which the path rises, straight up the pillar toward Geburah. A curtain hangs there, painted with Atu XII: a man hanging head-downward from an ankh, legs crossed, arms spread, against a grid of green tablets above dark water. Look at it until the image is clear and steady. Raise your hand and trace the letter Mem, מ, on the curtain stroke by stroke in deep blue light. Vibrate its name: Mem. Let your lips close on the final M and become a hum that fills your skull and chest; the Sepher Yetzirah calls Mem the humming letter, the mother of Water. The letter glows deep and steady, the painted water seems to ripple, and the curtain parts. Glance back at Mikael, then step through.

steps.title: The Causeway
steps.text: You stand at the edge of water. A great still lake, or a windless sea, stretches ahead under a deep blue sky. The path runs straight out across it as a narrow causeway of sea-green stone, level with the surface. Near your feet the water is clear. Farther out it darkens to deep olive-green and then to depths you cannot see. The cool air smells of myrrh and of something older and sharper, like shell and resin: onycha. Lotus flowers rest on the surface in scattered clusters, white flecked with purple, their stems going down out of sight. Begin to walk. Your footsteps make no echo. The stillness is not empty; it is the stillness of something very large holding its breath. Let your own breath slow to match it.

steps.title: The Hanged Man
steps.text: Midway across, the causeway ends at a tall ankh of pale stone rising from the water, its loop dark against the sky. A man hangs from it by one foot, head downward, just above the surface. His free leg crosses behind the other, so his legs form a cross. His arms spread outward and down, so that together with his head they form a triangle pointing at the water. Flat green tablets stand behind him in a grid, and you can see where he is nailed to them, yet his face is calm and his eyes are open. Beneath his shaven head, in the darker water, a serpent lies coiled and quiet. Stand before him. Notice any urge to rescue him, or to look away. Neither is needed. Simply watch how completely he is held.

steps.title: The Stable Intelligence
steps.text: Walk slowly around the ankh. Now and then the surface stirs: pale shapes of nymphs and undines rise, look at you without speaking, and sink again. Far overhead an eagle circles. On the stone at the foot of the ankh a scorpion rests, and below it the serpent turns its head. Eagle, snake and scorpion together are the Kerub of Water. Set into the stone is a beryl, clear sea-green, like a drop of this water made solid. Lay your hand on it. Feel that nothing here wobbles; even the hanging man is held in perfect balance. This is the Stable Intelligence, the constancy that runs through all the spheres and keeps each true to itself. Notice a quiet settling in your belly, in the organs of nourishment, as if something long clenched in you were finally allowed to rest and be fed.

steps.title: Asar
steps.text: Go back and stand before the hanging figure. You may know him now by an older name: Asar, Osiris, the god given to the waters who does not stay lost in them. He turns his calm, inverted gaze to you. Greet him. If you wish to test the vision, trace Mem before him in deep blue light; a true guide stays steady in it. A cup stands on the stone at the foot of the ankh, and if it is offered, you may drink. Then ask him what this path has to teach you, and what in you needs to be turned upside down. Wait. Let the answer come in whatever form it takes: a word, an image, a sensation, a change in how you see him or yourself, or silence. If you feel drawn to, you may share his view for a while, the world hanging from the water, but do not force anything. Take the time you need.

steps.title: The Threshold of Geburah
steps.text: When the exchange feels complete, thank him. Beyond the ankh the causeway continues, and now it begins to climb out of the water, rising straight ahead. Walk until the air grows warmer and drier and the blue sky takes on an edge of orange. The path ends at a threshold of red stone. Beyond it you glimpse the fifth sphere: a five-sided hall of scarlet, lit by a fierce, clean light. You may hear iron ringing and wheels turning, see a mighty warrior in his chariot, armed and crowned, and smell tobacco smoke on the hot air. Do not cross. Stand at the threshold and notice how the calm you carry from the water meets that force.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Turn and walk back along the causeway. The air cools, and the path sinks until it runs level with the still surface again. Pass the ankh and the hanging man, and bow to him as you go. Pass the lotus flowers, white flecked with purple. Keep the word or symbol you received safe. The curtain appears ahead with the deep blue Mem still shining on it. Step through into the orange temple of Hod. Turn to face the curtain and trace the letter in reverse, drawing it back until it fades and the painted card grows still. Turn to Mikael and thank the archangel for guarding the way. Let the eight walls soften into orange light, and the light into darkness.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Let the water you imagined filling your body drain slowly downward, through your legs and feet into the floor, and leave the body its ordinary weight and warmth. Take a few rounds of the fourfold breath, then let the breath return to its natural rhythm. Feel the seat beneath you, the floor under your feet, the air on your skin. Listen to the sounds of the room and of the world beyond it. Move your fingers and toes, and stretch your neck and shoulders. Say your name, the date and where you are. Open your eyes and look at a few ordinary objects, naming each one. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor. You are back, fully present, and the path is closed.

symbols.symbol: deep olive-green; white flecked with purple (Emperor and Empress scales)
still water, a lake or a calm sea
a man hanging head-downward from an ankh
crossed legs above a triangle of arms and head
a grid of green tablets; nails
a serpent coiled below the figure
eagle, snake and scorpion (Kerub of Water)
Asar (Osiris) as the Hanged Man; Isis, Ptah, Tum, Auramoth, Hathor

closing: Banish with the Star Ruby or the LBRP. Stamp firmly on the floor and put out the candle. Pour the water away with a word of thanks, or drink the wine. Eat something warm and solid, and wash your hands and face. Record the working right away: date, time, conditions, the vision in order, the word or symbol from Asar, and any bodily sensations, especially in the belly. Afterwards, check your record against the symbol list. Mark what matched, what did not and what surprised you, without revising the vision. Note your dreams for the next few nights.

tunnel.reflection: In the averse aspect the waters stop being a medium of surrender and become a place to disappear: passivity that calls itself acceptance, a mind that has given up its shape instead of offering it. Consider where you may have mistaken stagnation for peace or martyrdom for devotion, and where the Hanged Man's stillness has become a way of never acting. Treat this as contemplation after the day-side path has been worked and grounded, not as a working to enter or invoke.

notes: This journey uses Crowley's Thoth/777 attributions. The He/Tzaddi swap does not affect this path, and the Golden Dawn and Thoth attributions agree: Mem, Water, Atu XII The Hanged Man. Mem is one of the three Mother letters (Aleph, Mem, Shin) of the Sepher Yetzirah. Digest corrections: (1) Hod's God-name was misspelled אלהים בצאות; the correct form is אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (2) Hod's heaven was misspelled כובכ; the correct form is כוכב, Kokab. (3) The digest gives the letter name as מים 'Maim'. That is the word for water, which is the letter's meaning, and a spelling carried in 777-derived tables. The standard spelling of the letter's name is מם, Mem, and that is the name traced and vibrated here. (4) The trump-title field ran into Atu XIII's title. Atu XII is 'The Spirit of the Mighty Waters'; 'The Child of the Great Transformers' belongs to Death. (5) Geburah's vision field was merged with Tiphareth's. Geburah's vision is 'The Vision of Power'; the Vision of the Harmony of Things belongs to Tiphareth. (6) 777 gives this row's magical weapon as 'Cup and Cross of Suffering, Wine'; the digest listed only Wine [Water of Lustration]. (7) 'Queens' in the general Tarot attribution means the four Queens, the court cards of Water grouped with this row in 777 col. XIV; the trump itself is Atu XII. Mikael is Hod's archangel in the Golden Dawn/777 order; some writers swap Mikael and Raphael between Hod and Tiphareth. The guide step includes the Golden Dawn habit of testing a figure by tracing the path's letter before it; this is optional, and it comes before accepting the cup. In The Book of Thoth, Crowley treats the Hanged Man's formula of redemptive sacrifice as belonging mainly to the Old Aeon of Osiris. In Thelemic work the path can be approached as surrendering the ego's control to the deeper Will rather than as sacrifice for its own sake. The Thoth card details (ankh, crossed legs over a triangle, green tablets, nails, serpent below) are described in original words.

title: The Path of the Scythe and the Scarab
summary: The 24th path joins Netzach, the sphere of Venus and the feelings, to Tiphareth, the solar centre of the self, through the letter Nun (Fish), the sign Scorpio and Atu XIII, Death. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Imaginative Intelligence: here the forms the heart has clung to break down so that their essence can pass upward into the Sun. Working it builds the ability to let things end without losing what lived in them, and a steadier relationship with change, decay and renewal.

prepare.incense: Siamese benzoin and opoponax (777 col. XLII). For the Netzach temple you can open with Netzach's own perfume of benzoin, rose and red sandalwood.
prepare.candle: A green-blue candle (the path's King scale, 777 col. XV) on a dull brown cloth (the path's Queen scale, col. XVI). An emerald-green light for the Netzach temple (Netzach's Queen scale) is optional.
prepare.stone: Snakestone, for which an ammonite fossil serves, or greenish turquoise (777 col. XL)
prepare.facing: West. Scorpio is fixed Water, and West is the quarter of Water (the Eagle Kerub) in the Golden Dawn and Pentagram-ritual arrangement. If your temple has a fixed orientation, East is an acceptable default.
prepare.notes: Banish before you begin (Star Ruby or LBRP). A Tuesday (Mars, traditional ruler of Scorpio) or a time with the Moon in Scorpio suits this path, but timing is optional. 777 gives this path the magical weapon 'The Pain of the Obligation' [The Oath], so you may quietly restate your own oath or aspiration before you start. Keep a journal and pen within reach. This path deals with endings and decay. Postpone it during a raw bereavement or a hard low period.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair or on a cushion with your spine straight and your hands resting on your thighs, and close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold full for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count slow and even for several rounds until it runs by itself. On each exhalation let one part of the body let go: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the chest, the belly, the legs, the feet. Feel your weight settle into the seat and the floor. Let the sounds of the room fade without pushing them away. When the body is heavy and quiet and the breath is steady, notice a faint green light starting to gather in the darkness in front of you.

steps.title: The Temple of Netzach
steps.text: The green light widens into a room. You stand in a seven-sided temple whose walls glow a deep, luminous emerald. The floor is cool under your bare feet, and the warm air carries benzoin, rose and red sandalwood. At the centre stands a double-cube altar draped in green, with a single lamp and a bowl of red roses on it. Behind the altar, in a niche, stands the magical image of this sphere: a beautiful naked woman, calm and unashamed. Take a full breath and vibrate the God-name of Netzach, YHVH Tzabaoth, and let it resound from all seven walls. Then call the archangel: Haniel. Wait, and feel a presence gather beside you, tall and bright, in green and rose light. Ask Haniel to watch over the way you are about to take.

steps.title: The Veil of Nun
steps.text: Turn to the wall that faces inward, toward the centre of the Tree. A heavy curtain hangs there, painted with Atu XIII: a crowned skeleton sweeping its scythe through a dark, curling sea of forms. Look at it until the picture holds steady. Then raise your hand and trace the letter Nun, נ, on the curtain in clear green-blue light: the small head, the long downward stroke, the short base turning to the left. Vibrate its name, Nun, and let the sound hum in your chest. The letter brightens, the painted figures seem to stir, and the curtain parts down its centre. Glance back once at Haniel, then step through.

steps.title: The River of the Fish
steps.text: You stand at the foot of a long slope that rises gently ahead under a sky of deep green-blue, the colour of water seen from below. The ground is soft, dull brown earth, damp and rich, smelling of leaf-mould and of the dark, sweet resin of opoponax. A slow river runs beside the path and catches the green-blue light. In its shallows fish are moving, silver shapes turning in the current and working their way upstream, the same way you are going. Cactus and nettle grow along the bank, so walk with your hands at your sides. The air is still and faintly warm, with the warmth of fallen things quietly turning into soil. Begin to walk, and let each step settle into the earth. Nothing on this path hurries. It moves at the pace of decay and growth.

steps.title: The Dancer with the Scythe
steps.text: Ahead, where the path opens into a low meadow, a figure is at work. It is a skeleton, tall and unhurried, wearing the tall plumed crown of Osiris. It swings a great scythe in wide, even arcs, and it is dancing rather than labouring. Where the blade passes, the air curls into dark waves, and bubbles rise in the waves, each holding a small form: a seed, an embryo, a face not yet decided. What the scythe cuts, it also sets moving. At its feet a scorpion rests on a flat stone, a serpent raises its head beside it, and a fish leaps at the river's edge. High above, an eagle turns slowly against the green-blue sky. Stand and watch the rhythm of the blade until it feels less like a threat and more like a pulse.

steps.title: The Imaginative Intelligence
steps.text: The skeleton lets you pass, and the path climbs on beside the river. As you walk, a slow warmth gathers low in your belly, as though your gut were at last digesting something held for a long time. This path rules the intestines, where what is taken in is broken down so it can become you. In the bank lies a coiled fossil shell, a snakestone, beside a chip of greenish turquoise. Pick up the fossil: a living creature, long gone, turned into pattern. This is the Imaginative Intelligence, which gives things their likeness and carries a form's image forward after the form itself is spent. Let something you have outgrown or lost rise gently in memory, and notice what of it stays with you as shape and meaning. Set the stone down. A black beetle with a dark indigo-brown shell crosses in front of you, pushing a small ball of earth. Follow it.

steps.title: Khephra
steps.text: The beetle leads you to a bend in the river where the light begins, very faintly, to warm. There, seated on a rock, is a figure with a man's body and a great scarab in place of a head. This is Khephra, who rolls the sun through the hours of night toward its rising. He holds the ball of earth the beetle brought, and now you see a faint light glowing inside it. Greet him with respect. If you wish to test the vision, trace the letter Nun before him in green-blue light; a true guide stays steady in it. Ask him plainly what this path has to teach you, and what in you is ready to die. Then be silent. Let whatever comes arise in its own way: an image, a word, a feeling, something placed in your hands, or nothing at all. Do not reach for an answer or decide in advance what it should be. Take the time you need.

steps.title: Before Paroketh
steps.text: When the exchange is complete, thank Khephra and take your leave. Walk on up the slope until the path meets a curtain of fine mist, rose-pink and gold, hanging across the way. This is Paroketh, the veil before the sphere of the Adepts. Stop here. Through it you glimpse the sixth sphere: a vast golden radiance, warm on your face like noon, with the outline of a six-sided hall inside it. You may sense the images of Tiphareth, a king in majesty, a child, a figure with arms outstretched, and smell olibanum drifting toward you. Do not cross. It is enough to stand before the veil, let its light fall on you, and feel how naturally this path leads here.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Turn and walk back down the path. Pass the bend of the river and the stones on the bank, then the meadow where the scythe still swings in its slow dance. The fish still turn in the shallows. Keep the word or symbol you were given close to you. Soon the curtain appears ahead, with the green-blue letter Nun still glowing on it. Step through into the emerald temple of Netzach. Turn to face the curtain and trace the letter in reverse, drawing it back until it fades and the painted card grows still. Turn to Haniel and thank the archangel for guarding the way. Watch the green light soften as the temple gently fades around you.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Let the temple dissolve into a soft green glow, and the glow into the ordinary darkness behind your eyelids. Return to the fourfold breath for a few rounds, then let the breath find its natural rhythm. Feel the weight of your body on the seat, the pressure of your feet on the floor, the temperature of the air on your hands and face. Listen to the sounds of the room. Move your fingers and toes, and roll your shoulders. Quietly say your own name, the date and where you are. When you are ready, open your eyes and look around, naming a few objects you see. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor. You are here, in your body and in the present, and the path is closed behind you.

symbols.symbol: dull brown earth or ground (Queen scale)
very dark brown; livid indigo-brown like a black beetle (Emperor and Empress scales)
a skeleton in the crown of Osiris wielding a scythe
bubbles or waves carrying new forms, embryos
scorpion, serpent and eagle (the three forms of Scorpio)
beetle, lobster or crayfish, wolf; reptiles, shark
scent of Siamese benzoin and opoponax
Khephra the scarab; Typhon, Apep, the Merti goddesses
sensations in the gut or intestines
an oath, vow or felt obligation

closing: Perform the Star Ruby or the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram. Stamp your foot firmly on the floor and put out the candle. Eat and drink something substantial, such as bread and something salty, and wash your hands and face in cool water. Write up the working right away: date, time, astrological conditions, what you saw, heard and felt in order, Khephra's word or symbol, and anything unexpected. Only then check your record against the symbol list. Mark honestly what matched, what did not and what surprised you, and do not edit the vision to fit. Note your dreams for the next few nights.

tunnel.reflection: On the night side the same letter becomes a stagnant pool: decay that feeds nothing, and a fascination with endings that curls back on itself like the scorpion turning its sting on its own body. Consider where in you grief, resentment or morbid fascination has stopped composting and started simply to rot, and what it would take to let it move again. Hold this as reflection only, after the day-side path has been worked and grounded. It is not a place to enter or invoke.

notes: This journey uses Crowley's Thoth/777 attributions throughout. The He/Tzaddi swap affects only paths 15 and 28, and the Golden Dawn and Thoth attributions agree here: Nun, Scorpio, Atu XIII Death. Digest corrections: (1) The animal list read 'Scorpio'. 777 col. XXXVIII gives 'Scorpion, Beetle, Lobster or Crayfish, [Wolf]'. (2) The trump-title field ran into the next row. 'The Daughter of the Reconcilers' is the title of Atu XIV (Art/Temperance). Atu XIII is 'The Child of the Great Transformers; the Lord of the Gate of Death'. (3) Tiphareth's vision field was truncated. 777 gives 'The Vision of the Harmony of Things (also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion)', and the digest's bracketed 'Beatific Vision' is a supplementary attribution. Haniel is spelled האניאל as in 777; הניאל is also common. Raphael is Tiphareth's archangel in the Golden Dawn/777 order used here; some later writers swap Raphael and Michael between Tiphareth and Hod. Khephra is the guide, chosen from 777 col. XIX. He fits the path's beetle and its Empress-scale colour 'like a black beetle', and he echoes the Sun of Tiphareth. Typhon and Apep, from the same list, belong more to the averse side. The guide step includes the Golden Dawn habit of testing a figure by tracing the path's letter before it; this is optional. The Thoth card details (Osirian crown, bubbles of new forms, scorpion/serpent/eagle, fish) are described in original words. Snakestone is commonly taken to mean an ammonite fossil.

title: The Arrow through the Rainbow
summary: Path 25 rises straight up the Middle Pillar from Yesod, the Moon's foundation of images, to Tiphareth, the solar centre, by way of Samekh (the Prop), Sagittarius and Atu XIV Art. It is the path of the arrow loosed from the rainbow's bow, and of the alchemical cauldron where fire and water mix into something new. Working it builds single-pointed aspiration, steadiness under testing, and the art of blending your own opposites into a third thing.

prepare.incense: Lign-aloes (777 col. XLII), i.e. agarwood or oud. Jasmine, Yesod's perfume, suits the opening temple.
prepare.candle: Blue (King scale, the path's own colour), or yellow (Queen scale) instead. A violet cloth or candle (Yesod, Queen scale) for the temple you start from.
prepare.stone: Jacinth (777 col. XL). An orange-red zircon or hessonite is the usual modern stand-in.
prepare.facing: South, the quarter of Fire (Sagittarius is mutable Fire), or East if your temple is always set up that way.
prepare.notes: Thursday (Jupiter rules Sagittarius) or Monday (the Moon, for Yesod) suit this working; some practitioners also choose a time when the Sun or Moon is in Sagittarius. Keep Atu XIV in view and study it beforehand. This is one of the three Golden Dawn Portal paths (24, 25, 26), usually worked after paths 32 to 27. It climbs the Middle Pillar directly and crosses the Veil of Paroketh. Allow 30 to 40 minutes including reading time, and keep a journal within reach.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright with your spine straight and your feet flat, hands resting palms-down on your thighs. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold full for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the counting slow and unforced. As you breathe, move your attention down through the body, releasing tension wherever you find it: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. Feel yourself grow heavy and still, your spine rising in a straight line from the seat to the crown. Keep breathing until the breath settles into an even rhythm on its own, then let the counting go and rest.

steps.title: The Temple of Yesod
steps.text: Build the temple of Yesod around you. It has nine sides, and its walls glow a soft violet, the Queen-scale colour of the Foundation. Moonlight falls through an opening in the roof onto a round, still pool at the centre, and the air smells sweet with jasmine. Beside the pool stands the magical image of this sphere: a beautiful naked man, very strong, standing at ease, his strength quiet and complete. Everything in this temple shimmers slightly, the way images do before they settle into form. Breathe in, and vibrate the God-name so that it fills all nine walls: Shaddai El Chai. Then call the archangel of Yesod: Gabriel. Feel a presence gather above the water, cool and clear, robed in silver and blue, holding a cup.

steps.title: The Veil of Samekh
steps.text: A curtain hangs in the wall that leads straight upward along the Middle Pillar. It is painted with Atu XIV, Art: a single two-faced figure pouring fire and water into a golden cauldron, with a lion and an eagle at its feet. Stand before it and trace the letter Samekh in the air in clear, bright blue: ס. Watch the rounded letter close on itself and shine against the cloth. Vibrate its name, letting the sound rise through your body: Samekh. The letter glows, the painted figure seems to breathe, and the curtain parts. As you step through, look back. Above the temple of Yesod a great rainbow arcs across the sky like a drawn bow, and you are the arrow set to its string. Gabriel stays at the threshold. Let the curtain close behind you.

steps.title: The Straight Road
steps.text: You stand at the start of a road that runs ahead without a single bend, climbing gently toward a point of light on the far horizon. The sky is a deep, clear blue, and the plain on either side is green with grass. A stream runs beside the road, thick with rushes whose tall stems rustle in the wind. The air is warm and dry and smells of resinous, woody aloes. This is Sagittarius, mutable Fire ruled by Jupiter. The land is open and wide, and the horizon seems to pull you forward. Begin to walk. Feel the strength in your hips and thighs and the long, easy stride. The road never turns, so your only task is to keep your eyes on the light ahead.

steps.title: Centaur, Arrow and Desert
steps.text: You hear hooves behind you. Horses stream across the plain, manes flying, and a lean hunting dog falls in at your side, matching your pace. Then a centaur draws alongside: a man's torso rising from the powerful body of a horse, a bow across his back. He holds out a single arrow and lets you take it. Feel its weight and its perfect straightness. Its head is a deep orange-red stone, a jacinth, holding the light. Then he wheels away, and the horses and the dog go with him. The green plain thins into pale, open desert. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this the Intelligence of Probation, the place of testing. Nothing dramatic happens here. There is only distance, silence, and the question of whether you will keep walking. Keep walking, the arrow in your hand.

steps.title: The Cauldron of Art
steps.text: At the heart of the desert, in a circle of warm light, the figure of the trump waits. It is one being with two faces, one pale and one dark: the royal couple of the Lovers made one. A stream of fire falls from a torch in one hand, and water pours from a cup in the other. Both fall into a golden cauldron. Where they meet they neither put each other out nor scald each other, but rise together as a glowing vapour. A white lion and a red eagle flank the cauldron, their colours swapped from the Lovers card. A raven perches on a skull on the cauldron. Around the figure, in a disc of light, runs the Latin motto Visita Interiora Terrae Rectificando Invenies Occultum Lapidem: visit the interior of the earth; by rectifying you will find the hidden stone. As you watch, the vapour shimmers with every colour of a peacock's tail. Stand and watch the work.

steps.title: The Figure of Art
steps.text: The figure turns from the cauldron and looks at you with both faces at once. It may also appear as a huntress with a drawn bow, Diana or Artemis, as the old attributions allow. Accept whichever form comes. Greet it, and hold out the arrow the centaur gave you. Ask what this path has to teach you, and what in you needs to be tempered. Then wait in silence. The answer may come as words, as an image in the cauldron's vapour, as a feeling in the body, or as a symbol placed in your hands. It may be very simple. Don't hurry it or shape it. Stay with the figure and whatever comes up, for as long as it lasts.

steps.title: The Threshold of Tiphareth
steps.text: When the exchange is complete, the figure takes your arrow, sets it to a bow and looses it straight up the road. Follow its flight with your eyes, then with your feet. The desert ends at a curtain of shimmering light, the Veil of Paroketh, with a great golden sun blazing through it. Beyond the veil you see a six-sided temple of clear gold, filled with a warm, rosy light, and at its centre your arrow has struck home. Within the brightness you may sense a king, a child, a god offered up. The air is rich with frankincense. Do not cross the veil. Stand at its edge, take in the warmth on your face and chest, and know that this is where the arrow was always pointed. Then lower your eyes.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Turn and go back down the straight road. Thank the figure of Art as you pass the cauldron. Cross the desert, which feels shorter now, and come back to the green plain, the rushes by the stream and the blue sky. The centaur and the dog may greet you as you pass. Ahead you see the painted curtain beneath the arc of the rainbow. Step through into the violet temple of Yesod. Turn and trace the letter Samekh once more in blue over the curtain, then watch it fade and the curtain become solid wall. Stand by the moonlit pool. Thank Gabriel for keeping the threshold, and let the God-name Shaddai El Chai sound once, softly, in your mind.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Let the nine violet walls grow faint and the moonlight fade until only your ordinary sense of the room is left. Feel the chair beneath you, the floor under your feet, the temperature of the air on your skin. Take three slow, full breaths, each one bringing you further back into your body. Notice the sounds around you. Move your fingers and toes, stretch your arms and gently roll your neck. When you are ready, open your eyes and let them rest on something solid and ordinary. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor two or three times, and pat your arms and legs. You are fully here.

raven on a skull; the V.I.T.R.I.O.L. motto

closing: Close with a banishing: the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or the Star Ruby (Liber XXV). Stamp your feet, wash your hands and face, and eat and drink something plain and grounding. Write up the journey at once: date, time, planetary hour, incense, what you saw, what the figure of Art said or gave you, bodily sensations and mood. Check the record against the symbol list below. Note which correspondences turned up without prompting, which did not, and anything that clashed with them. Over the next days, add any theme of tempering, testing or aim that surfaces in dreams or daily life.

tunnel.reflection: The averse face of Samekh is failed alchemy: fire and water forced together before their time, poison where there should be elixir, an arrow loosed without aim that falls short in the desert. Consider where you have mixed things that were not ready, or mistaken restlessness for aspiration, and what your arrow still needs before it can fly true. Contemplate this from ordinary waking awareness, as reflection and not invocation, and only after you have worked the day-side path of Samekh and recorded it.

notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth scheme: Samekh, Sagittarius, Atu XIV Art (called 'Temperance' in the Golden Dawn and Rider-Waite decks), joining Yesod (9) to Tiphareth (6) on the Middle Pillar. The Liber AL I:57 He/Tzaddi (Star/Emperor) exchange does not affect this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) 'Temperence' is spelled Temperance. (2) The trump title was cut short; the full 777 / Golden Dawn title is 'The Daughter of the Reconcilers, the Bringer-forth of Life'. (3) Yesod's grade was given as '2°=9□ Theoricus 1°=10□ Zelator'. That is a shifted row: Yesod is 2°=9□ Theoricus only, and 1°=10□ Zelator belongs to Malkuth. (4) Yesod's perfume 'Jinseng' is the spelling 777 itself uses; it means ginseng. The digest's 'complete practical attribution of Egyptian gods' field is in Coptic script (read as Arōueris, Horus the Elder). Its reading is uncertain, so the script does not use it. Archangels follow the Golden Dawn / 777 order (Gabriel in Yesod, Raphael in Tiphareth). Temples use the Queen scale (Yesod violet, Tiphareth gold), and the letter is traced in the path's King-scale blue. The rainbow-as-bow image comes from the Golden Dawn teaching that Qoph, Shin and Tau (paths 29, 31, 32) spell Qesheth, the bow, from which Samekh's arrow is loosed toward Tiphareth through the Veil of Paroketh. The jacinth arrowhead, the centaur handing over the arrow and the desert of testing are working images, not traditional doctrine. The digest's 'keyword' and 'meditation' lines are the app's editorial synthesis and are not presented as tradition. The tunnel genius Saksaksalim follows Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden (Liber 231).

title: The Path of the Opened Eye
summary: Path 26 joins Hod, the Splendour of the mind, to Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree, by way of Ayin (the Eye), Capricorn and Atu XV The Devil. It is the climb up the mountain of matter in the company of Pan. Working it trains you to see through fixed appearances and the chains you mistake for reality, and to meet raw creative and instinctual force with clear sight and laughter instead of fear or shame.

prepare.incense: Musk or civet (777 col. XLII, which also allows Saturnian perfumes). Use synthetic musk or ambrette seed, not animal products. Storax, Hod's perfume, suits the opening temple.
prepare.candle: Indigo (King scale, the path's own colour) or black (Queen scale) for the path. An orange candle or cloth (Hod, Queen scale) for the temple you start from.
prepare.stone: Black diamond (777 col. XL). Any dark faceted stone can stand in as a focus.
prepare.facing: North, the quarter of Earth (Capricorn is cardinal Earth), or East if your temple is always set up that way.
prepare.notes: Saturday (Saturn rules Capricorn) or Wednesday (Mercury, for Hod) suit this working; some practitioners also choose a time when the Sun or Moon is in Capricorn. Keep Atu XV in view and study it before you begin. In the Golden Dawn this is one of the three Portal paths (24, 25, 26), usually worked after paths 32 to 27. Allow 30 to 40 minutes including reading time, and keep a journal and pen within reach.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat and hands resting on your thighs, or take the god-form posture if you know it. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count slow and even. With each out-breath, let one part of the body let go: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs. Notice your weight settling down into the seat and the floor. Thoughts will pass. Let them go by like traffic heard through a closed window. When the breath keeps its rhythm without effort, stop counting and rest in it for a while.

steps.title: The Temple of Hod
steps.text: A temple forms around you. It has eight sides, and its walls glow a clear, warm orange, the Queen-scale colour of Hod. The floor is laid in black and white squares, and the air smells of sweet storax resin. An altar stands at the centre. Above it hangs the magical image of this sphere, poised and calm: a hermaphrodite, holding both halves of the self in balance. Faint symbols and figures move across the walls like writing that keeps rearranging itself. This is Mercury's splendour, the mind's delight in order and pattern. Breathe in, and vibrate the God-name so that it resonates through the whole temple: Elohim Tzabaoth. Then call the archangel of Hod: Mikael. Feel a tall, bright presence gather in the orange light behind you. Mikael keeps both the way out and the way home.

steps.title: The Veil of Ayin
steps.text: A heavy curtain hangs in the wall that faces the heart of the Tree. It is painted with Atu XV of the Thoth deck: the great goat with spiralling horns and an eye in his forehead, standing on a mountaintop in front of a towering column. Stand before the curtain. With your finger or wand, trace the letter Ayin in the air in front of the painting, in a deep indigo light that glows against the fabric: ע. Vibrate its name slowly and feel it resonate in your chest: Ayin. The letter holds steady, and the painted goat seems to look back at you. The curtain grows thin, then parts. Mikael puts a small lit lamp in your hand. Step through, and let the curtain fall closed behind you.

steps.title: The Mountain Track
steps.text: You stand at the foot of a mountain in the last hour before full night. The sky is indigo, darkening to black at its edges, and the rock under your feet is a cold dark grey, almost black. The air is thin and sharp with frost, with a faint smell of musk. A narrow track zigzags upward between boulders. Your lamp throws a small warm circle ahead of you, enough for the next few steps and no more. Begin to climb. This is Capricorn, cardinal Earth ruled by Saturn. The going is slow and steady, and it asks for patience, not haste. Feel the effort in your thighs and knees, the grit shifting under your feet, your breath clouding in the lamplight. Every step lands on solid ground.

steps.title: Goat, Ass and Black Diamond
steps.text: Thistles grow in the cracks along the track, their purple heads closed against the cold. Among them you may notice other hardy plants: the ragged leaves of hemp, the pale root of an orchis pushing through thin soil. A laden ass comes plodding down the slope, patient under its load, and you step aside to let it pass. Higher up, goats move with perfect ease along ledges that look impossible, leaping from rock to rock. One stops and looks down at you. Hold its gaze. Its pupil is a flat horizontal bar, strange and steady. This is the Eye, the meaning of Ayin: seeing the world from an angle that is not your own. Where your lamplight touches a seam in the rock, something flashes. It is a black diamond set in the stone, dark and full of fire. Look at it for as long as you need.

steps.title: The Lord of the Gates of Matter
steps.text: The track brings you out onto the summit. On the highest rock stands the figure of the trump: a great Himalayan goat, his horns turning in slow spirals, a third eye open in the middle of his forehead. He is grinning, but the grin is not cruel. It is the pleasure of a creature as much at home on barren stone as in any green valley. Behind him a huge column rises from the mountain into the sky. At its root, two translucent globes hold small figures that stir and press against the walls, like seeds about to break open. In front of him rises a wand topped with a winged disc and twin serpents. The Sepher Yetzirah names this path the Renovating Intelligence. Breathe the thin, clear air and let it renew you. Stand in the presence of this force and simply watch.

steps.title: Pan
steps.text: Near the summit, in the shelter of a boulder, someone is waiting: a figure with the horns and legs of a goat and the body and face of a man. This is Pan, whose name the Greeks heard as 'All'. He may be playing a reed pipe, or just sitting with his arms around his knees, watching you with amusement. Greet him politely, and ask him plainly what this path has to teach you. Then wait. He may answer in words, with a gesture or a sound, with laughter, or by showing you something. He may give you a symbol or a single word. Take whatever comes without judging it, and don't decide yet what it means. If nothing seems to come, that is also an answer. Stay with him in the silence.

steps.title: The Threshold of Tiphareth
steps.text: When the exchange feels complete, Pan points onward. Past the summit the path narrows to a ridge, and at its end the dark gives way to a wash of rose and gold, as if dawn were breaking from inside the rock. Walk to the edge of that light and stop. Across a shimmering veil, the Veil of Paroketh, you see a six-sided temple of gold, bright as the midday sun. Inside it you may make out the shapes of a king, a child, a god offered up. Feel the warmth on your face and smell the frankincense drifting toward you. Do not cross. This is Tiphareth, Beauty, the heart of the Tree. It is enough to know it is there and that this path leads to it. Let the light print itself on you, then lower your eyes.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Turn and retrace your steps. Cross back over the summit, bowing your head in thanks to Pan and the great goat as you go. Go down the zigzag track by the light of your lamp, past the goats on their ledges, the black diamond in the rock, the thistles closed against the cold. Going down is quicker and lighter than the climb. At the foot of the mountain the painted curtain is waiting. Pass through it into the orange temple of Hod. Turn back and trace the letter Ayin once more in indigo over the curtain, then watch the letter fade and the curtain become solid wall. Give the lamp back to Mikael and thank the archangel for guarding the way. Stand for a moment in the warm splendour of the eight-sided temple.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Let the temple of Hod grow faint, its orange walls fading into your ordinary awareness of the room. Feel your body again: the weight of your seat, the soles of your feet on the floor, the air on your hands and face. Take three deeper, fuller breaths, each one bringing you further back. Listen to the sounds of the room and the world outside it. Wriggle your fingers and toes and roll your shoulders. When you are ready, open your eyes. Look around and name a few ordinary objects to yourself. Before you do anything else, stamp your feet firmly on the ground and sit quietly a moment longer. You have returned.
