closing: Close with a banishing: the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or the Star Ruby. Stamp your feet, wash your hands and face in cool water, and eat and drink something simple and grounding, like bread and a warm drink. Then write up the journey straight away: date, time, planetary hour, incense, what you saw, the word or symbol Pan gave you, bodily sensations and mood. Check the record against the symbol list below. Note which correspondences appeared without prompting, which did not, and anything that contradicted them. Come back to the entry after a few days and add anything that has surfaced since in dreams or daily life.

tunnel.reflection: On the averse side the Eye stops looking upward. Matter is taken as the whole, the goat has no eye above its horns, and the chain is mistaken for the body. Consider where a fixed appearance has become a prison in your own life, and where laughter has soured into contempt. Hold this as quiet reflection from ordinary waking awareness, not as invocation, and only after you have worked the day-side path of Ayin and written up what it taught you.

notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth scheme: Ayin, Capricorn, Atu XV The Devil, joining Hod (8) to Tiphareth (6). The Liber AL I:57 He/Tzaddi (Star/Emperor) exchange does not affect this path; the Golden Dawn and the Thoth deck agree on it. Corrections to the digest: (1) Hod's God-name was given as אלהים בצאות, with letters transposed. It is corrected to אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (2) Hod's Heaven was given as כובכ and is corrected to כוכב, Kokab. Archangels follow the Golden Dawn / 777 order (Mikael in Hod, Raphael in Tiphareth). Some modern writers swap these two; if your lineage does, change the archangel in step 2. Temples use the Queen scale (Hod orange, Tiphareth gold), and the letter is traced in the path's King-scale indigo. 'Khem' is the older reading of Min, the ithyphallic god of Koptos, which 777 pairs with Set. The path crosses the Veil of Paroketh, so Tiphareth is glimpsed but not entered. The digest's 'keyword' and 'meditation' lines are the app's own editorial synthesis, and the script does not present them as tradition. The goat's horizontal pupil and the lamp handed over at the veil are working images, not traditional doctrine. The tunnel genius A'ano'nin follows Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden (Liber 231). Musk and civet in 777 are animal-derived, so synthetic substitutes are recommended.

title: The Path of the Lightning and the Mouth
summary: Path 27 is the lowest of the Tree's three horizontal paths. It crosses from Hod, the sphere of Mercury and ordered thought, to Netzach, the sphere of Venus and feeling, and carries Pe, the mouth, with Mars and Atu XVI The Tower. Working it builds the courage to let rigid structures of mind break under a greater force, and to meet that breaking as release rather than catastrophe.

prepare.incense: Dragon's blood resin (777 col. XLII, Mars row: 'Pepper, Dragon's Blood, all Hot Pungent Odours'). Burn a few grains of storax first to open the temple of Hod. Do not burn pepper indoors, because the smoke irritates the lungs; set a small dish of whole peppercorns on the altar instead.
prepare.candle: A scarlet candle (King scale of Pe / Mars, 777 col. XV). You can put an orange cloth (Queen scale of Hod, the starting temple) under it.
prepare.stone: Ruby, or any red stone such as garnet or red jasper (777 col. XL).
prepare.facing: East, as in ordinary temple work. South, the quarter of fire, is a fitting alternative for Mars.
prepare.notes: Tuesday (Mars) is the traditional day; Wednesday (Mercury) also suits the start in Hod. A sword or dagger on the altar fits this path (777 col. XLI, The Sword) but is not required. This path can stir up strong feeling, so work it when you are rested and not already upset, and keep your journal ready.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a straight-backed chair with your feet flat on the floor and your hands resting palm-down on your thighs. Let your spine lengthen and your chin drop slightly. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: breathe in for four slow counts, hold for four, breathe out for four, hold empty for four. After a few rounds, use each out-breath to release tension from one part of the body at a time: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, arms, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet. Watch especially for clenching in the jaw and fists, and let it go. When the body feels settled and heavy, stop counting and let the breath find its own rhythm. Rest there for a while, awake and still.

steps.title: The Temple of Hod
steps.text: An eight-sided temple forms around you. Its walls are a clear, warm orange, and the light is bright and even, like afternoon sun through amber glass. The floor is polished stone laid in a precise geometric pattern. The air is sweet and faintly balsamic with storax. At the centre stands a double-cube altar draped in orange, with a single flame on it and beside it a caduceus, the sign of Mercury, whose sphere this is. Near the altar stands the image of Hod: a hermaphrodite, poised and composed, both and neither. Take your place before the altar, facing east. Breathe deeply and vibrate the divine name of this sphere so that the eight walls ring with it: Elohim Tzabaoth.

steps.title: Calling Mikael
steps.text: Call on the archangel of Hod: 'Mikael, archangel of this sphere, be present and protect this working.' The orange light behind the altar gathers and brightens until a tall presence stands there, armoured or robed, with a clear and searching quality like light off polished metal. Around the walls you may sense the Beni Elohim, the Sons of the Gods and the choir of this sphere, as a quick shimmer at the edges of your vision. Tell Mikael that you mean to walk the path of Pe across to Netzach and to return by the same road. Wait until you feel you have been heard. Then look to the wall on your right, where a curtain hangs, glowing deep scarlet.

steps.title: The Veil of Pe
steps.text: Walk to the curtain. It is painted with Atu XVI, The Tower, in Crowley and Harris's design. A rigid tower breaks apart under a forked bolt, flames burst from gaping jaws at its base, stiff geometric figures tumble from its walls, and a single radiant eye looks down over it all. Hold the image until it is vivid. Then, with the index finger of your right hand, trace the letter Pe, פ, on the curtain in brilliant scarlet, the King-scale colour of this path. Let it burn there, bright as a live coal. Breathe in fully and vibrate the name of the letter: Pe (peh). The sound seems to strike the curtain like a blow, and it splits open from top to bottom. Step through, and feel it close behind you.

steps.title: The Red Plain
steps.text: You stand at the edge of a wide plain under a heavy, low sky. The light is scarlet, and the earth under your feet is red, dense and faintly springy, as though the ground itself were muscle. The air is hot and carries a peppery, resinous sharpness you can taste at the back of your throat. Behind you the orange light of Hod glows faintly; far across the plain a green gleam marks where the road ends. Clumps of bitter grey-green absinthe and rue grow along the way. Begin to walk. Feel your own strength in each step as the muscles of your legs, back and arms work together. This is the Exciting Intelligence, the path by which every created thing receives its spirit and its motion. Let that energy rise in you, steady and warm, without urgency.

steps.title: The Creatures of Mars
steps.text: As you walk, the plain comes alive. A red-brown horse gallops past in the distance, gleaming, then wheels away. On a low ridge a bear rears up, drops, and ambles on. At the edge of your sight a grey wolf keeps pace with you, silent, neither threatening nor friendly. Somewhere in the scrub a boar crashes through the undergrowth. Let each creature be exactly as it appears, and notice your own response to it: fear, excitement, admiration, calm. Midway across the plain another road crosses yours at right angles, running from the lunar lowlands up toward a golden height. This is the path of Samekh. You do not turn onto it. Ahead, rising out of the flat land, you now see a tall, angular building. It is the Tower.

steps.title: The Lightning
steps.text: Stop at a safe distance and watch. The tower is severe and angular, built of hard, square-cut blocks, its walls without ornament. Above it, in the darkening sky, an immense eye opens, rayed with light. In that instant forked lightning strikes the summit. The structure splits and blocks shear away. Stiff geometric figures, more like broken diagrams than people, tumble from its walls. At its base great jaws gape and breathe out fire. Through the smoke a white dove flies with an olive sprig in its beak, and near it a lion-headed serpent coils in the air; Crowley read the two as two forms of desire. You are not harmed. Watch until the tower is down. Then quietly ask yourself what in you resembles that tower, and simply notice what comes.

steps.title: The Falcon-Headed Warrior
steps.text: Where the tower stood, the air begins to clear. Out of the settling dust walks a warrior with the head of a falcon. He may be Horus in his martial aspect, whom 777 gives to this path, or Menthu, the war-god of Thebes, crowned with tall plumes and a disc; accept whichever form appears. He carries a sword, and his presence is hot, direct and unhurried. Salute him in your own way. Tell him you have come from Hod by the path of Pe, and ask: what does this path have to teach me? Then be still and wait. The answer may come as a spoken word, a gesture, an image, a sensation in the body, or something placed in your hands. Receive it as it is, without editing it. Take all the time you need, and when it feels complete, thank him.

steps.title: The Threshold of Netzach
steps.text: Walk on across the last of the plain. The scarlet light cools and softens, and green enters it. Grass grows under your feet, and the peppery air gives way to the scent of roses and red sandalwood. You come to a threshold and stop. Beyond it stands a seven-sided temple of glowing emerald, its outline lit amber, and above it the planet Venus shines clear. Through the open door you may glimpse the image of this sphere, a beautiful naked woman, and faintly hear the name YHVH Tzabaoth. Do not cross. Stand at the edge and feel the contrast between the road of breaking behind you and the beauty before you. Let the vision of Victory rest in you for a few breaths.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Turn and walk back across the plain the way you came. Pass the place where the tower stood; see what remains there now, and note it without stopping. Salute the falcon-headed warrior if he is still present. Cross the road of Samekh again, and pass the horse, the watchful wolf, the absinthe and rue. The light deepens to scarlet, and then the orange glow of Hod appears ahead. The curtain stands before you; step through into the eight-sided temple. Turn and see the letter Pe still burning on the curtain. Trace it in reverse, or draw your hand down through it, and watch the scarlet fade until the curtain hangs plain and closed. Face the altar and thank Mikael for his protection. Vibrate once more: Elohim Tzabaoth.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Let the temple of Hod fade. The orange walls, the altar flame and the patterned floor dissolve like a picture in dimming light. Feel your body in the chair again: the weight of your hips, your feet on the floor, your hands on your thighs. Take three fuller breaths, and with each one feel your body grow more solid and present. Listen to the ordinary sounds of the room. Press your feet firmly into the floor, open and close your hands, and stretch your arms. When you are ready, open your eyes and look slowly around at familiar things. Say your name aloud. Sit for a moment longer, then write down everything you experienced, starting with whatever the warrior gave you.

closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby, and stamp your foot firmly three times. Because this is a Mars path, work off any leftover energy physically before you sit quietly: a brisk walk, some stretching, or some honest physical work. Eat something substantial and drink water. Record the session at once: the date, time, planetary day and hour, what you saw at the tower, the guide's form and gift, and any emotions it stirred. Check your record against the symbols list only afterwards. If agitation lingers over the following days, don't repeat the path until it settles.

tunnel.reflection: The averse face of Pe is destruction that clears nothing: force spent for its own sake, the tower left as rubble with no new sight in its place, and a mouth that speaks only to wound. Consider how the same lightning that frees can, without the opened eye behind it, become mere rage or a habit of tearing things down. Look honestly at where anger or harsh speech in your own life breaks things without renewing them. Work the day-side path of the Tower first, until you know its shattering as release, and treat Parfaxitas as a theme for reflection and journal work, not a force to call.

notes: ATTRIBUTION: Pe, פה (mouth), value 80 (final ף = 800); Mars; Atu XVI, called The Tower in the Thoth deck and The House of God in the Golden Dawn and 777. Its Golden Dawn title is 'The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty'. The Thoth swap does not affect this path. Sepher Yetzirah: the 27th path, the Exciting (or Active) Intelligence. Path 27 crosses path 25 (Samekh, Yesod-Tiphareth) on the Middle Pillar, between Yesod and Tiphareth, which is why the journey passes a crossing road. DATA CORRECTIONS: (1) The digest gave Hod's God-name as 'אלהים בצאות', with letters transposed; the correct spelling is אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (2) The Heavens of Hod appeared as 'כובכ'; the correct form is כוכב, Kokab (Mercury). (3) 777 gives the Empress-scale colour of Pe as 'bright red, rayed azure or emerald', not 'azure or orange'. (4) The trump-title field ran on into the Star's title ('The Daughter of the Firmament...'), apparently from a shifted row; the Tower's title is only 'The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty'. ARCHANGEL: Mikael for Hod follows the Golden Dawn / 777 order used in this series; some writers swap Mikael and Raphael between Hod and Tiphareth. GUIDE: The falcon-headed guide draws on 777 cols. XIX (Horus) and XX (Menthu); Ares or Mars (cols. XXXIV-XXXV) may appear instead, and you can record whichever form you meet. The remark that the dove and the lion-headed serpent are 'two forms of desire' reports Crowley's reading of the Thoth card; it is not presented as independent tradition.

title: The Path of the Hook and the Throne
summary: Path 28 joins Yesod, the lunar foundation, to Netzach, the sphere of Venus. In Crowley's Thoth attribution it carries Tzaddi, the fish-hook, with Atu IV The Emperor and Aries, the first fire of the zodiac. Working it builds initiative and self-rule: the power to draw the loose tides of imagination up into a clear, living will.

prepare.incense: Dragon's blood resin (777 col. XLII, Aries row 15; the Thoth swap brings Aries' correspondences to Tzaddi). You can burn a little jasmine first to open the lunar temple of Yesod. Golden Dawn users would burn galbanum (Aquarius) here instead.
prepare.candle: A scarlet candle (King scale of Aries, 777 col. XV, row 15, which the Thoth swap brings to Tzaddi) on a violet cloth (Queen scale of Yesod, the starting temple). Golden Dawn alternative: violet, the King scale of Aquarius.
prepare.stone: Ruby (777 col. XL, Aries row). A garnet or other clear red stone will do if you have no ruby.
prepare.facing: East, toward sunrise. This suits Aries, the sign of the spring equinox and of the Sun's exaltation.
prepare.notes: This working is especially apt with the Sun in Aries (around the spring equinox and the Thelemic Equinox of the Gods), on a Tuesday (Mars rules Aries), or on a Monday for the start in Yesod. Keep your journal and pen within reach, and make sure you will not be disturbed for about 30 minutes.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair with your feet flat on the floor, your hands resting on your thighs and your spine tall without strain. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for a count of four, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep the count slow and even. With each out-breath, let one part of the body soften in turn: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs, the feet. Notice the weight of your body resting on the chair and the floor. When thoughts arrive, let them drift across your attention and return to the count. Continue until the breath runs on by itself and the body feels heavy, warm and still. Then let the counting fall away and simply rest in the quiet.

steps.title: The Temple of Yesod
steps.text: Around you a temple takes shape. It has nine walls of deep, glowing violet, a floor dark and smooth as still water, and cool air sweet with jasmine. Through an opening in the roof a crescent Moon hangs silver in an indigo sky. Its light pools on a double-cube altar at the centre, draped in violet, with a single flame burning on it. Beside the altar stands the image of this sphere: a beautiful naked man, very strong, still as a statue and yet plainly alive. Take your place before the altar, facing east. Draw a full breath and vibrate the divine name of Yesod so that it rolls outward and fills the whole temple: Shaddai El Chai. Feel the nine walls take up the sound and hold it.

steps.title: Calling Gabriel
steps.text: Call on the archangel of this sphere, aloud or in your mind: 'Gabriel, archangel of Yesod, be present and guard this working.' Behind the altar the violet light gathers and brightens until a tall figure stands there, robed in silver and violet, bringing the cool smell of night air over water. You need not see a face clearly. Feel the presence as calm, watchful and steady. At the corners of your sight you may sense the Kerubim, the angelic choir of this sphere, as a soft stirring of wings. Tell Gabriel that you mean to walk the path of Tzaddi toward Netzach and to return by the same road. Wait until you feel the request has been received. Then look to the wall ahead and to your right, where a curtain glows scarlet.

steps.title: The Veil of Tzaddi
steps.text: Walk to the curtain. It is painted with Atu IV, The Emperor, as Crowley and Harris made it: a crowned king enthroned in blazing red and orange, the pillars of his throne topped with the heads of wild mountain rams, a sceptre in one hand and an orb in the other. Study it until the image is sharp. Then raise your right hand and, with the index finger, trace the letter Tzaddi, צ, on the curtain in brilliant scarlet light, the King-scale colour of Aries. See it hang and burn in front of the painted king. Breathe in and vibrate the letter's name: Tzaddi (tsah-DEE). The letter flares, and the curtain parts down its centre. Step through, and feel it fall closed behind you.

steps.title: The Scarlet Country
steps.text: You stand on a rising road at the first edge of dawn. The light is scarlet. It deepens to red in the hollows and flares to bright flame wherever it touches the tops of the stones. The air is cold and clean, the air of early spring, and a wind from ahead carries the sharp resin of dragon's blood. Behind and below you, the violet dusk of Yesod lies like a quiet lake. The road climbs and curves toward a distant glow of green. Walk slowly. Feel the ground under your feet: hard reddish rock, veined with iron. Everything here seems newly begun, as though the land were made this morning. This is the Natural Intelligence, through which everything beneath the Sun is brought to its full nature. Let yourself feel that quickening.

steps.title: The Ram, the Owl and the Hook
steps.text: A clear, fast stream runs beside the road, flowing down toward the lunar waters behind you. Tiger lilies grow along its banks, orange-red and speckled, among low clumps of scarlet geranium. On a ledge above, a wild ram stands against the brightening sky with heavy, curled horns, watching you without fear. Farther on, an owl sits in a bare tree, still awake at the end of its night. Notice how each creature looks at you, and how you feel under its gaze. Then look down into the stream. Something glints there: a hook of bright metal, curved like the letter you traced. Consider it without hurry. A hook reaches into the water and draws up what lives there. Notice what the road itself seems to be doing as it curves upward from the waters, and let any understanding come in its own time.

steps.title: The Throne of the Emperor
steps.text: The road levels onto a high plateau. There, with the rising Sun at its back, stands a throne whose two pillars are crowned with the carved heads of Himalayan rams. On it sits the Emperor, crowned and robed in red and gold. Look at the shape he makes. His head and arms form a triangle pointing upward, and his crossed legs form a cross beneath it: the alchemical sign of sulphur. In one hand he holds a sceptre topped with a ram's head. In the other he holds an orb with a cross on top. A shield leans against the throne, bearing a double-headed eagle and a red disc. At his feet a lamb lies quietly beside a banner. Behind him the Sun clears the horizon. Take in the whole scene, and feel the steady heat that comes from it.

steps.title: The Emperor's Answer
steps.text: Approach the throne and stop at a respectful distance. Greet the Emperor in your own words, and give a sign of greeting if you use one. Tell him you have come up from Yesod by the path of Tzaddi, and ask him plainly: what does this path have to teach me? Then fall quiet and wait. He may speak, show you something, place an object in your hand, or simply look at you. The answer may arrive as a word, an image, a feeling or a memory. Receive whatever comes without judging or editing it, and do not hurry to interpret it. If nothing seems to happen, rest in the silence; that is worth recording too. When the exchange feels complete, thank him, and ask his leave to look toward the end of the road.

steps.title: The Threshold of Netzach
steps.text: Walk on past the throne. The road climbs one last short rise, and the scarlet light softens and mingles with green. At the crest you reach a threshold and stop. Before you, a little way off, stands a seven-sided temple glowing emerald, its edges touched with amber. The scent of roses drifts toward you. Low in the paling sky above it burns Venus, the morning star, brighter than anything around her. Through the open doorway you may glimpse the image of this sphere, a beautiful naked woman, and hear the name YHVH Tzabaoth sounding faintly from within. Do not enter; this is as far as today's journey goes. Simply look, breathe the rose-scented air, and let the sight of Victory settle into you.

steps.title: The Return
steps.text: Turn and walk back down the road the way you came. Bow to the Emperor as you pass the throne. Pass the owl in its tree, the ram on its ledge, and the lilies and geraniums by the stream with its bright hook. The scarlet deepens toward red, and below you the violet of Yesod widens. Soon the curtain hangs before you, with the painted Emperor now seen from behind, glowing faintly. Step through into the temple of Yesod. Turn and see the letter Tzaddi still burning on the curtain. Trace it once in reverse, or draw your hand down through it, and watch the scarlet fade until the curtain hangs plain and closed. Face the altar and thank Gabriel for guarding your way. Vibrate once more: Shaddai El Chai.

steps.title: Grounding
steps.text: Let the temple of Yesod grow dim: the violet walls, the altar flame, the Moon above. Let it fade like a room at dusk until only you remain. Become aware of your body in the chair again: its weight, the pressure of your feet on the floor, your hands on your thighs. Take a deeper breath and listen to the sounds of the room around you. Wriggle your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and gently turn your head. When you are ready, open your eyes and rest them on something solid and ordinary. Say your name quietly aloud. Before you move on to anything else, take up your journal and write down everything you remember, above all what the Emperor gave you.

closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby, then stamp the floor three times to seal. Eat and drink something simple (bread, fruit, water) and wash your hands and face. Write your journal record at once: the date, time, Moon phase and the Sun's sign, what appeared on the path, anything that didn't match what you expected, and the Emperor's word or symbol exactly as it came. Compare it with the symbols checklist only after writing. Note whether the images matched the Aries (Thoth) set or the Aquarius (Golden Dawn) set; that tells you something about which attribution your own imagery follows.

tunnel.reflection: In its averse aspect, the path of Tzaddi shows authority cut off from the life it was meant to serve: rule that feeds only itself, a hook that catches and holds but never draws anything up into the light. Without calling on anything, contemplate where your own will has hardened into mere control, or where a rigid inner law keeps your imagination captive. Work the day-side path of the Emperor several times, until you know it well, before taking up this reflection. Treat the tunnel as a subject for meditation and journal study, not as an invocation.

notes: ATTRIBUTION: Crowley's Thoth swap (Liber AL I:57, 'but צ is not the Star', i.e. Tzaddi; explained in The Book of Thoth) gives Tzaddi to Atu IV The Emperor and He to Atu XVII The Star. The paths follow their letters, so in the Thoth system path 28 (Tzaddi, Netzach-Yesod) carries The Emperor / Aries, and path 15 (He, Chokmah-Tiphareth) carries The Star / Aquarius. In the Golden Dawn attribution, and in the rows of 777 as printed, path 28 is Atu XVII The Star / Aquarius, titled 'Daughter of the Firmament, Dweller between the Waters'. DATA CORRECTIONS: The digest lists the Golden Dawn / Aquarius set for this path: The Star, Atu XVII; Aquarius; King scale violet, Queen sky blue, Emperor bluish mauve, Empress white tinged purple; galbanum; man or eagle and peacock; olive and coconut; artificial glass; Ahephi, Aroueris and Nuit; Athena and Ganymede; Juno; Astrology. Under the Thoth swap the sign's correspondences go with the trump, so this journey uses 777's Aries row (row 15) instead: King scale scarlet, Queen red, Emperor brilliant flame, Empress glowing red; ram and owl; tiger lily and geranium; ruby; dragon's blood; the horns, energy and burin; Men Thu, Athena, Mars/Minerva, Shiva; the power of consecrating things; head and face. The digest's trump title ('Dweller between the Waters') and trump design ('a water-nymph') belong to the Star; the Emperor's Golden Dawn title is 'Sun of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty'. The digest's magical-weapons field ('The Censer or Aspergillus The Twilight of the Place and Magic') appears to merge two rows. Some things stay with the path whichever attribution you use: the letter Tzaddi צדי (fish-hook), value 90 (final ץ = 900), its position between Netzach and Yesod, and the 28th Sepher Yetzirah path, the Natural Intelligence. The digest spells Haniel האניאל; the usual spelling is הניאל. The tunnel digest pairs Tzuflifu with the Emperor / Aries (Crowley/Grant) and gives the Golden Dawn Star / Aquarius as the alternative. VARIANT: If you keep path colours with the letter rather than the sign, trace Tzaddi in violet instead of scarlet. Nothing else in the working needs to change.

title: The Path Between the Towers
summary: Path 29 runs from Malkuth, the Kingdom of the physical world, to Netzach, the Victory of feeling and desire. It is governed by Qoph (the back of the head), Pisces and Atu XVIII The Moon. It is the Corporeal Intelligence: the road through the body's instincts, fears and dreams, where the Sun travels unseen through the night before it rises. Working it builds the ability to walk through illusion and fear without running from it or believing it, and to trust the slow, patient life of the body.

prepare.incense: Ambergris (777 col. XLII). Real ambergris is rare; an ambergris-type blend or ambrette seed will do as a stand-in. Note the substitution in your record.
prepare.candle: A deep crimson candle (King scale, 'crimson, ultra violet') on a buff or stone-coloured cloth (Queen and Empress scales).
prepare.stone: Pearl (777 col. XL).
prepare.facing: West, the quarter of Water, since Pisces is mutable Water. In the vision the temple of Malkuth faces east, and the Qoph door is right of centre (south-east), with the Tree seen from the front.
prepare.notes: Best worked at night, and a waning moon suits it: Crowley's correct design for this trump is the waning moon. Work barefoot, because the path rules the legs and feet. A small hand mirror (the path's weapon) and a bowl of water can sit on the altar. Study Atu XVIII for a few minutes beforehand. This path stirs fear and glamour, so choose a time when you are rested and steady, and do not skip the banishing afterwards.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright with your bare feet flat on the floor. This path rules the legs and feet, so let them be felt. Rest your hands on your thighs. The crimson candle burns low, the room is dim, and a faint sweetness of ambergris hangs in the air. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold for four. Keep it slow and effortless. On each out-breath release a little more: forehead, jaw, throat, shoulders, belly, thighs, calves, the soles of the feet. Feel the body's weight drain down into the ground. When the rhythm runs by itself, let go of counting, and let the darkness behind your eyes become a space waiting to be entered.

steps.title: The Temple of Malkuth
steps.text: Build the temple of Malkuth around you. It is a square hall of solid stone, and its floor is divided into four quarters of citrine, olive, russet and black, the Queen-scale colours of the Kingdom. The walls are plain and sturdy, and a double-cube altar stands at the centre. The air smells of earth after rain and, faintly, of dittany. Beside the altar is the magical image of this sphere: a young woman, crowned and throned, calm and entirely present. Facing east, take a deep breath and vibrate the Divine Name: Adonai Melekh. Feel the stone answer through the soles of your feet. Then call the archangel Sandalphon, and sense a tall presence arrive beside you, rooted and patient, whose attention reaches down into the ground and up toward the heights at once.

steps.title: The Veil of Qoph
steps.text: There are three doors in the eastern wall. The one right of centre, toward the south-east, is hung with a curtain painted with Atu XVIII, The Moon: a waning crescent above, two dark towers, jackal-headed figures at the gate, and a beetle in the water below. Raise your hand and trace on the curtain the letter Qoph, ק, in lines of deep crimson light. It has a curved head-stroke, and beneath it a separate stem that drops below the line, like a skull and the spine hanging from it. As it glows, vibrate its name: Qoph. Feel the sound at the base of your skull. The curtain darkens and softens, like water seen from above at night. Sandalphon remains in the temple. Step through, and feel coolness close around you and then part.

steps.title: The Shore of Night
steps.text: You stand at the edge of dark water under a night sky. The light is a crimson so deep it seems almost beyond sight, the King-scale colour of this path. Where it thins, it turns buff flecked with silver, like moonlight on sand. The shore is wet, and your bare feet sink a little at each step. Mangroves stand with their roots in the tide. In the shallows a great beetle works with patient effort, rolling a disc of dim gold before it. This is Khephra, carrying the Sun beneath the water through the hours of night. Farther out a fish turns, and a dolphin's back curves briefly out of the sea and is gone. The air smells of salt, weed and sweet musk. A path of pale stone rises from the waterline and leads inland.

steps.title: Between the Towers
steps.text: Follow the path up from the shore. Ahead it passes between two dark towers, blank and windowless, standing like the posts of a gate. Above them hangs the waning Moon, and drops fall slowly from its lower edge, each shaped like a small Yod. Before each tower stands a tall figure with the head of a jackal, still as carved stone, and at their feet two jackals wait with lowered heads. Fear may come here: a tightening in the belly, a sense of something behind you, shapes at the edge of sight that shift between human and animal. Do not run, and do not argue with them. Keep walking at the same pace, breathing slowly. This is the Corporeal Intelligence, the old wisdom that shapes and grows every body and speaks in the language of instinct.

steps.title: The Moving Water
steps.text: Past the gate the path winds upward through low, silver-dark hills. Pale poppies grow along its edges, and a drowsiness rises from them; notice it and stay awake. A stream runs beside the path, and its water seems to move both ways at once, rising and falling like a slow tide. Kneel and look into it. The surface is a mirror, and the face that looks back may not be quite your own. Watch without judging. On the stream bed lies a pearl, grown layer by layer around a grain of grit. Take it up and hold it in the hollow of your hand. Pisces is the last sign of the zodiac, the sea in which forms dissolve and from which new ones come. Feel your body as a tide that has come and gone many times.

steps.title: The Guide of Souls
steps.text: One of the jackal-headed wardens has left the gate and now walks beside you. This is Anubis, whom the Greeks matched with Hermes, the guide of souls. He is tall and dark, his ears alert, his eyes steady and without malice. He knows this road in darkness as well as by day. Stop, face him, greet him, and ask what this path teaches. Then wait in silence. An answer may come as a word, a picture, a sensation in the body, a scent or an object offered to you. It may be something you do not yet understand. Do not supply the answer yourself or steer it toward what you hoped for. Receive it, and fix it in memory exactly as it comes. Stay here as long as you need.

steps.title: The Threshold of Netzach
steps.text: Thank Anubis. The path climbs a last rise and the night begins to thin. Ahead, where the sky pales, stands a seven-sided temple whose walls glow emerald, the Queen-scale colour of Netzach. Its doorway is wreathed with roses, and the scent of rose and benzoin reaches you on warmer air. Inside you may glimpse the image of this sphere, a beautiful naked woman, or only a shimmer of green and amber like dawn through leaves. This is Victory, the sphere of Venus. Venus is exalted in Pisces, so the dark road has been leading toward beauty all along. Do not enter. Stand at the edge of the light, let it touch your face, and remember what you see.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Turn and go back down the path. The emerald light fades behind you, and the poppies and the tidal stream slip past. The pearl stays with you, along with anything else you were given. Walk between the two towers again; the jackal-headed warden returns to his post and lets you pass. Go down to the shore, where Khephra still rolls the hidden Sun through the dark water. Ahead is the curtain, glowing faintly crimson. Step through into the stone temple of Malkuth and feel the four-coloured floor firm beneath you. Turn to the curtain and trace the letter Qoph once more, drawing it back into the painted veil until its crimson light fades and the trump is still. Then thank the archangel Sandalphon for guarding the Kingdom while you travelled.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Let the temple walls grow thin and fade until only the sense of solid ground remains, and then only the floor of your own room beneath your bare feet. Press your soles down firmly. Feel your calves, your knees, your thighs, and the weight of your body on the chair. Take three fuller breaths. Move your fingers and toes, stretch your legs, and roll your head gently to loosen the back of the neck, where Qoph sits. Listen to the ordinary sounds around you. When you are ready, open your eyes and look slowly around the room, naming a few plain objects. If you feel heavy or dreamy, stand up and stamp your feet. Come fully back before you start thinking about what you saw.

symbols.symbol: a waning moon letting fall Yod-shaped drops
two dark towers forming a gate
jackal-headed figures and jackals at the gate
a scarab rolling the sun through the water
Poseidon or Neptune; Hermes as guide of souls
phantoms or shapes shifting between human and animal
the back of the head; the legs and feet

closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or your usual banishing. This path works with illusion and glamour, so do not leave the banishing out. Put out the candle and switch on an ordinary light. Write the record at once, describing what you saw before you interpret it. Then test it against the symbol list and note what matched, what did not, and anything new. Eat something substantial, drink water, and wash your hands and face in cold water. Because this path touches the dreaming mind, give your dreams a line in the journal for the next few nights. Leave at least a day before working another path.

tunnel.reflection: The averse side of Qoph is the Moon's tide turned to nightmare. It is illusion taken for revelation, glamour that bewitches the one who casts it, fear rising from the oldest part of the brain, and a road that keeps doubling back on itself. Consider where you have been deceived by your own images, or where fear has quietly steered your choices while calling itself caution or intuition. Keep Qulielfi's tunnel as a subject for reflection and journal work, never as something to call up, and turn to it only after you have walked and recorded the day-side path of Qoph with a clear, banished mind.

notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth system and Liber 777: Qoph (value 100, 'back of the head'), Pisces, Atu XVIII The Moon, titled 'The Ruler of Flux and Reflux, the Child of the Sons of the Mighty', running from Malkuth to Netzach. Crowley's correct design for the trump is the waning moon. The He/Tzaddi exchange of paths 15 and 28 does not affect this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) Malkuth's Hebrew name was misspelt מלכור and is corrected to מלכות. (2) 777 gives Malkuth's magical image as 'a young woman, crowned and throned', not 'veiled'. (3) The col. V entry '(36) אלה' (Eloh) is the Sun's name, shifted from path 30, and is not used here. On the God-name: 777 gives Adonai Melekh (אדני מלך), while Golden Dawn practice often uses Adonai ha-Aretz (אדני הארץ). Vibrate whichever one you use in your own Malkuth work. 777 spells Haniel as האניאל; הניאל is the more usual spelling. Opium is one of 777's plants for this path; here it appears only as imagery. The double-bracketed perfume in the digest is left out of the practical preparation. Linking Pisces to Netzach through Venus's exaltation in Pisces is standard astrology used as imagery, not a 777 entry. Directions assume you see the Tree from the front while facing east, which puts Netzach on the right. Mirror them if you use the body convention.

title: The Path of the Unwalled Sky
summary: Path 30 joins Yesod, the Foundation of images and dreams, to Hod, the Splendour of mind and language. It runs under the letter Resh (the head or face), the Sun and Atu XIX The Sun. It is the Collecting Intelligence, where scattered impressions are gathered into ordered knowledge and the intellect is lit from above instead of by its own reflections. Working it builds clarity, honesty about what one actually knows, and a warm confidence that does not need to guard itself.

prepare.incense: Olibanum (frankincense) with a little cinnamon (777 col. XLII, 'all glorious odours').
prepare.candle: An orange candle (King scale, the path's own colour) on a gold-yellow cloth (Queen scale). A small violet light for Yesod is optional.
prepare.stone: Chrysolite (777 col. XL). The old name covers yellow-green stones such as peridot. If you have none, a clear sunny stone can stand in; note the substitution in your record.
prepare.facing: East, toward sunrise. In the vision the temple of Yesod also faces east, and the Resh door is in the left-hand (north-east) wall, with the Tree seen from the front.
prepare.notes: Best worked by day, ideally on a Sunday or in the Sun's planetary hour. Before you begin, spend a few minutes studying Atu XIX where you can see it. Keep your journal and pen within reach. A bay (laurel) leaf, sunflower seeds, or a small image of a lion or hawk can sit on the altar. Keep the room warm and well aired.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs. Let the orange candle and the frankincense stay at the edge of your attention. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Keep it easy, never strained. With each out-breath let one part of the body soften in turn: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the backs of the legs. Feel your weight settle downward while the spine stays light and tall. When the rhythm carries itself, let the counting fall away. The room grows quieter, and your attention turns inward, toward the space behind your closed eyes, which is ready to take shape.

steps.title: The Temple of Yesod
steps.text: Build the temple of Yesod around you. It is a nine-sided chamber whose walls glow a soft violet, the Queen-scale colour of the Foundation, and whose floor is cool and faintly silvered, like wet sand under moonlight. A crescent moon hangs in the violet dome above. The air smells of jasmine and of damp roots. At the centre stands an altar, and beside it, still as a statue yet breathing, is the magical image of this sphere: a beautiful naked man, very strong, standing on the foundation that holds up everything built above it. Face east. Draw a full breath and vibrate the Divine Name: Shaddai El Chai. Let it roll out through the nine walls. Then call the archangel Gabriel, and feel a presence gather at your side, cool as rain, attentive and calm.

steps.title: The Veil of Resh
steps.text: In the wall to your left as you face east, toward the north-east, hangs a curtain you had not noticed before. Painted on it is Atu XIX, The Sun: a great disc of light with twelve rays, a green hill beneath, and two winged children dancing there. Raise your hand and trace on the curtain the letter Resh, ר, in lines of clear orange light: a single stroke that runs level and then turns down, like a brow and the profile of a head. As it glows, vibrate its name: Resh. Feel the sound warm your chest. The curtain turns translucent, lit from behind as if by morning. Gabriel remains in the temple; this road you walk yourself. Step through the painted light and feel it pass over your face like the first sun on a cold day.

steps.title: The Road of the Sun
steps.text: You stand on a road of pale, packed earth that climbs gently ahead. The light here is orange, the King-scale colour of the path. Toward the horizon it deepens into rich amber, and overhead it brightens to gold. There are almost no shadows; the air itself seems lit. On both sides, fields of sunflowers hold their heavy faces toward a brightness further on that you cannot yet look at directly. Laurel grows along the verges, dark and glossy, giving off a sharp green smell when you brush it, and small purple heliotrope turns with the light. Beneath these scents you catch a faint trace of frankincense and cinnamon. Walk slowly. Feel warmth settle on your forehead and face, for Resh is the head, and let the light find whatever in you has been kept in shade.

steps.title: The Hill and the Children
steps.text: The road rises to a round green hill, and you see that a low wall runs around its base. The wall is well built and solid, but it encloses nothing overhead: above the hill the sky is completely open. On the summit two children are dancing, each with bright, patterned wings like a butterfly's. They are not performing for you; they are simply at play, and their play makes the whole hill feel lighter. Above them the Sun hangs vast and near, its twelve rays reaching out toward the ring of the zodiac, the twelve signs set around the sky like a slow wheel. This is the Lord of the Fire of the World. Stand by the wall and watch. Notice what in you wants to join the dance, and what holds back.

steps.title: The Lion, the Hawk and the Stone
steps.text: A lion walks out of the tall grass and lies down across the road ahead of you, unhurried, its mane catching the light like a second small sun. It does not threaten; it simply fills the way with its whole weight, and you walk around it with respect. A sparrowhawk circles overhead, then settles on a laurel branch and watches the ground with complete attention. In the dust at your feet lies a clear yellow-green stone, a chrysolite; pick it up and feel it warm in your palm. This is the Collecting Intelligence, where scattered things are gathered: the images of Yesod, the words of Hod, the patterns of the stars. Feel your own scattered thoughts drawing together, like sunlight brought to a single point through a lens.

steps.title: The Guide
steps.text: Where the road levels near the top of the rise, a figure waits in the full light. It has a man's body and a hawk's head, and above its brow rests the disc of the Sun, circled by a serpent. This is Ra, as the path's attributions give him. If a golden archer with a bow appears instead, that is Apollo, who also belongs to this road. Greet the figure in whatever way feels right, and ask plainly what this path teaches. Then be quiet. You may receive a word, an image, a gesture or something placed in your hand, or only a warmth you cannot name. Do not reach for an answer you expected. Let whatever comes, come, and hold it in memory exactly as it is. Take all the time you need.

steps.title: The Threshold of Hod
steps.text: Thank your guide. Beyond the hill the road runs on toward a building on the rise ahead: an eight-sided hall whose walls shine orange, the Queen-scale colour of Hod. Fine letters and numbers are cut into its surfaces, and they seem to rearrange themselves as you look. A trace of storax drifts down to you. Through the open doorway you may glimpse the poised figure of the Hermaphrodite, or only light moving over polished stone. This is Splendour, the sphere of Mercury, of language, number and measure. Do not go in. For today it is enough to see it from the end of the Sun's road and to know that the path you have walked arrives here. Let the image of the hall settle into memory.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Turn back the way you came. Walk down past the walled hill and the dancing children and past the lion resting in the grass, while the sparrowhawk watches you go. Carry whatever you were given. The orange light softens with each step, sliding toward amber and then toward a quiet violet as the road descends. Ahead is the curtain, seen now from its far side and glowing. Step through into the nine-sided temple of Yesod. Turn to face the veil and trace the letter Resh again, as though drawing it back into the curtain. Watch its orange light fade until only the painted trump remains, still and closed. Then turn to Gabriel, waiting beside the altar, and thank the archangel for keeping the Foundation while you travelled.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Let the temple of Yesod grow thin, its violet walls turning transparent, until only the sense of the altar remains, and then only your own body sitting in the room. Feel your feet on the floor and the chair beneath you. Take three breaths a little deeper than before. Move your fingers and toes, roll your shoulders, and notice the sounds around you, the temperature of the air and the scent of the incense. When you are ready, open your eyes and look at a few ordinary objects, naming them to yourself. Stamp your feet lightly or press your palms firmly together. Do not rush to interpret anything yet. First come fully back.

symbols.symbol: rich amber; amber rayed with red
a great sun with twelve rays and the ring of the zodiac
two winged children dancing on a green hill
a wall around the hill, open to the sky
bow and arrow, or a lamen
Ra, hawk-headed and crowned with the sun disc
a head or face lit from above
scattered things gathered into one sight; the patterns of the stars

closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or your usual banishing, then put out the candle. Write the record straight away: the date and time, and every image, word and sensation, including the guide's answer. Describe what happened before you interpret it. Afterwards, check the record against the symbol list and note what matched, what did not, and anything new. Eat something simple and drink water. Step out into daylight if you can. Leave at least a day before working another path.

tunnel.reflection: The averse side of Resh is the Sun as glare instead of light. It is brilliance that blinds rather than shows, vanity, false enlightenment, and a bright face with nothing behind it. Consider where in your own life you have mistaken being seen for seeing, or confidence for clarity. Keep Raflifu's tunnel as a subject for reflection and journal work, not as something to call up, and turn to it only after you have worked and recorded the day-side path of Resh.

notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth system and Liber 777: Resh (value 200, 'head'), the Sun, Atu XIX The Sun, titled 'The Lord of the Fire of the World', running from Yesod to Hod. The He/Tzaddi exchange of paths 15 and 28 does not affect this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) Hod's God-name was misspelt אלהים בצאות and is corrected to אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (2) Hod's heaven כובכ is corrected to כוכב, Kokab. (3) The 777 col. V entry seems shifted by one row. אלהים (Elohim) is the divine name of Fire and belongs to path 31. The Sun's name is אלה (Eloh, value 36, the number of cells in the 6x6 square of the Sun), which the digest places on path 29. (4) Several fields have path 31 (Fire / Atu XX, titled The Aeon in the Thoth deck) material mixed in, and it was not used here: 'The Angel or Last Judgement' in the Tarot field; Thoum-Aesh-Neith, Mau and Kabeshunt among the Egyptian gods; Agni and Yama among the Hindu deities (777 gives Surya for the Sun); and 'the Wand or Lamp, Pyramid of Fire' among the weapons (the Sun's are the Lamen or Bow and Arrow). Directions assume you see the Tree from the front while facing east, which puts Hod on the left. If you use the 'backed into the Tree' body convention, mirror them. The guide is Ra, following 777 cols. XIX-XX. Some Thelemites will meet Ra-Hoor-Khuit here; that is a personal reading, not the table's attribution.

title: The Path of the Primal Fire
summary: Path 31, Shin, joins Malkuth to Hod on the Pillar of Severity. It carries elemental Fire and, in its second attribution, Spirit. Crowley's Atu XX, The Aeon, replaces the old Judgement with the gods of the Stele of Revealing and marks the passing of one age into the next. Working it develops the ability to let the fire of spirit burn away stale forms in the self, so that resurrection is felt as renewal and not punishment, and it readies the mind for the clarity of Hod.

prepare.incense: Olibanum (frankincense), which 777 col. XLII gives with 'all fiery odours'. Dittany of Crete (Malkuth) may be burned briefly first to establish the temple.
prepare.candle: Glowing orange-scarlet candle (King scale, 777 col. XV) on a vermilion cloth (Queen scale, col. XVI).
prepare.stone: Fire opal (777 col. XL).
prepare.facing: South, the quarter of Fire in the Golden Dawn scheme. Face East instead if you keep a fixed temple orientation for all path work.
prepare.notes: A single steady flame on the altar is the natural focus. You may set red poppies, hibiscus or any scarlet flowers beside it, and a wand if you have one. Place the candle safely and never leave it unattended. Banish beforehand with the LBRP or the Star Ruby. Keep your record book open beside you. If you are working the paths in sequence, work path 32 (Tau) first.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright with your feet flat on the floor, hands on your thighs and spine tall. Close your eyes and take up the fourfold breath: in for four, hold for four, out for four, empty for four. Keep the count gentle. As you breathe, notice the warmth in your body: the heat of blood moving through you, the pulse at your wrists and throat, the steady circulation that 777 assigns to this path. With each out-breath let tension go from the brow, jaw, neck, shoulders, chest, belly, hips, legs and feet. Let your weight sink into the chair and the floor, and allow the room to recede. When your breath is slow and even and your attention rests quietly inside you, begin.

steps.title: The Temple of Malkuth
steps.text: You are standing in the temple of Malkuth. Underfoot is the chequered floor of black and white. Around you the walls hold the four Queen-scale colours of this sphere, citrine, olive, russet and black, like the quarters of a single circle. Today notice the russet especially, the colour of fire within earth. A black altar stands at the centre with a flame burning on it. Near it sits the young woman, crowned and throned, who is the image of the Kingdom. In the eastern wall hang three veils. Stand at the altar facing East and vibrate: Adonai Melekh. Feel the name resonate down through the floor. Then call: Sandalphon. The archangel's presence gathers, tall and quiet, as though the whole temple had drawn breath. Ask for guidance and protection on the path of Fire, and wait for the sense that it is granted.

steps.title: The Veil of Shin
steps.text: Go to the veil on the side of the Pillar of Severity, the one that leads toward Hod. On it is painted Atu XX, The Aeon. The star-bodied goddess Nuit arches across the top, with a winged globe of fire beneath her. Below them the hawk-headed god sits enthroned, and before him stands a translucent child with a finger at his lips. At the foot is the letter Shin, with human figures rising in its three flames. Raise your hand and trace the letter Shin, ש, in glowing orange-scarlet, feeling heat at your fingertips. Vibrate the name of the letter: Shin. The painted colours brighten until the curtain seems to burn without being consumed. Give the Sign of the Enterer and step through.

steps.title: The Land of Perpetual Fire
steps.text: You come out into heat and light. The sky here is a glowing orange-scarlet, like the heart of a forge, and the ground under your feet is warm red rock veined with vermilion. Where the light catches it, flecks of gold spark in the scarlet, and here and there you see a shimmer of crimson and emerald, as at the core of a flame. Low fires burn along the way with no fuel and no smoke, each one steady and unending. The air smells of frankincense. Between the fires grow red poppies and hibiscus, dark stands of nettle, and scarlet flowers of every kind. Feel the heat on your face and hands; it warms you but does not burn. Walk forward, and notice how your body answers the fire in your heartbeat, your blood and your breath.

steps.title: Sun, Moon, Salamander and Lion
steps.text: As you walk, look up. The sun and the moon cross the burning sky, each keeping its own course, neither overtaking the other. The Sepher Yetzirah calls this path the Perpetual Intelligence because it keeps the sun and moon in their ordered motions. Feel that order beneath all the heat around you. Now look down into the fires beside the road. Salamanders move within them, the elemental beings of Fire, quick, bright and curious. Watch them without reaching for them. Ahead of you a lion lies across the path. It is the Kerub of Fire, tawny and gold, its mane stirring in the rising heat. Stop before it, stand upright and still, and let it take your measure. When it rises and walks beside you, or moves aside, go on.

steps.title: The Old Judgement and the New Aeon
steps.text: The path opens onto a broad plain, and here you see the old image of this trump: rows of stone tombs under a dim sky, and a great angel raising a trumpet to wake the dead. It is the Judgement of the old tarot. As you watch, the angel's note sounds and the scene changes. The dim sky becomes the dark-blue body of Nuit, arched from horizon to horizon and strewn with stars. Beneath her a globe of fire opens its wings. The tombs are gone. In their place the letter Shin rises as a great triple flame, and from each of its three tongues a human figure lifts upward, as if being born rather than raised. Stand in the heat of it. Consider what in you is ready to wake, and what is ready to burn away.

steps.title: The Guide
steps.text: A figure comes toward you from the centre of the flame. It may be a hawk-headed god, crowned, clothed in scarlet and gold and bearing a wand: Horus, lord of this Aeon, as he sits enthroned on the Stele. He may instead come as the silent child with a finger to his lips, or something else entirely may come. Whoever approaches, test it: trace the letter Shin before it in orange-scarlet flame and vibrate the letter name. A true guide stands firm or grows brighter, and anything false wavers and fades. When you are satisfied, greet the figure with respect and ask what this path has to teach you. Then keep silent. Let the answer come in its own form and its own time: a word, an image, a sensation, a symbol placed in your hands, or nothing yet. Remain for as long as the meeting lasts.

steps.title: The Threshold of Hod
steps.text: When the meeting ends, the path climbs a little further and comes to a threshold. The fire thins here, and the scarlet light shades into a clear, bright orange, the Queen-scale colour of Hod. Through the opening you glimpse a hall of polished surfaces where light is reflected and multiplied, and where figures and letters seem to be written on the air itself. At its centre stands the magical image of Splendour: a hermaphrodite, poised and luminous. You may sense the name Elohim Tzabaoth sounding there, and the presence of the archangel Mikael. Do not cross. Take in the colour and the clarity, and notice how the fire behind you has prepared you for this light. Then bow and turn back.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Retrace the path. Cross the plain where the triple flame of Shin still burns. Pass the lion and the salamanders, the perpetual fires and the scarlet flowers, with the sun and moon still moving in their order overhead. Hold close whatever you received. Your guide may walk part of the way with you; thank it when you part. The veil appears before you, glowing from within. Step through into the temple of Malkuth. Turn and trace the letter Shin on the curtain once more. Then draw your hand downward and watch the scarlet fade from the painted trump; the way is closed. Give the Sign of Silence. Go to the altar, thank Sandalphon for guarding your journey, and feel the archangel's presence withdraw.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Let the temple fade around you, its colours sinking into ordinary darkness. Feel the chair beneath you and the floor under your feet. Notice the temperature of the room, which is probably cooler than the path you have just walked, and let your body settle into it. Take three deep breaths. Move your hands and feet, and stretch your neck and shoulders. Say your name aloud. Open your eyes, look slowly around, and name a few ordinary objects. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor. If you feel lightheaded or overheated, drink some water and rest both palms flat on the floor for a moment. Then record what you experienced before speaking to anyone or doing anything else.

closing: After stamping your feet, close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Put out the candle deliberately, with a snuffer if you have one, as a conscious act of ending the working. Drink cool water and eat something. Write the record at once: date, time, moon phase, planetary day and hour, your physical state, and everything seen, heard or received. Then go through the symbols checklist and note what matched and what did not. Treat unfamiliar images as material to research, not as authority.

tunnel.reflection: Liber 231 names Shalicu as the genius of the tunnel behind Shin. Its averse face is fire that only annihilates: judgement without mercy, and a hunger for apocalypse as an ending instead of a birth, burning down what could have been transformed. Consider where you are drawn toward that kind of destruction, of habits, of relationships or of yourself, and ask what renewal the day-side fire of the Aeon would offer in its place. Work the day-side path first, and hold this as reflection only, never as invocation.

notes: Dual attribution: Shin carries both Fire (path 31) and Spirit (31 bis). 777 gives Spirit its own row: King scale white merging into grey, Queen scale deep purple nearly black, Emperor scale the seven prismatic colours with violet outside, and Empress scale white, red, yellow, blue and black, with black outside. This journey works the Fire aspect, with the spiritual renewal of the Aeon as its theme. Trump: Crowley replaced the Golden Dawn's Atu XX Judgement (an angel with a trumpet and the dead rising) with The Aeon, drawn from the Stele of Revealing, to mark the Aeon of Horus. The 777 'correct design' entry still describes Israfel and the rising dead, and the journey shows the old image giving way to the new. The He/Tzaddi swap does not affect this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) the Hebrew spelling of Malkuth is 'מלכור' in the digest and should be מלכות. (2) Hod's God-name is misspelled 'אלהים בצאות'; it should be אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (3) The Heavens of Hod are misspelled 'כובכ'; they should be כוכב, Kokab. (4) The magical image of Malkuth is 'a young woman, crowned and throned', not 'veiled'. (5) The digest's col. V divine name for this path, '(15) יה (3) אב', matches the Saturn magic-square names (Ab = 3, Yah = 15). It appears to be a row shifted from path 32. The Golden Dawn elemental God-name of Fire is Elohim (אלהים). (6) The Hindu entry 'Surya (as ☉)' looks shifted from path 30 (the Sun). For this path 777 gives Agni (Tejas), the fire god, together with Yama, lord and judge of the dead; verify this against your edition. (7) In the grade column, Malkuth is 1°=10□, not 0°=0□. The digest's Hod grade of 3°=8□ Practicus is correct in both the Golden Dawn and the A∴A∴. The Hod temple details are kept to its standard attributions: orange (Queen scale), the hermaphrodite image, Elohim Tzabaoth, and Mikael.

title: The Path into the Night of Time
summary: Path 32, Tau, runs from Malkuth straight up the Middle Pillar to Yesod. It is attributed to Saturn and to Earth, and its trump is Atu XXI, The Universe. It is traditionally the first path worked upward. It trains the passage from bodily, sensory awareness into the astral Foundation and back again, and it teaches Saturn's lessons of patience, limit and form, with the finished world seen as a completion and not a prison.

prepare.incense: 777 col. XLII gives assafoetida, scammony, indigo and sulphur ('all evil odours'). These are unpleasant and impractical to burn indoors. Burn Dittany of Crete (Malkuth), myrrh (Binah, the Sephirah of Saturn) or storax (777's perfume for the Earth attribution) instead.
prepare.candle: Indigo candle (King scale, 777 col. XV) on a black cloth (Queen scale, col. XVI). A black candle is also acceptable.
prepare.stone: Onyx (777 col. XL). You can also place a small dish of salt on the altar for the Earth attribution (32 bis).
prepare.facing: East, toward the imagined veils of the Tree. North, the Golden Dawn quarter of Earth, also suits this path.
prepare.notes: Saturday or an hour of Saturn suits the path. Work in dim light. Tau is the usual first path in a pathworking sequence because it leaves Malkuth by the Middle Pillar. Banish beforehand with the LBRP or the Star Ruby. Keep your magical record open beside you so you can write immediately afterward.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit upright in a firm chair, feet flat, hands resting on your thighs, spine straight but not stiff. If you know the God-form of the seated Egyptian, take it. Close your eyes. Begin the fourfold breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for four, hold empty for four. Let the rhythm become even and unforced. With each exhalation release one region of the body: the jaw and brow, the shoulders, the hands, the belly, the legs, the soles of the feet. Notice the weight of your body resting on the chair, the chair resting on the floor, and the floor resting on the earth itself. This path begins in the body and in matter, so first let yourself be fully here. When the breath runs on its own, let the room grow dim and quiet around you.

steps.title: The Temple of Malkuth
steps.text: Around you a temple takes shape. The floor is a pavement of black and white squares, cool beneath your feet. The walls glow in the Queen-scale colours of Malkuth: citrine, olive, russet and black. Citrine is highest, toward the East before you, and black is deepest, down toward the ground. At the centre stands a double-cube altar draped in black, with a lamp burning above it and a small dish of salt beside it. In the eastern wall hang three veils. Near the altar sits the magical image of this sphere: a young woman, crowned and throned, calm and watchful. Stand at the altar, facing East, and vibrate the Divine Name: Adonai Melekh. Feel the syllables settle into the floor. Then call the archangel: Sandalphon. A tall presence gathers beyond the altar, robed in the colours of earth, and inclines its head. Ask Sandalphon's protection for your journey, and wait until you sense it given.

steps.title: The Veil of Tau
steps.text: Walk to the East. Of the three veils, go to the central one, which leads straight up the Middle Pillar. It is a heavy curtain, and on it is painted Atu XXI, The Universe: a naked dancer within a great ellipse of small rings, a serpent coiling about her, the four Kerubic heads at the corners, and at the foot the outline of a building of many chambers. Raise your hand and trace the letter Tau, ת, on the curtain in deep indigo light, its strokes glowing where your fingers pass. Vibrate the name of the letter: Tau. The painted figures deepen and seem to stir, and the curtain thins like smoke. Give the Sign of the Enterer, projecting yourself forward, and step through with Sandalphon's presence at your back.

steps.title: The Onyx Road
steps.text: You stand on a road that runs gently upward through the night. The sky is deep indigo, darkening toward the horizon to blue-black. The road beneath you is paved with onyx, bands of black and white laid in a slow, even rhythm. The air is cool and still. Dark trees grow on either side: yew and cypress and ancient ash, and in their shade the low leaves of nightshade and the pale cups of hellebore. Nothing here hurries, and your own steps slow to match the place. Overhead, seven lights move across the indigo. They are the seven planets, weaving and never colliding. This is the Administrative Intelligence of the Sepher Yetzirah, the path that directs the seven wandering stars and keeps each to its own course. Walk on, and watch them turn.

steps.title: The River and the Crocodile
steps.text: The road descends to a broad, slow river. Its water is black, faintly rayed with blue, as if the night sky had been poured out and gathered here. A low bridge of stone crosses it, though its far end fades into mist. At the water's edge a great crocodile lies motionless, its eyes just above the surface. It is the beast of Sebek and Mako, the gods 777 sets on this path. Do not hurry past it, and do not fear it. Stop and greet it with respect. It regards you for a long time, with the patience of something that has watched this river for ages. Notice what you feel under that gaze, whether it is heaviness, stillness, age or something else. When the crocodile sinks back or lets its eyes close, cross the bridge.

steps.title: The Dancer in the Ellipse
steps.text: Beyond the river the land opens into a wide plain beneath the turning planets, and ahead of you the trump comes alive. A vast ellipse of small rings stands upright in the air, seventy-two of them linked like a wreath. Within it a woman dances, naked, balanced and unhurried. A great serpent coils about her as she moves, and she turns its coils as easily as a dancer turns a ribbon, so that its spiral and her movement become one motion. At the four quarters around the ellipse you sense the Kerubim: bull, lion, eagle and human face. Far below her feet rises a vast building of many small rooms, each room one of the elements of matter. Stand here and feel that the dance, the serpent and the solid house are one thing: the finished world, sealed and still alive.

steps.title: The Guide
steps.text: The dance slows, and the dancer steps down out of the ellipse to stand before you. Something else may come instead, such as an aged, grey-bearded figure with a sickle, the god of time and limits whose planet rules this path. If so, let it come. Look carefully at whatever figure approaches, and test it: trace the Tau before it in indigo and vibrate the letter name again. A true guide of this path holds steady or grows clearer, and anything false fades or breaks apart. When you are satisfied, greet it and ask plainly what this path has to teach you. Then be silent. Let the answer come in its own form: a word, an image, a gesture, a feeling, or nothing at all. If you are offered a symbol, accept it and hold it. Stay with this meeting for as long as it lasts.

steps.title: The Threshold of Yesod
steps.text: When the meeting is complete, the road carries you a little further, to where it ends at a threshold. Before you rises a doorway filled with violet light, the Queen-scale colour of Yesod, silvered at its edges like moonlight on water. Through it you glimpse a hall of violet and silver, and at its centre the magical image of the Foundation: a beautiful naked man, very strong, standing as though he bears the weight of everything around him. Behind him you sense vast, slow movement, tides and pulses, the turning wheels of the world's hidden machinery. Far off the name Shaddai El Chai is sounding, and you may feel the presence of Gabriel. Do not cross. This is the edge of today's journey. Take in what you can, bow, and turn back.

steps.title: Return
steps.text: Walk back the way you came. Your guide may go with you to the edge of the plain or leave you there; thank it either way. Pass the ellipse, now still, and cross the bridge over the black-blue river. Follow the onyx road down between the yews and cypresses, with the seven planets turning above you. Hold close whatever you were given. At the end of the road the veil hangs before you, and you see the painted trump from its reverse side. Step through into the temple of Malkuth. Turn to face the veil and trace the letter Tau on it once more. Then draw your hand downward and watch the indigo fade from the curtain; the passage is closed. Give the Sign of Silence. Return to the altar, thank Sandalphon for guarding your way, and feel the presence withdraw.

steps.title: Ground
steps.text: Let the temple of Malkuth grow faint around you, its colours sinking into the ordinary darkness behind your eyelids. Feel the chair again, the weight of your body, the floor under your feet, and the air on your hands and face. Take three breaths fuller than before. Move your fingers and toes, and roll your shoulders. Say your own name quietly aloud. When you are ready, open your eyes, look around the room, and name a few ordinary things you see. Stamp your feet firmly on the floor two or three times, and know that you are fully back. Before doing anything else, write down what you saw and what you received.

closing: Once you have stamped your feet and are fully back, close the working with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Eat something plain and earthy (bread with a little salt suits this path) and drink water. Write your record at once: date, time, moon phase, planetary day and hour, how your body felt, and everything you saw, heard or received, however small. Then go through the symbols checklist and note what matched. Treat anything that appeared but is not in the correspondences as a question to research, not a revelation to accept.

tunnel.reflection: Liber 231 names Thantifaxath as the genius of the tunnel behind Tau. Its averse face is matter felt as a tomb: form as nothing but imprisonment, time as nothing but loss, and the finished world as a dead end where there should be a dance. Notice where that mood lives in you, in routines that have hardened or in a body felt only as a burden, and set the day-side image of the dancing maiden against it. Work the day-side path until it is familiar before you turn to its shadow, and hold this only as a meditation, never as a call to the genius.

notes: Dual attribution: Tau carries both Saturn (path 32) and Earth (32 bis), and 777 gives Earth its own row. That row has a King scale of citrine, olive, russet and black, a Queen scale of amber, the stone salt, and the divine name Adonai ha-Aretz (אדני הארץ). The digest's col. V entry for this path, '[הארץ]אדני', is that Earth name. This journey works the Saturnian path, and Earth is present through the Malkuth temple and the dish of salt. You may vibrate Adonai ha-Aretz in place of Adonai Melekh; both are standard names of Malkuth. Atu XXI is 'The Universe' in both the Golden Dawn and Thoth decks, so the He/Tzaddi swap does not affect this path. The descriptions of the trump are drawn from Crowley's Thoth design: the dancing maiden with the serpent, the ellipse of 72 circles, the Kerubim, and the house of the elements at the base. Corrections to the digest: (1) the Hebrew spelling of Malkuth is 'מלכור' in the digest and should be מלכות. (2) The magical image of Malkuth in 777 and Golden Dawn is 'a young woman, crowned and throned', not 'veiled'. (3) The grade column appears shifted. Malkuth is 1°=10□ (Zelator in the Golden Dawn, Neophyte in the A∴A∴), 0°=0□ lies outside the Tree, and Yesod is 2°=9□ alone. (4) The Saturn divine names from the magic square, Ab (אב, 3) and Yah (יה, 15), appear in the digest under path 31. They belong with this path's Saturn attribution. The 777 'evil odours' incense is listed for completeness but substitutes are recommended.
